article.articleHeadline: Kongossa jo yli 5 000 ebolatapausta - lähes puolet on kuollut
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Over 5,000 Ebola cases in Congo already — nearly half have died.
article.articleSummary: As of August 19, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo has confirmed over 5,000 Ebola cases, with 2,378 deaths, according to official statistics. The current outbreak has killed more people and progressed more rapidly than any previous Ebola epidemic, surpassing the 2018–2020 outbreak, which involved about 3,500 cases and 2,300 deaths. The World Health Organization warned in late July that the epidemic was likely to spread further. There is currently no vaccine for the circulating Ebola virus strain. The report underscores an ongoing, severe outbreak in the DRC with mounting fatalities, highlighting the urgent need for public health measures and surveillance, even as vaccine options for this specific strain remain unavailable.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴで既に5,000人以上のエボラ症例、約半数が死亡
triage.triage_reason: 5,000例超・死者2,378人という大規模かつ過去最悪の進行速度を示すエボラ流行であり、ワクチンも存在しないため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: WHOも7月末にさらなる拡大の可能性を警告しており、当該株に対するワクチンが存在しない点が管理可能性の懸念を高めている。

article.articleHeadline: Antall ebola-tilfeller i Kongo har passert 5000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of Ebola cases in the Congo has surpassed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, centered in Ituri Province in the eastern region, has surpassed 5,000 infections. Official figures list 5,021 cases and 2,378 deaths. Declared mid‑May, the WHO notes the outbreak likely began in February. About 90% of cases are in Ituri, with confirmed infections in five other provinces, including Kisangani, one of the nation’s largest cities. The outbreak occurs in a region long affected by war and mass displacement. The circulating strain is Bundibugyo ebolavirus, rarer than the strains behind prior West and Central African epidemics; there are no approved vaccines or treatments for this variant. Data current as of 19 August 2026.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ感染者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCのエボラ流行が5,000例・死亡2,378例に達し、複数州へ拡大、ワクチン・治療法未承認の稀少株（Bundibugyoエボラウイルス）であることから、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当し即時のフルリスク評価が必要と判断される。
triage.notes: 致死率約47%と非常に高く、紛争・避難民の多い地域での流行拡大、承認ワクチン・治療薬がない稀少株であることが特に懸念される。WHOによる国際的対応の動向を継続的に確認する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Peste 5.000 de cazuri de Ebola, confirmate în Congo. Aproape jumătate dintre pacienți au murit: numărul real al infectărilor ar putea fi mult mai mare
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Over 5,000 Ebola cases confirmed in Congo. Almost half of the patients have died: the real number of infections could be much higher.
article.articleSummary: DR Congo reports over 5,000 confirmed Ebola cases (5,021 since May) with 2,378 deaths (47.4% case fatality) and more than 1,000 recoveries, under the Bundibugyo strain. Declared mid-May, it is the country’s 17th Ebola outbreak, with rapid spread across multiple regions per WHO. There is currently no vaccine or approved specific treatment for Bundibugyo Ebola, complicating control. Lab-confirmed figures are provided by WHO/DRC authorities, but authorities warn the real infection count may be higher, with studies suggesting the outbreak may have begun as early as February. Two-thirds of deaths occurred outside hospitals or isolation centers, as many patients die in villages, hindering containment. Since July, clinical trials for two antiviral therapies are underway to assess potential reductions in mortality and improved outcomes. Investigations into possible viral mutations are also underway.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴで5,000人以上のエボラ感染確認。患者のほぼ半数が死亡：実際の感染者数はさらに多い可能性
triage.triage_reason: 致死率47.4%の大規模エボラアウトブレイク（5000人超、複数地域に拡大）で、ワクチン・治療薬未確立、実数がさらに多い可能性がある重大事案のため、フルRRAへ進めるべき。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo株による第17回目のエボラアウトブレイク。ワクチン・承認された特効薬がなく、死亡の2/3が病院外で発生しており封じ込めが困難。2種類の抗ウイルス薬の臨床試験が進行中。ウイルス変異の可能性も調査中。

article.articleHeadline: शहर में डेंगू की घातक इंट्री, उपचाररत वृद्धा की मौत -
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue makes a deadly entry into the city; an elderly woman under treatment dies.
article.articleSummary: As of 19 August 2026, dengue has caused a fatal case in Satna city, Madhya Pradesh. A 60-year-old woman, Rajdulari of Life Jyoti Colony, tested dengue-positive after fever and was treated at Satna Government Medical College by Dr. Manoj Prajapati. Despite therapy, she deteriorated and was admitted to Prem Nursing Home on 16 August, then referred to Jabalpur; she died en route near Sihora. In response, the district malaria office conducted a family-wide follow-up; several relatives—two daughters-in-law aged 36 and 26, and a granddaughter aged 17—were febrile but dengue-negative on initial testing. Blood samples were collected from about 15 family members and sent to the district hospital for ELISA/microplate reader testing, with results expected Thursday morning. The incident follows a show-cause notice from the Chief Medical and Health Officer to Malaria Officer Sheela Sonkar for alleged laxity and irregularities in attendance and program duties.

triage.headline_ja: 市内でデング熱が猛威、治療中の高齢女性が死亡
triage.triage_reason: マディヤ・プラデーシュ州サトナ市で単発の死亡例が報告されたが、家族内の追加症例は陰性で確定検査結果待ちであり、国際的な拡大や重大な公衆衛生上の影響は現時点で確認できない。
triage.notes: インド国内の地方報道で、単発のデング熱死亡例と家族内追跡調査（ELISA検査結果待ち）が報告されている。マラリア担当官への行政処分（出頭命令）も言及されているが、これは地方行政の内部問題であり公衆衛生危機の指標ではない。続報でクラスター化の有無を確認する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Santé. " Ebola tue une personne toutes les 30 minutes " : en RDC, la course folle et mortelle de l'épidémie
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Health. "Ebola kills one person every 30 minutes": in the DRC, the frantic and deadly race of the outbreak.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-19, the Bundibugyo Ebola variant is spreading rapidly in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), with at least 5,000 infections and 2,325 deaths (case fatality ~45%). The DRC's 17th outbreak is the deadliest in Central Africa's history, and in three months has killed five times more than the early West Africa outbreak of 2013–2016. The WHO warns national and international spread remains likely, with border-country risk highest and global risk low. In late June, France diagnosed the first imported case in a doctor returning from a humanitarian mission in the DRC; he recovered after roughly 12 days with two negative PCR tests, and five in-flight contacts were isolated at home for 21 days. Several emergency-use vaccines are being tested against this rare strain; efficacy data may take months.

triage.headline_ja: 健康:「エボラは30分毎に1人を死亡させている」：コンゴ民主共和国における狂気的で致死的な流行の実態
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で史上最悪規模のエボラ流行（感染5000人超、死者2325人、CFR約45%）が進行中で、既にフランスへの輸入例も発生しており、IHR基準の複数該当及び国際的関心・支援の必要性が明らかであるため。
triage.notes: フランスは輸入例（帰国医師1名）が報告されているのみで、実際の流行発生国はDRCのみ。アンゴラは記事サマリー中で発生国として言及されていないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: RDC : les attaques contre les ambulances compliquent la lutte contre Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: Attacks on ambulances complicate the fight against Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, centered in Bunia, faces a major obstacle as attacks on ambulances and health teams escalate. The World Health Organization reports a rise in violence against responders, including an ambulance attack in Bunia yesterday, with incidents occurring almost daily. Such hostility reflects community mistrust amid the epidemic and severely hinders emergency interventions, delaying patient care and complicating efforts to contain transmission. The WHO calls on communities to protect health workers to allow responders to operate safely. Health authorities continue risk communication and community engagement campaigns to restore trust between communities and responders, a critical step to stop transmission and save lives in Bunia and surrounding areas.

triage.headline_ja: DRC:救急車への攻撃がエボラ対策を複雑化
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国（ブニア）で進行中のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクにおいて、救急車・医療従事者への攻撃が激化し対応が阻害されている。致死率の高い感染症であり、国際的な公衆衛生上の懸念が高い。
triage.notes: WHOが対応チームへの暴力増加を報告。地域住民の不信感が感染拡大対策を阻害しており、既存のエボラアウトブレイクの深刻化事案として扱う。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola cases in Congo exceed 5,000, government data shows | New Straits Times
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of Congo have reached 5,021 confirmed cases with 2,378 deaths, the latest government situation report shows. The current outbreak, centered in eastern Congo, has spread to a sixth province, Bas-Uele in the northeast. The World Health Organization has declared the Bundibugyo-type outbreak a public health emergency of international concern since May 17, with its director-general Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus noting ongoing global implications. Updated recommendations will be issued in coming days to the DRC government and other at-risk countries. Officials say the 2026 outbreak has surpassed the toll of the 2018–2020 epidemic, becoming the deadliest in the country’s history. The report underscores ongoing transmission and the need for continued public health measures amid the outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ感染者数が5,000人を超える、政府データが示す
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEIC（国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態）を宣言済みで、感染者5,021人・死者2,378人と過去最悪の規模に達しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: WHOは2026年5月17日よりBundibugyo型エボラのアウトブレイクをPHEICとして宣言済み。感染は東部から6番目の州（Bas-Uele）にも拡大しており、2018-2020年の流行を超える同国史上最悪の被害となっている。フルリスク評価（RRA）への即時移行を推奨。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Cases in Congo Exceed 5,000
article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 5,000 confirmed cases, reaching 5,021 with 2,378 deaths, marking the largest epidemic in the DRC’s history. Declared May 15, the Bundibugyo species of Ebola—lacking approved vaccines or treatments—continues to spread; health authorities describe it as the second-worst global outbreak, after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic, in both infections and deaths. The situation persists despite response efforts, with weak health infrastructure, community resistance, instability, and protests by responders hindering identification and containment. As of 2026-08-19, authorities warn response challenges persist, complicating efforts to curb transmission.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでのエボラ感染者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大規模のエボラ流行が発生し、5,000人以上の感染・2,378人の死亡、ワクチン・治療法未承認の株であることから公衆衛生への深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクが高く、IHR基準に複数該当する。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれているが、記事本文はDRCのみを主題としており、Angolaでの発生は言及されていないため除外した。Angolaは対象国リストにも含まれない。

article.articleHeadline: 综述丨刚果（金）埃博拉病例超五千 世卫维持警报
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Overview | Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceed 5,000; WHO maintains the alert.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ebola virus disease outbreak (Bundibugyo type) has surpassed 5,000 confirmed cases, with 5,021 cases, 2,378 deaths, and 1,061 recoveries reported as of August 16. On August 18, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said, after an Emergency Committee meeting, the outbreak remains a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Africa CDC warns this is the deadliest Ebola outbreak in DRC's history, with about one death every 30 minutes and ongoing high transmission, despite expanded laboratory testing and care capacity. The Ituri Province, especially Kisangani, is a focal point, with concerns about spread along transport networks to Kinshasa; no confirmed cases yet in Kinshasa. No vaccine or specific therapy exists for Bundibugyo Ebola; two vaccine candidates are in clinical trials. Ervebo (Zaire ebolavirus vaccine) is being considered for frontline workers under strict frameworks, but evidence of cross-protection against Bundibugyo is inconclusive and not for routine use.

triage.headline_ja: 概要｜コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ症例が5000人超、WHOは警報を維持
triage.triage_reason: 5,000例超・死亡2,378人に達するDRC史上最悪規模のエボラ流行でWHOがPHEICを維持しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当し国際的関心も高い。
triage.notes: WHOがPHEICを維持し、Africa CDCがDRC史上最悪のエボラ流行と警告。キンシャサへの拡大リスクが懸念されているが、キンシャサでの確認例はまだない。

article.articleHeadline: Un risque "élevé" de propagation internationale : l'épidémie d'Ebola en RDC est "loin d'être maîtrisée", alerte l'OMS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A high risk of international spread: the Ebola outbreak in the DRC is far from being under control, the WHO warns.
article.articleSummary: Outbreak: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo declared May 15, the 17th national outbreak, concentrated in northern and eastern regions with weak state capacity. By August 19, 2026, nearly 5,000 people infected and over 2,300 deaths across six provinces and 55 health zones. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned the outbreak is far from controlled and poses a high risk of national and international spread; the Emergency Committee again maintained Ebola as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern since May 17. The current outbreak is the second largest on record, advancing faster than earlier outbreaks; transmission is driven by insecurity, displacement, and large human movement along roads, rivers, and mining corridors. Early symptoms include fever and headaches, delaying diagnosis. No licensed vaccine or treatment; trials are underway. The EU has provided €2.5 million in rapid tests. Response efforts are being decentralized and community-focused amid security incidents and distrust.

triage.headline_ja: 国際的拡大リスクは「高い」：コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱流行は「制御にはほど遠い」とWHOが警告
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEICを維持し、国際的拡大リスクが高いと明言。感染者・死者数が多く、複数州・保健区に拡大しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: 第17回国家流行で史上2番目の規模、致死率高く、治安不安・人口移動が感染拡大要因。ワクチン未承認、EUが資金支援するなど国際支援が既に進行中。

article.articleHeadline: पूर्वांचल में तेजी से फैल रहा है स्क्रब टाइफस, बीएचयू में एक सप्ताह में मिल चुके 12 मरीज, जान लें क‍ितना है घातक - scrub typhus spreading rapidly in purvanchal 12 cases reported at bhu in a week
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Scrub typhus is spreading rapidly in Purvanchal; 12 patients have been reported at BHU in a week; know how deadly it is.
article.articleSummary: Scrub typhus is spreading in Purvanchal, eastern Uttar Pradesh, with Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in Varanasi reporting 12 admissions in the last week. BHU data show 2025 had 493 positives from 2,790 tested (19%), and 2024 Jun–Dec had 481 positives from 2,512 tested (17%). Patients also arrived from Bihar, West Bengal and Jharkhand. A death of a child on 17 August triggered a three-member inquiry (Dr Ajay Kumar Singh, Dr Shishir Kumar, Dr Sharat Chandra Pandey) that confirmed scrub typhus at Prakash Pathology Lab. Since January 2026, 23 cases have been detected; 2025 total was 91. Orientia tsutsugamushi, transmitted by chigger mites in grasses and fields, mainly threatens farmers and rural communities. IgM ELISA testing enables timely diagnosis, but BHU’s pediatrics department has 18 ventilators all in use, and district hospitals lack dedicated infectious-disease wards, risking poor patients. Fever with headache and body pain can mimic dengue, underscoring testing needs.

triage.headline_ja: プールヴァーンチャルでスクラブチフスが急速に拡大、BHUで1週間に12人の患者が報告—致死性を知る
triage.triage_reason: インド東部で従来から発生しているスクラブチフスの季節的増加であり、重症例・死亡例や医療体制不足への懸念はあるが、国際的拡大やヒト-ヒト感染のリスクは低く、フルRRAへの即時移行基準には達しない。
triage.notes: Scrub typhus（Orientia tsutsugamushi）はダニ媒介性で人-人感染はない。ウッタル・プラデーシュ州を中心にビハール州・西ベンガル州からも患者が来院しているが、いずれもインド国内の地域流行。BHUの小児ICU(人工呼吸器18台)が満床であることや地方病院の感染症病棟不足など医療体制への懸念が指摘されている。デング熱との症状の類似性から誤診リスクも示唆されている。

article.articleHeadline: Mobile gold miners in eastern Congo complicate health workers' efforts to contain Ebola
article.articleSummary: In Ituri province, eastern Congo, the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola drives the fastest-moving outbreak on record, with over 2,300 deaths among at least 5,000 cases across six eastern provinces. At artisanal gold mines such as Iga-Barrière, highly mobile workers travel between villages and sites with limited registration or monitoring, hampering contact tracing. Basic containment measures like handwashing and distancing are not consistently followed, and there are no specific treatments or vaccines for this strain. Health workers warn that two Ebola contacts recently moved to another mining site, highlighting gaps in tracking as miners cross communities. The outbreak is fueled by conflict and poverty in the region, where more than 100 armed groups operate. Among miners is 11-year-old Isaac Batisa, illustrating child labor within artisanal mining.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ東部の移動する金採掘労働者が保健当局のエボラ制圧努力を複雑化
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国東部で記録上最速のエボラ（ブンディブジョ株）流行が拡大し、死者2,300人超・症例5,000人超に達しており、ワクチン・治療法もなく、移動性の高い鉱山労働者が接触者追跡を困難にしているため、深刻性・異常性・拡大リスクいずれも高い。
triage.notes: ブンディブジョ株はワクチン・特異的治療法がなく、武装勢力が活動する地域での鉱山労働者の移動性が接触者追跡を妨げている。国境を越えた拡大リスクも懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: WHO says attacks on ambulances affecting DRC Ebola response
article.articleSummary: As of 19 August 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo is contending with its fastest-growing Ebola outbreak, which has killed more than 2,300 people—the deadliest Ebola event on record in Congo. WHO reports frequent attacks on health teams and vehicles, including an ambulance hit in Bunia, with responders describing such incidents as a near-daily threat. Community hostility complicates containment efforts, as residents struggle to understand transmission, symptoms, and where to seek care. Health workers emphasize that robust community engagement is essential to slow transmission, alongside correct recognition of Ebola symptoms and prompt access to treatment. Fear and mistrust among families already coping with seriously ill or dying relatives further hinder response operations, threatening to undermine surveillance, case finding, and patient care in the ongoing outbreak in DRC.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、DRCでのアンビュランス襲撃がエボラ対応に影響していると発表
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最悪となる2,300人以上の死者を出しているエボラ流行が進行中であり、医療対応への攻撃や地域社会の抵抗が制御を著しく妨げている。深刻な公衆衛生影響と国際的拡大リスクがあり、フルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: 史上最悪規模のエボラ流行に加え、医療従事者・救急車への攻撃や地域社会の不信が対応を阻害している点が重大。WHOによる継続的な監視と国際支援の必要性が高い。

diseases.name: Human Infection with Swine Influenza A H1N1

article.articleHeadline: H1N1 Swine Flu: Why Is It Spreading in India?
article.articleSummary: Delhi reports 1,449 H1N1 influenza A (H1N1) cases through August 12, 2026 per NCDC data, up from 229 in the same period last year; spread also extends to other Indian cities. H1N1 is an influenza A virus (H1N1) that emerged in 2009 via reassortment of swine, human and avian genes. Potential drivers include viral mutations, increased person-to-person contact, and monsoon-season dynamics, with seasonality and crowding contributing factors. Symptoms include fever, cough, headache, body aches, fatigue, chills and sweating. High-risk groups include seniors, children, pregnant women, immunosuppressed individuals, and those with asthma, diabetes or heart disease. Treatment relies on antivirals such as oseltamivir; antibiotics are ineffective. A seasonal influenza vaccine exists and is updated periodically; vaccination is advised for high-risk individuals after clinician consultation.

triage.headline_ja: H1N1豚インフルエンザ：インドで拡大している理由とは
triage.triage_reason: デリーでH1N1感染者数が前年同期比で約6倍に増加しているが、重症度や死亡者数、国際的拡大等の情報が不足しており、フルリスク評価の判断には材料が不十分。
triage.notes: NCDCデータに基づき症例数増加が報告されているが、重症度・死亡率・入院数などの詳細情報がなく、インド国内の季節性インフルエンザの通常変動範囲か否かの判断が難しい。続報を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola cases in Congo exceed 5,000
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's 17th Ebola outbreak is the largest in the country's history in both cases and deaths. The public health institute reports 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths, ranking it as the second-worst Ebola outbreak globally after 2014–2016 in West Africa. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo species, for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments. Declared May 15, the epidemic gained momentum in late July and has surpassed 5,000 confirmed cases as of August 19, 2026. Health authorities warn that response efforts are failing to contain the disease due to weak health infrastructure, community resistance, instability, and protests by response workers that hinder case identification and response activities. The situation underscores the need for intensified containment measures and sustained support for affected communities and health systems.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱感染者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大規模のエボラ流行（5,021例、死亡2,378例）が発生し、ワクチン・治療法が未承認のブンディブギョ株が原因で、対応も失敗しつつあるため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: Bluedotの発生地域にAngolaが含まれているが、記事サマリーではDRC国内の流行のみが述べられており、Angolaでの発生は確認できないため除外した。ワクチン・治療薬が未承認のBundibugyo種による流行であり、既に史上最大規模かつ世界第2位の死者数となっている点が重大。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Outbreak in DR Congo 'Far From Under Control', WHO Chief Warns
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is spreading faster than any prior Ebola outbreak, with over 2,300 deaths and nearly 5,000 cases since it was declared on May 15, making it the deadliest in the DRC’s history. It spans six provinces in the north and east amid insecurity, displacement, and widespread movement along roads, rivers and mining routes. The Bundibugyo strain currently has no vaccine or treatment, though trials are underway. WHO warns the risk of further national and international spread remains high, including Uganda; the emergency committee has met twice since declaring a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on May 17. Transmission is occurring at home and in communities, outside treatment centres and contact lists, underscoring the need for rapid, decentralised surveillance and community engagement, including protection of motorcycle taxi drivers involved in transport of patients.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱流行、「制御下には程遠い」とWHO事務局長が警告

article.articleHeadline: Nam bệnh nhân suy đa tạng, sốc nhiễm khuẩn do biến chứng nặng của COVID-19
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Five patients with multi-organ failure and septic shock due to severe complications of COVID-19.
article.articleSummary: A 43-year-old man (D.V.N.) with confirmed COVID-19 rapidly progressed from fever and cough to bilateral pneumonia, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), septic shock, and multi-organ failure. Admitted to Hospital 19-8 (Ministry of Public Security) in Vietnam, he deteriorated despite initial oxygen therapy and non-invasive ventilation, presenting with tachycardia (170 bpm) and SpO2 86% requiring intubation. CT revealed diffuse bilateral lung involvement. He received ARDS-network protective mechanical ventilation, prone positioning, antiviral and antibiotic therapy, vasopressors, anticoagulation, and metabolic stabilization. Within 72 hours, continuous renal replacement therapy with dual cytokine adsorption was initiated, with VV-ECMO readiness if needed. After nearly a month of intensive care, his condition stabilized and he was discharged, with follow-up recommended for ongoing recovery. The report highlights severe COVID-19 cases leading to ARDS and septic shock in Vietnam.

triage.headline_ja: COVID-19の重篤な合併症により多臓器不全・敗血症性ショックを発症した男性患者の例

article.articleSummary: On 2026-08-19, Ebola infections in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have surpassed 5,000 confirmed cases, with a cumulative total of 5,021 cases and 2,378 deaths. The figures come from the Public Health Institute in its latest epidemiological report, based on government data released yesterday evening, and they indicate that the outbreak remains active across the country. As of that date, the data reflect ongoing transmission of confirmed Ebola across the Democratic Republic of the Congo, underscoring the persistent burden of the outbreak. This update confirms that Ebola continues as an ongoing public health concern in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Virus: क्या है इबोला वायरस? जानिए इसके लक्षण, संक्रमण और बचाव के आसान उपाय
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola Virus: What is the Ebola virus? Learn its symptoms, transmission, and easy ways to prevent it.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus outbreak in Congo is described by World Health Organization as the second-largest in history. As of 2026-08-19, 1,094 confirmed cases and 277 deaths have been reported. Ebola, a highly lethal virus, requires vigilance beyond typical flu; early medical consultation is essential for fever, weakness, muscle pains, sore throat, and fatigue. Infected patients’ clothing should be burned. Experts advise five practical precautions: (1) wash hands with soap and water using clean towels, (2) avoid handshakes to limit direct contact, (3) avoid touching someone suspected of infection or their bodily fluids (urine, stool, blood, vomit, sweat, tears, semen, vaginal secretions), and avoid touching the body of a deceased person, which carries higher risk, (4) do not eat meat from monkeys, chimpanzees, or bats, and ensure meat is cooked thoroughly, (5) seek medical care promptly as hospital care prevents dehydration and provides pain relief. Hospitals are the safest place for treatment.

triage.headline_ja: エボラウイルスとは何か？症状・感染経路と予防法について
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で確認1,094例・死亡277例、WHOが史上2番目の規模と評価する大規模エボラ流行が進行中であり、深刻な公衆衛生上の影響と異常性が認められるためフルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: 記事は一般向け予防啓発コンテンツだが、WHOによる「史上2番目に大きい流行」との評価と具体的な感染者数・死亡者数（1,094例、277死亡）が含まれており、実際の大規模流行状況を反映している。続報や公式WHO発表の確認が推奨される。

article.articleHeadline: Число случаев Эбола в ДР Конго превысило 5 тыс.
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of Ebola cases in the DRC exceeded 5,000.
article.articleSummary: As of 19 August 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo has confirmed 5,021 Ebola virus disease cases, making this the country’s largest outbreak and the 17th since the disease emerged there. Reported deaths reached 2,378 over the latest weekend, surpassing fatalities of the previous major outbreak (2018–2020). The current outbreak ranks as the second-largest globally by both cases and deaths, after the West Africa outbreak of 2014–2016. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments. Health authorities declared the outbreak on 15 May. Efforts to contain spread have been hampered by weak health-system infrastructure, community resistance, ongoing instability, and worker protests against response activities.

triage.headline_ja: DRコンゴのエボラ出血熱感染者数が5,000人を超えた

article.articleHeadline: "إيبولا" يواصل التفشي في الكونغو والإصابات تتجاوز الـ5 آلاف
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola continues to spread in Congo, with cases surpassing 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola continues to spread in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with confirmed cases surpassing 5,000. A Public Health Institute report lists 5,021 cumulative cases and 2,378 deaths (case fatality rate about 47%). Last week, the Ministry of Communications said the outbreak extended to Bas-Uélé in the northeast, a region not previously affected. The new area raises concerns about transmission among contacts of an infected patient. Delays in detecting cases, ongoing conflict, and stretched health services are contributing to a faster spread than in earlier outbreaks. The government data were released late Tuesday, reflecting the situation as of August 19, 2026. Outbreak trajectory remains uncertain, and authorities emphasize the need for enhanced surveillance and response.

article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo reports 5,021 Ebola infections and 2,378 deaths, according to the health ministry cited by Reuters. The latest ministry tally notes that nearly half of cases have resulted in death; no details on transmission chains or laboratory confirmation are provided. The grim milestone underscores ongoing transmission and the urgent need for intensified public health response. As of the latest ministry statistics, the outbreak remains active.

article.articleHeadline: Mưa nắng thất thường, nguy cơ sốt xuất huyết lan rộng
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Erratic rain and sunshine increase the risk of dengue fever spreading.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever in Ha Tinh Province, Vietnam, since April 2026. By August, 215 dengue cases have been reported in Ha Tinh, including an active cluster in Tan Duc village, Ky Hoa commune (7 cases) and 4 additional scattered cases in Ky Hoa. A total of 209 cases have been recorded in Vung Ang and Hoanh Son wards and other areas, where outbreaks have been controlled and declared finished. Erratic rain and sun are creating favorable conditions for Aedes mosquitoes, keeping transmission risk high if control efforts lapse. The first local case was identified on 4 August in Ky Hoa; authorities undertook outbreak containment, epidemiological surveillance, environmental sanitation, and larval source reduction, with community education. Dr Vo Xuan Duc emphasizes household participation—weekly checks for standing water, covering containers, and eliminating water-holding items. CDC Ha Tinh Director Dr Nguyen Chi Thanh warns the risk of re-emergence remains elevated; ongoing environmental cleaning and larval control are needed.

article.articleHeadline: H1N1 या वायरल की चपेट में आने के बाद बुखार उतर गया, लेकिन कमजोरी बनी हुई है? डॉक्टर ने बताया कब किस स्थिति में तुरंत भागे अस्पताल
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Fever has subsided after contracting H1N1 or a viral infection, but weakness remains? Doctor explains when to rush to the hospital immediately.
article.articleSummary: At Indraprastha Apollo Hospital, Delhi, Dr. Suranjit Chatterjee explains that post-viral fatigue can persist after fever subsides from illnesses like dengue, chikungunya, influenza, or H1N1, common during the monsoon when infections co-circulate. A patient recovering from viral fever felt unusually tired despite a normal temperature and returned to work, showing that full recovery may lag fever resolution. Factors include dehydration, reduced intake, sleep disruption, and prolonged immune response, plus gradually rebuilding stamina. Returning to work too soon can cause a relapse; gradual reintroduction is advised. Co-infections are possible; a new infection may follow an initial one. Dengue can deteriorate after fever ends, with warning signs: persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain, bleeding, excessive sleepiness, breathing difficulty, confusion, or low urine output. Management emphasizes hydration, stable blood pressure and hematocrit, and overall clinical status—not platelet count alone. If symptoms persist or worsen, seek medical evaluation; avoid self-medication with antibiotics or steroids.

triage.headline_ja: H1N1やウイルス感染後に熱が下がっても倦怠感が続く？医師がすぐに病院へ行くべき状況を解説

article.articleHeadline: Baguio eyed as pilot site for Wolbachia technology against dengue
article.articleSummary: Baguio City is being eyed as a pilot site for Wolbachia bacteria technology, a method aimed at reducing mosquitoes' ability to transmit dengue. Baguio City Health Services Office chief epidemiologist Dr. Donabel Tubera Panes said two companies involved in the technology have expressed interest in using the city as a model site ahead of broader deployment. The report notes the city's dengue-control efforts are exploring innovative vector-control strategies. No timelines, trial results, or regulatory details were disclosed in the publication. No specific dates for pilots or cost estimates were provided.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola, il focolaio più letale nella storia della Repubblica Democratica del Congo: oltre 2.300 morti

This toll surpasses the country’s previous record from the 2018-2020 outbreak in the eastern region, which recorded 2,299 deaths from 3,381 confirmed cases. The new outbreak therefore stands as the most lethal Ebola event documented in the DRC to date. As of 2026-08-19, authorities in the DRC have reported 2,325 deaths and 4,945 confirmed cases.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola cases in Congo exceed 5,000
article.articleSummary: Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) exceed 5,000, with 5,021 cases and 2,378 deaths to date, according to government data. The 17th Ebola epidemic, caused by the Bundibugyo species, has become the largest in DRC history and the second-worst globally after 2014–2016 West Africa in infections and deaths. Declared May 15, the outbreak gained momentum in late July, with no approved vaccines or treatments available. Ongoing response efforts are hampered by weak health infrastructure, community resistance, instability, and protests by response workers, slowing case identification and response. The United Nations calls it the fastest-growing outbreak on record, with a victim reportedly dying every 30 minutes in the DRC. Latest situation reports list 5,021 cases and 2,378 deaths to date.

article.articleHeadline: Случаите на ебола в Демократична република Конго надхвърлиха 5000, показаха данни от правителството
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpassed 5,000, government data show.
article.articleSummary: As of August 19, 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo has over 5,000 confirmed Ebola virus disease (EVD) cases, government data cited by Reuters show, marking the 17th outbreak in the country and the largest by July’s end. The weekend death toll reached about 2,378, surpassing the 2018–2020 outbreak record. The National Institute of Public Health reports 5,021 cases to date, making this outbreak the second-worst globally in both cases and deaths after West Africa’s 2014–2016 epidemic. It is caused by Bundibugyo virus, for which no approved vaccines or specific treatments exist. Since the outbreak was declared on May 15, the spread has been accelerated by weak health infrastructure, community resistance, instability, and protests by outbreak-response workers, which hinder identification and treatment. An illustrative image shows a healthcare worker in PPE at an Ebola treatment center in Bunia, Ituri Province.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱感染者数が5,000人を超えたと政府データが示す
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で確認例5,000人超・死者約2,378人に達し、同国史上最大規模のエボラ流行（Bundibugyoウイルス、ワクチン未承認）であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれているが、記事サマリー中でAngolaでの発生は言及されていないため除外した。ワクチン未承認のBundibugyoウイルス株による第17次流行で、過去最大規模（症例数・死者数ともに世界2位）である点が重要。

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo Ebola cases top 5,000 as WHO warns outbreak is far from over
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) exceeds 5,000 cases and 2,320 deaths as of 19 August 2026, with WHO warning the outbreak remains a global health emergency and far from under control. Following an emergency meeting, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus urged intensified international support, noting the epidemic has a big head start and is still outpacing containment. The Bundibugyo strain currently lacks an approved vaccine or treatment, compounding response challenges amid armed conflict, misinformation, distrust of health workers, and entrenched cultural practices. The outbreak’s pace is described as unprecedented, and the geographical distribution of deaths suggests several transmission chains have yet to be identified. This is the DRC’s 17th Ebola outbreak and the deadliest in its history, surpassing the 2018–2020 episode.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱患者数が5000人を超え、WHOは流行が終息にほど遠いと警告
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRC史上最悪の流行に発展し、WHOが国際的緊急事態と警告、ワクチン・治療法未承認かつ武力衝突が対応を阻害しているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: 致死率約46%、承認されたワクチン・治療法がないブンディブギョ株、武力衝突・偽情報・医療従事者への不信が対応を阻害。DRC史上最悪・最速の流行と報告されている。

article.articleHeadline: L'OMS veut éviter une propagation d'Ebola en Ouganda ou au Soudan Sud
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO aims to prevent the spread of Ebola in Uganda or South Sudan.
article.articleSummary: On 19 August 2026, the WHO states that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo remains a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, following guidance from the Emergency Committee chaired by Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus. The Ebola variant has already led to more than 2,300 deaths. Latest totals show 4,945 confirmed cases and 2,325 deaths, making it the largest outbreak ever observed in the DRC and the second-largest globally after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic (about 11,000 deaths and ~28,000 cases). Transmission is concentrated in northeast DRC, with cases in six provinces. Risk levels are assessed as “very high” in the DRC, “high” in Uganda and neighboring countries, and “low” elsewhere. The WHO aims to prevent cross-border spread to Uganda or South Sudan.

triage.headline_ja: WHOはエボラのウガンダまたは南スーダンへの拡大を防ぐことを目指す
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEIC継続を宣言したDRCでの過去最大規模のエボラ流行であり、国際的拡大リスク（ウガンダ・南スーダンへの越境）が明確に指摘されているためフルRRAへ進むべき。

article.articleHeadline: Los casos de ébola en República Democrática del Congo superan los 5.000, según el Gobierno
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceed 5,000, according to the government.
article.articleSummary: As of August 19, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo has 5,021 confirmed Ebola cases and 2,378 deaths, according to government data. This is the 17th outbreak in the country and its largest by case count, ranking as the second-deadliest globally after the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak. The current outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which no licensed vaccines or treatments exist. Since its declaration on May 15, the response has struggled due to weak health infrastructure, community resistance, ongoing instability, and protests by responders, hindering case identification and control efforts. The public health institute notes the outbreak is escalating and remains a major ongoing public health challenge in the region.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱、政府発表で5,000例を超える

triage.notes: 史上最大規模の同国内アウトブレイクであり、致死率も高い（約47%）。Bundibugyo株にはライセンス済みワクチン・治療薬が存在せず、治安不安・対応者への抗議活動により対応が難航している点も重大なリスク要因。

article.articleHeadline: Epidemija ebole u Kongu izmakla kontroli: Više od 5.000 zaraženih, skoro polovina preminula
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has gotten out of control: More than 5,000 infected, almost half have died.
article.articleSummary: As of August 19, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 confirmed cases, with 2,378 deaths reported by the national Institute of Public Health. The government notes a case fatality rate rising to 46 percent, up from about 20 percent in early June, underscoring that the increase reflects weak health infrastructure and response challenges rather than greater virulence. The current epidemic is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which no licensed vaccine or treatment exists. The outbreak began on May 15 and has expanded to six provinces, amid ongoing community resistance and instability that hamper case finding and containment. The outbreak is the deadliest in DRC history, with 2,325 lives lost according to government data. WHO had suggested containment within 90 days, while a local official warned containment could take up to three months with sufficient resources.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱の流行が制御不能に：感染者5,000人超、約半数が死亡

triage.notes: 致死率が6月の約20%から46%まで上昇しており、医療体制の脆弱性とコミュニティの抵抗により制御が困難な状況。ワクチン・治療薬未承認のBundibugyoウイルス種による流行で、国際的な支援ニーズが高い。

article.articleHeadline: Exclusive: Pulkit Samrat loses 2.5 kg of muscle mass after Malaria: Why does an infection cause rapid muscle mass loss
article.articleSummary: Pulkit Samrat reported losing 2.5 kg of muscle mass during malaria; malaria can reduce muscle mass when prolonged—driven by inflammatory response with IL-2, IL-6 and TNF-alpha—and by reduced appetite leading to insufficient protein intake; malaria may also directly damage muscles; recovery hinges on nutrition, rest, and treating malaria; protein intake should be about 1 g/kg/day normally, rising to ~1.5 g/kg/day during tissue breakdown; typical recovery about six weeks; warning signs needing urgent care include fever, dehydration, confusion, fainting, breathing difficulty, chest pain, reduced urination, vomiting, or very severe muscle pain; doctors from Saifee Hospital Mumbai and Sterling Hospitals Ahmedabad emphasized these points; article context: India; latest update Aug 19, 2026.

triage.headline_ja: 独占:プルキット・サムラト、マラリア罹患後に筋肉量2.5kg減少 なぜ感染症が急速な筋肉量減少を引き起こすのか
triage.triage_reason: 有名人の個人的な健康・闘病エピソードに関する医療解説記事であり、公衆衛生上の異常事象やアウトブレイクの報告ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Еболата во ДР Конго надмина 5.000 случаи, починале 2.378 лица
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC surpasses 5,000 cases; 2,378 people have died.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 5,000 cases, with 5,021 confirmed and 2,378 deaths reported. The update, from the country’s Institute of Public Health, notes the outbreak expanding to a sixth province, compounding control challenges. A World Health Organization spokesperson, Tierno Baldé, said the epidemic could be brought under control within about three months if the necessary response resources are mobilized. WHO had earlier estimated that transmission might be halted within 90 days, but progress has lagged as the virus spreads. The report underscores intensifying outbreak dynamics in an additional region, highlighting the urgent need for enhanced surveillance, case management, and resource deployment to curb further spread and avert broader regional impact.

article.articleHeadline: Kebun Binatang di Jepang Berduka, 4 Penguin Mati Akibat Malaria
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Zoo in Japan Mourns as 4 Penguins Die from Malaria
article.articleSummary: Four Humboldt penguins died at Yagiyama Zoological Park in Sendai, Japan, from avian malaria between July 9 and 19, 2026. An investigation by the University of Iwate announced on Aug 14 that malaria transmitted by mosquitoes caused the deaths; mosquitoes acquire parasites from infected birds and pass them to others. None showed illness until a day before death; avian malaria does not transmit to humans. The park will redesign enclosures to reduce standing water and mosquito breeding, with the penguin exhibit set to reopen after preventive measures. In Sept 2025 the park housed six Humboldt penguins; there are no concrete plans to import new penguins at present. Humboldt penguins are native to coastal Peru and Chile; they tolerate warmer climates and are kept in zoos outside their natural range, including Indonesia's Taman Safari Bogor and Seaworld Ancol.

article.articleHeadline: Bengaluru: Two Teachers Test Positive For H1N1, 500 Students Down With Fever; School Declares Holiday
article.articleSummary: Two teachers at Clarence School in Bengaluru's Richmond Town tested positive for H1N1 swine flu, with lab confirmation at Baptist Hospital, prompting precautionary measures as about 500 students developed fever- or flu-like symptoms. The school declared a five-day holiday (14–18 August) for sanitisation after an initial break on 12 August; physical classes resumed 13 August, though absenteeism remained high and online classes continued during the break. Of roughly 2,500 students, around 500 were absent on 13 August and 21 staff members were also away; 137 children visited the first-aid centre, with 15 sent home and 19 kept under observation. BBMP inspected the campus, issued safety guidelines, and urged hygiene measures. The administration also raised concerns about unhygienic conditions around the campus due to street vendors; BBMP began steps to clear encroachments and improve cleanliness.

triage.notes: 季節性のH1N1流行としては典型的な学校内クラスターであり、重症例・死亡の報告はない。地域行政（BBMP）が衛生対策・環境改善に着手しており、国際的な支援要請は見られない。続報でクラスターの拡大状況（他校・地域への広がり）を確認する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: 肺炎鏈球菌感染不只是嬰幼兒、年長者專利！醫籲：「這族群」更不能輕忽 - 健康新聞 - PChome Online 新聞
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Streptococcus pneumoniae infections are not limited to infants and the elderly; doctors urge that "this group" must not be overlooked.
article.articleSummary: Streptococcus pneumoniae remains a leading cause of adult community-acquired pneumonia and invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD), with risks of bacteremia, meningitis, and death. Taiwan now publicly funds the new 21-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine, in addition to the existing 20-valent vaccine, offering broader protection for eligible adults. Dr. Xie Yijun says serotype replacement in IPD is ongoing, so vaccination strategies must align with current epidemiology. The two vaccines provide complementary protection, to be selected with a physician based on health status. Not only the elderly; high-risk adults—workers under stress, irregular schedules, smokers, heavy drinkers, and those with diabetes, hypertension, or hyperlipidemia—are advised to consider vaccination. Frequent travel to pneumococcal-endemic regions (Japan, China, Hong Kong) or the United States may warrant discussion. With autumn-winter flu season approaching, preemptive vaccination strengthens protection before infections surge.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Underestimating the flu can cost you dearly; never make these mistakes when you’re sick.
article.articleSummary: Influenza (flu) is a viral infection affecting the nose, throat, and lungs. In New Delhi, India, flu symptoms include sudden fever, cough, sore throat, headache, body aches, fatigue, and loss of appetite, often mistaken for a cold. Most recover with rest, fluids, and good nutrition, but seek care if fever is very high, breathing difficulty, chest pain, or deterioration, especially for children, the elderly, pregnant women, and those with existing illnesses. Dehydration is a risk due to fever and sweating; drink frequent small amounts of water, soups, or coconut water, and avoid relying on tea or coffee. Rest, adequate sleep, and limited contact with others help transmission. Eat small, protein-rich meals (lentils, eggs, dairy, paneer) with fruits and vegetables; light options like khichdi or oats are fine. Antibiotics are not routinely needed for viral flu.

article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 confirmed infections, with 2,378 deaths reported in early this week. The seventeenth outbreak wave, reaching late July, is the largest in the DRC by case load and has cumulative cases at 5,021, making it the second-worst Ebola outbreak globally after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic. The current flare is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which there are no licensed vaccines or treatments. Since the outbreak was declared on May 15, transmission has accelerated amid weak health infrastructure, community resistance to safety measures, ongoing violence, and protests by health workers, impeding rapid detection and response. Doctors Without Borders warns limited community engagement; emergency coordinator Trish Newport stresses the need for awareness of signs and procedures, noting some families have lost up to 15 relatives in Ituri. The WHO says the outbreak is moving faster than tracing, with a record 579 cases and 304 deaths last week, while response activities expand to outpace it.

triage.headline_ja: 政府データ：コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ感染者数が5000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で確認例5,021人・死亡2,378人に達し、史上2番目に大きいエボラ流行となっており、IHR基準（深刻性・異常性）を2つ以上満たすため、フルリスク評価に進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: Bluedotの発生地域にAngolaが含まれるが、記事サマリー中でAngolaでの発生に関する記述はなく、主題はDRC（特にIturi州）に限定されるため除外した。ワクチン・治療薬未承認のBundibugyo型エボラウイルスによる流行で、WHOも追跡が感染拡大に追いついていないと警告している点は特に注視すべき。

article.articleHeadline: 刚果（金）埃博拉病例逾5千　世卫维持警报
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola cases in DR Congo exceed 5,000; WHO maintains alert.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease (EVD) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has surpassed 5,000 confirmed cases, with 5,021 infections, 2,378 deaths and 1,061 recoveries reported as of August 16, 2026. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus; no vaccine or specific therapy exists for this strain. The WHO Director-General declared it a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). The Africa CDC warns it is the deadliest Ebola outbreak in DRC history, with an estimated death every ~30 minutes amid intense surveillance challenges. The JoPo Province and its capital Kisangani are focal due to transport links, with spillover risk to other regions; Kinshasa has had no confirmed cases yet. Two Bundibugyo-targeted vaccines are in clinical trials; Ervebo (Zaire ebolavirus vaccine) may be used for frontline workers under strict research/ethics, but cross-protection for Bundibugyo is unproven.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ感染者5000人超　WHOは警戒継続
triage.triage_reason: 5000人超の感染者・2378人の死亡者を伴うPHEIC宣言済みのエボラ流行であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため、フルRRAへ進めるべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: WHOによるPHEIC宣言済み、Bundibugyoエボラウイルスに対するワクチン・治療法が未確立であり、感染拡大リスクが高い。Kinshasaでは未確認だが交通拠点Kisangani経由での拡散リスクが指摘されている。

article.articleHeadline: Epidemia di Ebola in Congo "più letale di sempre", bilancio di morti e contagiati: qual è la causa del virus
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in Congo 'deadliest ever', death toll and number of infections: what is the cause of the virus.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo is battling its 17th Ebola outbreak, the deadliest to date, centered in the northeast. The Bundibugyo virus has caused 4,945 confirmed cases and 2,325 deaths, with the United Nations noting it as the fastest‑growing epidemic and reporting a death roughly every 30 minutes. There is no vaccine or specific treatment for this strain. Transmission occurs through contact with bodily fluids, producing severe hemorrhagic fever, amid severely under-resourced health infrastructure and ongoing armed conflict in the north‑east. The outbreak was declared on 15 May 2026. By comparison, the 2013–2016 West Africa epidemic (Liberia, Sierra Leone, Guinea) killed over 11,300. WHO hopes to reverse spread within three months; authorities stress prevention, including handwashing stations at businesses, though community engagement remains weak according to regional WHO director Mohamed Janabi.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ出血熱が流行「史上最も致死的」、死者数と感染者数：ウイルスの原因は何か
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最も致死的とされるエボラ（ブンディブギョ株、ワクチン・特効薬なし）の流行が拡大中で、死亡率・拡大速度ともに深刻。武力紛争下で医療体制が脆弱であり、WHOも介入している。
triage.notes: リベリア・シエラレオネ・ギニアは2013-2016年の西アフリカ流行との比較として言及されているのみで、現行のアウトブレイクの発生地ではないため verified_locations から除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola, il focolaio più letale nella storia della Repubblica Democratica del Congo: oltre 2.300 morti
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola, the deadliest outbreak in the history of the Democratic Republic of the Congo: over 2,300 deaths.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-19, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 2,325 deaths among 4,945 confirmed cases, making it the deadliest Ebola epidemic in the country’s history. The tally surpasses the 2018–2020 outbreak in the eastern DRC, which reported 2,299 deaths over 3,381 confirmed cases. The article notes the ongoing progression of infections and deaths, a development that is drawing concern from international health authorities as the nation fights one of its gravest crises in recent years. The data cited reflect official counts, underscoring the severity of the current outbreak compared with past transmission. Authorities in the DRC continue to monitor the situation.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱、コンゴ民主共和国史上最も致死的なアウトブレイク：死者2,300人超
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRC史上最悪の規模（死者2,325人、確定症例4,945人）に達し、国際的な公衆衛生上の懸念が高まっているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 過去最大規模のアウトブレイクであり、致死率が高く（約47%）、国際保健当局の注視対象。フルリスク評価（RRA）への移行が適切。

article.articleHeadline: DR Kongo ne uspijeva suzbiti ebolu: Broj oboljelih premašio 5 tisuća slučajeva
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DR Congo fails to contain Ebola: The number of cases has surpassed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's 17th Ebola outbreak has surpassed 5,000 confirmed cases, with government data showing 5,021 total cases and 2,378 deaths as of the latest weekend tally. The outbreak is the largest in DR Congo's history by case count, reaching that milestone by the end of July, and health authorities warn containment efforts are failing to curb the deadly disease. The Institute of Public Health ranks it as the second-worst Ebola outbreak globally, after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic, in both infections and fatalities. The report provides no details on symptoms, transmission chains, or infection sources, and there is no mention of exported cases in the article. The figures reflect government-reported data for this continuing crisis in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

triage.headline_ja: DRコンゴ、エボラの抑制に失敗：感染者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRコンゴで史上最大規模のエボラ流行が拡大し死者2,378人に達しており、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクが認められるため。
triage.notes: アンゴラは発生地域として付与されているが、記事本文ではDRコンゴのみが感染拡大地域として記載されており、アンゴラでの発生は確認できないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Épidémie d'Ebola : la course au vaccin s'accélère pour contrer le virus Bundibugyo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak: the race to a vaccine accelerates to counter the Bundibugyo virus.
article.articleSummary: Since May 15, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) faces Ebola’s deadliest outbreak in its history, driven by the Bundibugyo virus. The article reports an accelerated race to develop a vaccine to counter Bundibugyo, signaling intensified local and international public health efforts as the outbreak evolves. Bundibugyo, a form of Ebola, presents heightened challenges for containment within the DRC. The piece highlights rapid vaccine design, testing, and deployment as central to the response, reflecting urgency amid ongoing surveillance and outbreak management in affected areas of the DRC. Health authorities emphasize urgency to protect frontline workers and communities, with vaccine developers collaborating across international partners to shorten development timelines.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱の流行：ブンディブギョ・ウイルスに対抗するためワクチン開発競争が加速
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で史上最悪とされるエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）の流行が継続中であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルリスク評価に進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: 記事は2026年5月15日以降DRCで発生している『史上最悪』とされるエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）流行とワクチン開発競争を報じている。感染規模・死亡率等の具体的数値は記事中に記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: Kinshasa : l'alerte d'un cas suspect d'Ebola à Lemba invalidée après investigation
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Kinshasa: alert of a suspected Ebola case in Lemba ruled out after investigation.
article.articleSummary: Kinshasa’s Lemba commune generated an alert for a suspected Ebola case, later invalidated after investigation by the Kinshasa Provincial Health Division and the Public Health Emergency Operations Center. The National Public Health Institute (INSP) said no epidemiological linkage to the current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo was found. The investigation, while closing the alert, reinforced critical response functions at Kinshasa’s University Clinics: epidemiological surveillance, case-definition application, patient triage and routing, early alert notification, and infection prevention and control. The DRC is contending with its 17th Ebola outbreak, with six provinces affected and six provincial zones reporting new cases. Ituri remains the epicenter, while security and worker-pay issues have disrupted response operations, notably at Bunia treatment centers. Ongoing insecurity in the east and population movements raise concerns for surveillance, contact tracing, and patient care.

triage.headline_ja: キンシャサ：レンバ地区のエボラ疑い症例、調査後に否定される
triage.triage_reason: キンシャサでの疑い例自体は否定されたが、記事はDRCで進行中の第17次エボラ流行（6州に拡大、治安・資金問題で対応が混乱）に言及しており、国際的拡大や対応能力への懸念からフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: キンシャサ・レンバ地区の疑い症例は現行流行との疫学的関連なしと結論。ただしDRC全体では第17次エボラ流行が継続中で、イトゥリ州が中心地、ブニアの治療センターでは治安・給与問題により対応が阻害されている。地理的拡大（6州）と治安悪化・人口移動によるサーベイランス・接触者追跡・患者管理への懸念が続く。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC: l'OMS maintient l'urgence sanitaire internationale et appelle à renforcer la riposte
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC: WHO maintains the Public Health Emergency of International Concern and calls for strengthening the response.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo remains a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, according to the WHO Emergency Committee meeting on 18 August 2026. This is the 17th Ebola outbreak in the DRC, with six provinces affected and six provincial zones reporting new cases, the epicentre in Ituri. Despite the DRC's prior experience, the response faces significant obstacles in areas with weak health infrastructure and ongoing insecurity that hampers access to communities, surveillance, and patient care. In Ituri, strikes by some responders disrupted Ebola treatment centers in Bunia, with reported delays in payment of staff allowances; authorities have acknowledged delays and moved to regularize payroll via staff list validation and digitalization. Security attacks and population displacements in the eastern conflict zones further complicate the response. Updated recommendations for the DRC and other at-risk countries will be issued in coming days.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ流行下のDRC：WHOは国際的な公衆衛生上の緊急事態（PHEIC）を維持し、対応強化を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEICを維持していることは既に国際的な公衆衛生上の懸念が認定されている事象であり、IHR基準の複数該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、国際拡大リスク）とWPRO基準の複数該当が確認されるため、フルRRAへの移行が適切。
triage.notes: 本事象はDRCで進行中の第17次エボラ流行であり、WHOは既にPHEICを維持継続中。治安不安・医療インフラ脆弱性・スタッフのストライキ等が対応の障害となっており、継続的なモニタリングと国際支援強化が必要とされる状況。

article.articleHeadline: 肺炎鏈球菌感染不只是嬰幼兒、年長者專利！醫籲：「這族群」更不能輕忽
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Pneumococcal infection is not exclusive to infants and the elderly; doctors urge that this group should not be overlooked.
article.articleSummary: Taiwan's adult pneumococcal vaccination program now offers both the 20-valent and newly added 21-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccines under public funding, reflecting evolving local IPD epidemiology and serotype replacement. Streptococcus pneumoniae remains a leading cause of community-acquired pneumonia and invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD), with severe outcomes including bacteremia, meningitis, or death. The new PCV21 coverage aligns with Taiwan’s current circulating serotypes, providing more precisely tailored protection alongside the existing PCV20. While seniors (65+) are eligible for public funding, doctors warn that many adults at high risk—long-working, stressed workers, smokers, drinkers, those with diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia—should discuss vaccination with clinicians. Travel to Japan, China, Hong Kong, and the United States brings exposure to diverse serotypes and resistant strains. With autumn-winter flu season, reduced immunity elevates risk; vaccination strategy should cover pneumococcus, not just influenza.

triage.headline_ja: 肺炎鏈球菌感染不只是嬰幼兒、年長者專利！醫籲：「這族群」更不能輕忽
triage.triage_reason: 台湾における肺炎球菌ワクチン接種プログラムの拡充に関する一般的な医療情報記事であり、感染症の異常発生やアウトブレイクの報告ではない。
triage.notes: 記事は台湾国内の公費ワクチン接種プログラム拡大に関する啓発・医療情報であり、感染症のアウトブレイクや異常事象を報じるものではない。日本・中国・香港・米国への言及は旅行時の血清型多様性への注意喚起に過ぎず、いずれの国でも実際の発生事例は記載されていない。台湾はGeoNames対象国リストに含まれていないため、verified_locationsは空配列とする。

article.articleHeadline: شیوع ابولا در کنگو هنوز یک وضعیت اضطراری بهداشتی در سطح جهانی است
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in Congo remains a global health emergency.
article.articleSummary: As of 19 August 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). WHO Director‑General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, following the Emergency Committee’s guidance, urged governments and partners to intensify efforts and mobilize resources to better protect communities in the coming months. Updated recommendations will be issued to the DRC and other at‑risk countries in the coming days. Anadolu Agency reported the latest figures: 2,325 deaths—the highest mortality tally in the country to date—and more than 5,000 confirmed cases, with a case fatality rate of 46%. The report highlights ongoing transmission and international concern, as authorities prepare additional measures and broader international support.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでのエボラ流行は依然として国際的な公衆衛生上の緊急事態である
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEIC（国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態）を継続指定しており、死者2,325人・症例5,000人超・致死率46%と深刻な公衆衛生影響が確認されているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: WHOによりPHEICとして継続認定されているエボラ出血熱流行。致死率46%と非常に高く、国際的な資源動員と追加対応策が求められている。

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo Ebola outbreak remains global health emergency as cases surge
article.articleSummary: DR Congo Ebola outbreak (Bundibugyo ebolavirus) remains a public health emergency of international concern (PHEIC) as cases surpass 5,000. As of Sunday, 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths reported across 55 health zones in six provinces, CFR 47.4%. Ituri province is the epicenter, accounting for about 84.8% of cases, with spread accelerating to neighboring provinces. No approved vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo; two Bundibugyo-specific vaccines in human trials; PARTNERS trial evaluating remdesivir, MBP134, and their combination; obeldesivir tested as post-exposure prophylaxis. Ervebo (Zaire ebolavirus vaccine) is being explored for cross-protection; Africa CDC supports controlled expanded use for high-risk workers with a Phase III trial to assess protection against Bundibugyo. Risks of further spread within DRC remain very high; cross-border risk to Uganda, South Sudan, Central African Republic; Kisangani (Tshopo) and Kinshasa focal points; screening intensified along rivers.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱流行、症例増加に伴い依然として国際的な公衆衛生上の緊急事態
triage.triage_reason: WHOによりPHEICと認定された大規模エボラ流行で、症例数・死者数が急増し複数州・近隣国への拡大リスクがあるため、IHR基準・WPRO基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: 近隣国（ウガンダ、南スーダン、中央アフリカ共和国）への越境リスクが指摘されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。

article.articleHeadline: Một tháng nguy kịch do Covid-19, bệnh nhân được cứu sống nhờ can thiệp ECMO
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A month in critical condition due to COVID-19, the patient was saved thanks to ECMO intervention.
article.articleSummary: 43-year-old male police officer in Vietnam (D.V.N) developed COVID-19 with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), septic shock and multi-organ failure. After July 16 symptoms and a July 20 positive test, he was transported hundreds of kilometers to Hanoi for care at Bệnh viện 19-8 (Ministry of Public Security Hospital). He required invasive ventilation, vasopressors, renal replacement therapy, antibiotics, corticosteroids and anticoagulation. Facing rapid deterioration, ICU teams planned VV-ECMO and initiated advanced supportive care, including continuous renal replacement therapy with cytokine adsorption within the first 72 hours. After nearly 30 days of intensive care, pulmonary and organ function improved; he was weaned from the ventilator and discharged on 19 August 2026. Health officials emphasize early diagnosis and multidisciplinary management as crucial, noting the patient’s return to police duty.

triage.headline_ja: COVID-19により1か月間重篤な状態にあった患者、ECMO治療により命を救われる
triage.triage_reason: 単一患者の重症COVID-19治療成功例を報じる医療記事であり、集団発生や異常な流行状況を示す情報は含まれていない。
triage.notes: 本記事は個別患者の治療経過（ECMO導入による救命）を紹介する内容であり、公衆衛生上の新たな脅威やアウトブレイクを示すものではない。

article.articleHeadline: H1N1 Outbreak At Bengaluru School, 500+ Students Fall Sick: What Parents Should Know
article.articleSummary: Two students at Clarence High School in Bengaluru’s Richards Town tested positive for H1N1 influenza A, with one staff member undergoing treatment at Bangalore Baptist Hospital. As of 2026-08-19, the flu-like illness has affected more than 500 students and 21 staff, prompting the school to shut temporarily. Symptoms include fever, cough, cold and body aches. Health officials caution that confirmed H1N1 cases do not imply all ill individuals have H1N1, since other influenza strains and respiratory infections can mimic symptoms. Testing is needed to distinguish cases. Guidance emphasizes hand hygiene, respiratory etiquette, staying home when sick, vaccination, and consulting a doctor, particularly for high-risk children (under five, asthma, heart disease, diabetes, neurological disorders). Early antiviral treatment is most beneficial within the first 48 hours for those at higher risk. Seek urgent care if breathing difficulties, bluish lips, dehydration, altered consciousness, seizures, or persistent vomiting occur.

triage.headline_ja: バンガロールの学校でH1N1アウトブレイク、500人以上の生徒が発症：保護者が知っておくべきこと
triage.triage_reason: 既知の季節性H1N1インフルエンザによる単一校内での集団発生であり、重症例の報告はなく国際的拡大の兆候もないが、罹患者数が多く学校閉鎖に至っているため続報を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 確定例は2名のみで、残り多数は症状類似の他の呼吸器感染症の可能性もあると記事内で明記されている。重症化例や死亡例の報告はなく、学校コミュニティ内に限定された事象と見られる。

article.articleHeadline: Deadliest Ebola Outbreak in DRC History Overwhelms Health System
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), centered in Ituri Province, is the deadliest Ebola outbreak on record with more than 4,900 confirmed cases and over 2,300 deaths since it was declared on May 15, 2026. BVD is a rare Ebola strain for which there are no licensed vaccines or approved therapies, leaving emphasis on early detection, supportive care, infection prevention, and community engagement. The outbreak originated in Ituri, with transmission driven by armed conflict, population movement, detection delays, and mistrust within communities. Laboratory capacity has expanded to over 12 laboratories within Ituri to speed diagnosis, though testing and treatment are still hampered by conflict. Stopping transmission requires medical care, security, governance, and trust-building as of 19 August 2026.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国史上最悪のエボラ出血熱流行、医療システムが崩壊
triage.triage_reason: DRC史上最大規模のエボラ（ブンディブギョウイルス病）流行で、死者2,300人超・確認例4,900人超。ワクチン・治療薬未承認かつ武力紛争が拡大要因となっており、IHR基準の複数該当およびWPRO基準の該当が明確。
triage.notes: ブンディブギョウイルス病（BVD）はエボラ属の一種で、ワクチン・治療薬が未承認。武力紛争、住民移動、検知遅延、コミュニティの不信感が感染拡大の要因。史上最悪規模の流行とされ、国際的な支援・注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: DOH says leptospirosis cases down 35%, 3.1M prophylaxis caps ready
article.articleSummary: Leptospirosis in the Philippines declined to 3,440 cases as of Aug. 8, down 35% from 5,318 in the same period in 2025. However, epidemiological monitoring shows a 27% biweekly rise from July 12–25, 2026 (348 cases) versus June 28–July 11 (275). In response to heavy rains from the habagat monsoon, the DOH has positioned 3.1 million doxycycline capsules across its central office and 17 regional CHDs, with YAKAP provider prescriptions and DoH Code White Alert centers, plus nearly 3,000 PhilHealth-accredited GAMOT providers supplying prophylaxis. PhilHealth benefit updates (effective July 15, 2026) raise standard hospitalization to P63,000 from P21,450; severe/critical care is now P170,000–P411,000. Severe leptospirosis treatment is covered under the DOH Zero Balance Billing Program in DOH-administered and PhilHealth-accredited hospitals. Exposed individuals should seek medical evaluation within 24–48 hours; precautions include wearing boots and washing with soap and water. Symptoms include fever, headache, chills, leg muscle pain, and eye redness.

triage.headline_ja: DOH、レプトスピラ症症例が35%減少と発表、予防薬310万カプセルを準備
triage.triage_reason: レプトスピラ症はフィリピンで毎年雨季に発生する既知の風土病であり、全体としては前年比35%減少と報告されているが、直近2週間では27%の増加も見られるため経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: モンスーン季の増水に伴う季節性の風土病であり、DOHは予防薬の配備と保険制度の拡充で対応済み。直近の増加傾向（6月末〜7月に27%増）は続報で確認が必要。
