article.articleHeadline: Nashik News: महापालिकेच्या २०८ आस्थापनांना नोटीसा; डेंग्यूच्या अळ्यांचा शोध - Deshdoot
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Nashik News: Notices to 208 establishments of the Municipal Corporation; search for dengue larvae - Deshdoot
article.articleSummary: Since a monsoon lull, Nashik city has seen rising dengue activity, prompting the municipal malaria department to intensify larva surveillance and door-to-door inspections. Dengue larvae were found in eight government offices, including Nashik Zilla Parishad, Nashik Road Railway Station, and the Government Technical Institute. In response, the Nashik Municipal Corporation has served show-cause notices to 208 establishments; 120 notices were issued in July and 88 in August. Inspections target risk sites such as construction sites, vacant plots, basements, scrap depots, tire shops, and rooftop water tanks to prevent water stagnation and mosquito breeding. Dengue cases rose from 6 in January to 33 in July; August’s first 14 days added 29 more, totaling 85 for the season. Separately, three swine flu deaths have heightened health concerns. Authorities urge eliminating standing water to curb transmission.

triage.headline_ja: ナシック市:市役所208施設に通知;デング熱幼虫の捜索
triage.triage_reason: 季節性のデング熱発生と自治体による通常の幼虫駆除対応であり、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは見られないが、豚インフルエンザ死亡例の言及もあり継続的な監視が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はナシック市（マハーラーシュトラ州）における季節性デング熱の増加と自治体の対応を報告。豚インフルエンザによる3件の死亡も言及されているが詳細情報は不足。ローカルな公衆衛生対応であり、国際的な影響は現時点で確認されない。

article.articleHeadline: WHO v koncoch: Ebola sa šíri a zdravotníctvo pomaly zlyháva
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO at the end of its rope: Ebola is spreading and healthcare is slowly failing.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 confirmed cases (5,021) with 2,378 deaths, ranking as the second-largest Ebola epidemic by both cases and fatalities, behind the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak (Guinea, Liberia, Sierra Leone) that recorded about 28,000 cases and over 11,300 deaths. The current outbreak—the 17th in the DRC—is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which no approved vaccine or treatment exists. Declared May 15, the outbreak has intensified amid weak health infrastructure, community resistance, political and security instability, and protests by frontline workers. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned the disease could spread to other countries; the risk remains high and the outbreak is not under control, spreading more rapidly than any prior Ebola event. Cross-border movement and public distrust have hindered containment.

triage.headline_ja: WHOは限界に:エボラが拡大し、医療体制が徐々に崩壊している
triage.triage_reason: DRCで第17次エボラ流行が5,000例・死亡2,378人に達し、過去最大級の規模で急速に拡大しており、WHOが他国への拡大リスクを警告しているためIHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 発生地域にリベリア・ギニア・シエラレオネが含まれているが、これらは2014-2016年の過去の流行との比較対象であり、現在の発生国ではないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Unpaid health workers deepen strain on DRC Ebola response
article.articleSummary: DRC Ebola outbreak worsens as of mid-August 2026: 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths (case fatality 47.4%).  Health workers are heavily affected with 155 infected and 45 dead (≈29% fatality among infected staff), representing about 3.1% of all cases and 2% of deaths. Frontline teams monitor 19,630 contacts, manage 751 active cases in isolation, and operate across 47 health zones in five provinces; the outbreak has expanded to six provinces and 55 health zones. Latest confirmed case detected in Bas-Uélé after a patient travelled from Haut-Uélé, signaling cross-provincial transmission. In July 2026, Ituri response workers went on strike over unpaid salaries, temporarily closing centres and interrupting care as confirmed cases surpassed 2,000. Bed occupancy is 63.4%, with 751 active cases occupying more than 60% of beds, underscoring the need to retain and protect health workers to sustain outbreak response.

triage.headline_ja: 未払いの医療従事者、DRCのエボラ対応に更なる負担
triage.triage_reason: DRCで確認例5,021件・死亡2,378件（致死率47.4%）と大規模化しており、州間伝播や医療従事者の未払いによるストライキが対応能力を損なっているため、フルリスク評価が必要と判断。
triage.notes: 州間（Haut-UéléからBas-Uéléへ）の伝播が確認されており、医療従事者の未払い問題が対応の持続性に影響。国境を越えた国際的拡大の明確な証拠は記事内になし。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Congo, oltre 2300 morti: Ue dona test diagnostici
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Congo, over 2,300 deaths: EU donates diagnostic tests.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues, with 2,325 deaths among 4,945 confirmed cases, the deadliest Ebola epidemic in the country's history, surpassing the 2018-2020 crisis (2,299 deaths/3,381 cases). The European Union is purchasing 2.5 million euros worth of rapid molecular point-of-care diagnostic tests and analysis tools for delivery to the African CDC by month end, with a separate WHO-backed agreement planned for additional tests. The initiative follows a visit to Ituri, emphasizing the urgent need for faster diagnostics to enable timely care and curb spread, per EU Commissioner Hadja Lahbib. The EU has mobilized 493 million euros in emergency aid, vaccines, treatments, and health security in the Great Lakes region and Uganda.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ、死者2300人超：EUが診断検査キットを寄贈
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で同国史上最悪のエボラ出血熱流行（死者2325人/確定4945例）が継続し、EUやWHOが緊急支援を実施していることから、国際的関心・公衆衛生上の深刻性が高く、フルRRAに進むべき事案。
triage.notes: 発生地域にNSW州・オーストラリア・ウガンダが含まれるが、記事本文で確認された発生地はコンゴ民主共和国（イトゥリ州）のみ。ウガンダはEUの支援対象地域として言及されているが、感染発生の確認情報はない。

article.articleHeadline: Mobile gold miners in eastern Congo complicate health workers' efforts to contain Ebola
article.articleSummary: Eastern Congo’s Ituri province faces the fastest-moving Ebola outbreak in history, driven by Bundibugyo Ebola virus. As of 2026-08-19, nearly 5,000 people are infected and about 2,325 have died. The outbreak is spreading across six eastern provinces, with Ituri at the center, and lacks specific treatments or vaccines for Bundibugyo. Health workers warn that the movement of artisanal miners complicates containment: miners travel between villages and mining sites with minimal infection-control practices, making contact tracing and surveillance difficult. At the Iga-Barrière artisanal gold mine, hundreds work, including children, often in unsafe conditions; two identified contacts moved to unknown destinations, hindering tracing. No reliable system registers mine workers or tracks movements. Artisanal mining employs roughly 2 million in Congo, and UNICEF estimates about 15% of children aged 5–17 are in child labor. Pregnant women are among those observed at sites.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ東部の移動する金採掘労働者、エボラ拡大防止の取り組みを複雑化させる
triage.triage_reason: 史上最速の拡大とされるエボラ（ブンディブジョ株）流行で、感染者約5000人・死者約2325人、6州に拡大しワクチン・治療薬もなくIHR基準複数該当。
triage.notes: 記事はコンゴ東部イトゥリ州を中心とするエボラ（ブンディブジョ株）流行を主題とし、6州への拡大、鉱山労働者の移動による接触者追跡困難、ワクチン・治療薬未確立など複数の懸念要因が明記されている。

article.articleHeadline: إصابات إيبولا في جمهورية الكونغو الديمقراطية تتجاوز 5 آلاف حالة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpass 5,000.
article.articleSummary: As of August 19, 2026, Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 confirmed infections, with a cumulative total of 5,021 cases and 2,378 deaths, according to government data and the Public Health Institute’s latest epidemiological report. The report confirms ongoing Ebola activity in the DRC but provides no details on symptoms, laboratory confirmation methods, or infection sources. No information is provided on transmission dynamics, geographic hotspots within the country, or any imported or exported cases. The figures indicate a persistent, fatal Ebola outbreak in the DRC.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ感染者数が5000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約47%の大規模エボラ流行が5000例を超え継続中であり、公衆衛生上深刻かつ国際的拡大リスクを有するため、フルRRAへ進めるべきシグナルと判断する。
triage.notes: 感染源、伝播動態、地理的分布、症例の輸出入に関する情報は記事中に記載がなく不明。累計5,021例、死亡2,378例と致死率が非常に高く、継続的な流行が示唆される。

article.articleHeadline: Ебола у Конгу не посустаје: више од 5.000 заражених, скоро 2.400 преминулих
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Congo continues unabated: more than 5,000 infected, nearly 2,400 dead.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo continues unabated, with 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths reported as of 19 August 2026. This marks the largest Ebola outbreak in the country's history, now spreading to six provinces. A new Ebola treatment center in Rvakoleu, Bunia, features a handwashing station at its entrance, reflecting ongoing containment efforts, though access and delivery of aid remain challenging given weak health infrastructure. The World Health Organization has cautioned that, with adequate resources, the outbreak could be brought under control within about three months, revising earlier optimistic timelines that suggested a 90-day halt. The latest epidemiological report underscores the expanding scale and the need for intensified on-the-ground support to curb transmission and ensure patient care.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ収束せず：感染者5,000人超、死者は2,400人近くに
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で史上最大規模のエボラ流行が6州に拡大し、死亡者数も多く公衆衛生上の深刻な影響とヒト-ヒト感染リスクが認められるため、フルRRAへ進める。
triage.notes: 史上最大規模のエボラ流行が6州に拡大しており、WHOも資源投入の必要性を指摘。国際的な支援体制の強化が急務。

article.articleHeadline: Эбола унесла почти 2400 жизней в ДР Конго, число заражённых превысило пять тысяч
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola has claimed nearly 2,400 lives in DR Congo, with the number of infected surpassing five thousand.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths (approx. 47.4% case fatality), making it the second-largest outbreak on record. The disease has spread across six provinces and 55 health zones, with mid-August confirmations in Nord-Uele (Lower Uele) expanding the initial Ituri epicenter. The outbreak, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, was declared on 15 May. There is no approved vaccine or specific treatment for this Ebola species, though two vaccines designed against it are in human trials. WHO maintains the outbreak as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, noting the risk of further spread remains high; WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on 18 August that transmission is far from under control. Uganda confirmed cases until 21 June, with last discharge on 16 July and a 42-day monitoring period beginning, during which no new transmission chains were detected in the country.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱による死者が約2400人に達し、感染者数は5000人を超えた
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEIC（国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態）を維持しているコンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）流行で、致死率約47%、6州55保健区に拡大しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進めるべき事案。
triage.notes: ウガンダでの感染確認は6月21日までで、7月16日の最終退院後42日間の監視期間中に新規伝播は確認されておらず、現時点でウガンダは主要な発生地ではないため verified_locations から除外した（対象国リストにも含まれない）。

article.articleHeadline: Kongom tiho hara druga najgora epidemija ebole u povijesti. Munjevito se širi, cjepiva nema
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In the Congo, the second-worst Ebola epidemic in history is silently ravaging. It is spreading rapidly; there is no vaccine.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 5,021 cases and 2,378 deaths, according to the latest government state report, making it the second-worst Ebola outbreak globally after the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak and the largest in the Congo by case count. Declared on May 15, the epidemic has rapidly expanded, with end-of-July figures marking the country’s largest Ebola burden to date. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccines or treatments. Authorities warn that weak health infrastructure, local resistance, political instability, and strikes by health workers hindering suppression efforts are hampering detection and containment, allowing ongoing transmission. The ongoing outbreak underscores serious challenges to disease control in the region.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでは静かに史上2番目に悪いエボラ流行が拡大している。急速に広がっており、ワクチンはない。
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でのブンディブギョ株エボラ流行が5,021例・2,378死亡に達し、史上2番目の規模でワクチン・治療薬もなく、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクが認められるため、フルリスク評価に進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: 記事はコンゴ民主共和国（DRC）でのブンディブギョ株エボラ流行を主題としており、Bluedotが付与したAngolaは本文中で言及されておらず対象国リストにも含まれないため除外した。致死率は約47%と非常に高く、ワクチン・治療薬が存在しない点、医療従事者のストライキや政治的不安定さが対応を妨げている点が特に懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo Ebola outbreak remains global health emergency as cases surge
article.articleSummary: DRC Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus is a WHO public health emergency of international concern (PHEIC) as of Aug 19, 2026, with 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths across 55 health zones in six provinces (case fatality rate 47.4%). Ituri remains the epicenter, about 84.8% of cumulative cases, with infections accelerating in neighboring provinces. The epidemic is the second-largest and spreading faster than all previous outbreaks; deaths outside treatment facilities and rising surveillance workload indicate transmission is not yet interrupted. No Bundibugyo-specific vaccine or treatment is approved; two vaccines against Bundibugyo are in human trials. The PARTNERS trial is evaluating remdesivir and MBP134, alone and in combination; obeldesivir is studied for post-exposure prophylaxis. Ervebo cross-protection for Bundibugyo is unconfirmed, though Africa CDC backs controlled use for high-risk workers with a Phase III trial. Cross-border risk remains high for Uganda, South Sudan, and Central African Republic; Kinshasa remains at risk, with intensified river route screening.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱流行、症例増加で国際的な公衆衛生上の緊急事態が継続
triage.triage_reason: WHOによりPHEICと宣言されており、致死率47.4%・5000例超・複数州への拡大・近隣国への越境リスクが確認されているため、フルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はDRC（イトゥリ州が震源地、キンシャサにも波及リスク）を主題としており、ウガンダ・南スーダン・中央アフリカ共和国は越境リスクとして言及されているのみで対象国リストにも含まれないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Число случаев заболевания лихорадкой Эбола в Конго превысило 5 тысяч
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of Ebola virus disease cases in the Congo has surpassed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: In the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ebola virus disease cases have surpassed 5,000, with 5,021 confirmed infections and 2,378 deaths reported by late July, making this the second-largest outbreak globally after the 2014-2016 West Africa epidemic. The current flare-up is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which there are no approved vaccines or therapies. Government data cited by AZERTAC and Reuters indicate that outbreak response measures have not contained spread. The 17th Ebola outbreak in the DRC highlights persistent challenges, including weak health infrastructure, community resistance, instability, and protests by responders that hinder case detection and the overall response.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでのエボラ出血熱感染者数が5000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCで5,021人の感染者、2,378人の死亡が確認され、史上2番目の規模のエボラ流行となっている。ワクチン・治療法未承認の系統であり、公衆衛生上重大な影響と国際的拡大のリスクが認められる。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれているが、記事サマリーではDRCのみが主題として扱われているため除外した。承認ワクチン・治療法のないBundibugyoエボラウイルスによる流行であり、既存の対応策で拡大を制御できていない点が特に懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: La minería de oro en el este del Congo dificulta la lucha contra el brote de ébola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Gold mining in eastern Congo hinders the fight against the Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, across six provinces and centered in Ituri, is the fastest-spreading and deadliest in the country’s history. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus is responsible; over 5,000 infections and more than 2,300 deaths, about 90% in Ituri. Transmission occurs via direct contact with bodily fluids and contaminated surfaces. Artisanal gold mining drives a highly mobile workforce, including many children, in illegal mines where basic prevention is absent, hindering surveillance and contact tracing. Health workers report difficulties tracing contacts as miners move between sites; two identified contacts disappeared after relocating. The response emphasizes miner education, community engagement, and case-tracking despite impassable roads and armed groups. Mercy Corps and MSF warn of expansion toward routes near the South Sudan border; no vaccines or specific treatments exist for Bundibugyo Ebola.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ東部の金採掘がエボラ出血熱の流行対策を困難にしている
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の大規模流行（感染5000人超、死亡2300人超）で、国際的拡大リスク（南スーダン国境付近への拡大懸念）と対応の困難さがあり、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当する。
triage.notes: 南スーダン国境付近への拡大懸念が記載されているが、南スーダンは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めない。ワクチン・特異的治療法が存在しないBundibugyo型エボラウイルスによる流行であり、武装勢力の存在や違法金採掘場の労働者の高い流動性が対策を困難にしている点が特筆される。

article.articleHeadline: Uganda: Ntungamo Lifts Foot-and-Mouth Disease Quarantine in Most Areas
article.articleSummary: Foot-and-Mouth Disease quarantine in Ntungamo District, Uganda, has been lifted in most areas after eight months of containment that began December 2025. Slaughter, transport and movement of animal products resume in disease-free zones; Ngoma, Rweikiriniro sub-counties and Rubaare Town Council remain quarantined where the disease persists on nine farms. District Veterinary Officer Dr Yake Basulila said outbreaks have been contained to the remaining nine farms. Lower local governments must gazette designated livestock loading points before movement resumes. Enforcement agencies will monitor compliance and penalize violators. Vaccination continues district-wide, with farmers charged Shs8,000; only three sub-counties remain quarantined out of 34. Stakeholders welcomed the lifting, noting adverse impacts on livelihoods, while warning that vaccination and monitoring will continue to eradicate FMD.

triage.headline_ja: ウガンダ:ントゥンガモ、ほとんどの地域で口蹄疫の検疫を解除
triage.triage_reason: 動物疾病（口蹄疫）に関する話題であり、対象国リストに含まれないウガンダでの発生。検疫は解除傾向にあり公衆衛生上の緊急性は認められない。
triage.notes: 発生地域にDRCが記載されているが、記事本文の主題はウガンダ・ントゥンガモ県の口蹄疫であり、DRCでの発生は確認できないため除外。動物疾病でヒトへの感染リスクの記載もない。

article.articleHeadline: 涉隱匿COVID-19疫情相關文件　美國佛奇前顧問認罪 - 國際新聞 - PChome Online 新聞
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Former Fauci adviser pleads guilty to concealing documents related to the COVID-19 pandemic - International News - PChome Online News
article.articleSummary: Former U.S. infectious disease adviser David Morens, 78, pleaded guilty in Greenbelt, Maryland federal court to one count of conspiracy to obstruct federal records related to the COVID-19 pandemic. Morens, who served as a senior official at the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) during the pandemic, admitted conspiring to evade public-records requests for documents tied to COVID-19 research funding. Prosecutors said the case centers on the NIH decision to cancel a bat coronavirus research grant after allegations the work originated at the Wuhan Institute of Virology. The grant recipient allegedly provided portions of funds via sub-awards to Wuhan labs. Morens reportedly helped seek to restore the grant and counter lab-origin theories, and, anticipating FOIA requests, used his private email instead of his government account. Sentencing is set for November 12, 2026; maximum penalty five years.

triage.headline_ja: COVID-19疫情関連文書の隠蔽に関与か　米ファウチ氏の元顧問が罪を認める
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は公文書隠蔽に関する司法手続きに関する内容であり、新規の感染症発生や公衆衛生上のリスクに関する情報ではないため、シグナルとして取り上げる必要はない。
triage.notes: 記事は過去のCOVID-19起源調査に関連する司法・行政上のスキャンダル報道であり、現在進行中の感染症発生事例ではない。中国（武漢）は文脈上言及されるが、現行の発生地域ではないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: DOH on guard vs potential leptospirosis surge
article.articleSummary: Facing Habagat-induced floods and heavy rains, the Department of Health (DOH) raised Code White Alert in affected parts of the Philippines and warned of a potential leptospirosis surge. The DOH is monitoring cases as flooding and rainfall continue. About 3.1 million doxycycline capsules have been placed on standby at the DOH Central Office and 17 Centers for Health Development to support hospitals and local government units. PhilHealth already maintains a leptospirosis benefit package for eligible patients. Leptospirosis is a bacterial disease spread through contact with water or soil contaminated with the urine of infected animals. Symptoms include high fever, severe headache, chills, muscle pain, vomiting, jaundice, red eyes, abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rash. More than 3,000 cases have been reported nationwide this year; 3,440 cases as of August 8, 2026, about 35% lower than 5,318 in the same period last year.

triage.headline_ja: DOH、レプトスピラ症の急増可能性に対し警戒を強化
triage.triage_reason: フィリピンで季節性の洪水に伴うレプトスピラ症の“急増可能性”についてDOHが予防的警戒を発したものだが、実際の症例数は前年同期より35%減少しており、現時点で異常な増加や国際的拡大の兆候はないため、続報を注視する。
triage.notes: レプトスピラ症はフィリピンで毎年雨季（Habagat）に発生する季節性の風土病であり、DOHは洪水に備え予防的にコード・ホワイト警戒を発令し、抗生剤（ドキシサイクリン）を配備している。現状の症例数（2026年8月8日時点で3,440件）は前年同期（5,318件）より約35%減少しており、急増の実態は確認されていない。国際的拡大やヒト-ヒト感染のリスクは低く、国内の医療体制（PhilHealthの給付制度含む）で対応可能とみられる。今後の洪水状況や症例数の推移を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Actualité | Ebola : un " enseignement à distance léger " prévu dans 18 zones de santé à haut risque | mediacongo.net
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: News | Ebola: a light-distance-learning program planned in 18 high-risk health zones | mediacongo.net
article.articleSummary: In the Democratic Republic of Congo, as Ebola continues to affect several provinces, authorities announced a differentiated school return for 2026-2027 starting Sept 1, focusing on 18 health zones deemed high-risk. To curb transmission, the government will implement a light-distance learning program that requires no internet or devices: printed worksheets based on core curricula will be distributed to students, supplemented by radio educational broadcasts. Schools will not be fully closed; teachers will monitor students, and parents can retrieve materials periodically via a zoned system. The initial pilot lasts four weeks, after which health and education conditions will be reassessed to adjust modalities according to epidemic evolution. As of August 18, more than 5,000 confirmed Ebola cases and over 2,300 deaths are reported across five provinces involved in the response.

article.articleHeadline: Бројот случаи на ебола во Конго надминаа 5.000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of Ebola cases in Congo surpassed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of Congo reports Ebola cases have surpassed 5,000, with the Institute of Public Health recording 5,021 cases and 2,378 deaths by the latest update, marking the 17th Ebola outbreak in the country and the largest by cases in its history as of late July. The outbreak involves the Bundibugyo strain, for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments. The epidemic began May 15 and has intensified amid weak health infrastructure, local resistance, ongoing instability, and protests by health workers, all hampering detection and containment efforts. Globally, it ranks as the second-worst outbreak by both cases and deaths, behind West Africa's 2014-2016 epidemic. Ongoing transmission underscores the need for intensified public health measures in the region.

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo Ebola confirmed cases top 5,000
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has surpassed 5,000 confirmed cases and more than 2,320 deaths as of Aug 17, 2026, across six provinces—Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, Bas-Uele and Tshopo. The transmission is driven by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, with case fatality ratio near 50% and the outbreak described by the Africa CDC as the fastest-growing on record and the deadliest in DRC history. Officials say the region is facing roughly one death every 30 minutes, and unless its trajectory is urgently reversed, it risks becoming the deadliest Ebola outbreak globally. The DRC declared the outbreak on May 15. Uganda ended its Bundibugyo outbreak on July 28, illustrating that rapid, community-centered public health measures can contain transmission.

diseases.name: Human Infection with Swine Influenza A H1N2

article.articleHeadline: China reports first human swine influenza A(H1N2)v case, doctor explains if Indians should be concerned - India TV News
article.articleSummary: China’s first human case of swine-origin influenza A(H1N2)v was detected in a healthy boy aged 2 years 10 months in China. He developed recurrent fever and paroxysmal cough, progressed to bronchopneumonia and infectious fever, and was hospitalised. Laboratory testing detected influenza A, with sputum culture suggesting Haemophilus influenzae co-infection; chest CT showed increased, blurred pulmonary markings. He received cefoperazone-sulbactam, oseltamivir, ambroxol and nebulised budesonide, and was discharged after complete recovery. Dr Prateek Kadian of Aastha Hospital (New Delhi) said the case warrants monitoring but does not imply high risk for Indians without pig contact; human-to-human spread remains the key unknown. Surveillance and timely reporting are essential, especially for those with occupational pig exposure. Symptoms to watch after pig exposure include fever, cough, sore throat, runny nose, headache, body aches, fatigue, and occasional GI symptoms. Precautions: hygiene, protective gear, avoid contact with visibly ill animals, and handwashing; no need for panic.

article.articleHeadline: West Nile, morto a 84 anni: così si è sviluppata la malattia di Lorenzo Corradin
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: West Nile virus, died at 84: how Lorenzo Corradin's illness developed.
article.articleSummary: West Nile virus infection proved fatal for Lorenzo Corradin, 84, of Presina di Piazzola sul Brenta, Veneto, the first West Nile death recorded there in the 2026 Veneto summer. On August 6 he developed high fever with vomiting and diarrhea, was admitted to Cittadella hospital and diagnosed with West Nile infection, then moved to Neurology for treatment. Despite care, he died on August 16, 2026. Laboratory exams during hospitalization confirmed West Nile as the cause; investigators said the incubation period was at least two weeks. Corradin had spent time outdoors in gardens and on his allotment before symptoms. No further linked cases were reported in Presina, and no district-wide disinfestation was required. A July Padova case involved a man who had returned from Thailand and recovered. In 2025, three cases were registered in Ulss 6 Euganea; 2022 saw a peak in regional West Nile activity.

article.articleHeadline: 'Far from under control' - WHO warns of rapid Ebola spread in DR Congo
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-19, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo remains far from under control, per WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus. Declared May 15, this is the 17th Ebola epidemic in DRC, with more than 2,300 deaths among nearly 5,000 cases. Transmission continues at an unprecedented pace and likely began weeks before official identification. Northern and eastern DRC are hardest hit, where weak infrastructure, insecurity, and armed-group activity hinder access to affected communities. The crisis is fueled by insecurity, displacement, and intense population movement along roads, rivers and mining routes, keeping national and international spread risk high. WHO will issue additional recommendations to strengthen efforts in identifying and interrupting transmission chains and to prevent cross-border spread.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RD Congo : l'OMS met en garde contre un risque élevé de propagation internationale
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in DR Congo: WHO warns of a high risk of international spread.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo remains uncontrolled, with a high risk of international spread. Since the May 15 declaration of the 17th outbreak, the virus has spread across six provinces and 55 health zones, infecting nearly 5,000 people and causing more than 2,300 deaths. WHO warns the outbreak is the second-largest on record and is progressing faster than prior epidemics, fueled by insecurity, population movement, and cross-border movement along roads, rivers, and mining routes. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus causes fever and headaches early, often delaying diagnosis; no licensed vaccine or treatment exists, though clinical trials are underway and the WHO has urged organizing an Ervebo vaccine trial. Response has been criticized for slowness, with deaths occurring before contacts are identified and ambulances vandalized in Ituri. The EU has provided €2.5 million for testing; no imported/exported cases are described.

article.articleHeadline: 規避法規全認了！美國佛奇前顧問涉隱匿COVID-19疫情相關文件
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Fully admits to evading regulations! Former Fauci adviser implicated in concealing COVID-19 pandemic-related documents.
article.articleSummary: David Morens, a 78-year-old former adviser to Anthony Fauci and senior official at the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) during the COVID-19 era, pleaded guilty in Greenbelt, Maryland federal court to conspiring to obstruct the Public Records Act by concealing government documents related to COVID-19 research funding. Charged in April, Morens faces up to five years in prison when sentenced on November 12. Prosecutors say his plea centers on NIH’s cancellation of a bat coronavirus research grant, tied to the Wuhan Institute of Virology, with funds allegedly routed via subgrants to the Wuhan lab. Morens agreed to help restore the grant and disputed the lab-origin theory of COVID-19. He admitted using a private email account to contact colleagues, anticipating Freedom of Information Act requests, instead of his government email.

triage.headline_ja: 規避法規全認了！米国ファウチ前顧問がCOVID-19疫情関連文書の隠匿に関与
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は米国政府関係者による研究資金・文書隠匿に関する司法手続きの報道であり、公衆衛生上の新たな感染症発生や拡大リスクを示す内容ではない。
triage.notes: 本記事はCOVID-19の起源調査・研究資金隠匿に関する米国内の法的措置についての報道であり、中国（武漢）は過去の研究資金提供先として言及されているのみで、現在進行中の感染症発生事象ではないため対象国に含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Pune Hospitals Report Rise in Dengue, Chikungunya Symptoms Amid Monsoon
article.articleSummary: As of 19 August 2026, Pune hospitals report a rise in dengue- and chikungunya-like illnesses linked to monsoon conditions favorable to Aedes breeding in stagnant water and high humidity. The Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) intensified anti-larval operations and fogging in identified mosquito-breeding hotspots, while residents are urged to remove standing water from balconies, terraces, containers, and other open spaces, and to keep stored water properly covered. Symptoms prompting medical care include fever, body ache, weakness; dengue warning signs include persistent vomiting, abdominal pain, bleeding, or unusual drowsiness or restlessness. Chikungunya presents with intense joint pain that can persist after fever resolves, with closer monitoring advised for infants, pregnant women, and those with underlying conditions. Early testing and medical consultation are emphasized to distinguish mosquito-borne infections from other seasonal illnesses and reduce complications. Use mosquito nets, repellents, and stay hydrated during fever; report potential breeding sites to field teams.

article.articleHeadline: RDC : plus de 5 000 cas d'Ebola, l'épidémie devient la plus grave de l'histoire du pays - Tunisie Numerique
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: More than 5,000 Ebola cases, the outbreak becomes the most severe in the country's history - Tunisie Numerique
article.articleSummary: DRC reports 5,021 cumulative Ebola cases and 2,378 deaths by the end of July, marking the 17th Ebola outbreak in the country and the largest by infections in its history. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain; there is no vaccine or approved treatment specifically for this variant. It ranks as the second-deadliest Ebola outbreak globally, behind West Africa's 2014–2016 epidemic. Since the official outbreak announcement on May 15, transmission accelerated amid fragile health infrastructure, portions of the population resisting preventive measures, and ongoing regional instability. Protests involving some frontline personnel hindered field operations, delaying rapid case identification and patient care. Authorities warn that current measures have not contained the spread and stress the need to strengthen surveillance, testing, and care capacity to prevent further transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Le nombre de cas d'Ebola en RDC dépasse les 5.000, selon des données
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of Ebola cases in the DRC exceeds 5,000, according to data.
article.articleSummary: Ebola is surging in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). As of Aug 19, 2026, government data show 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths, marking the 17th DRC outbreak and its largest by case count since late July. The outbreak ranks as the second-deadliest globally, behind the 2014–2016 West Africa Ebola epidemic. It is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no licensed vaccine or approved treatment. Health authorities warn that current control measures may be insufficient to curb transmission as the situation remains ongoing. Data come from the Public Health Institute, with Reuters reporting on the update. This highlights the severe and continuing threat of the Ebola outbreak in the DRC and its global ranking among major Ebola events.

article.articleHeadline: Congo´s Ebola outbreak reaches 5,000 cases as it outpaces response...

The data show transmission accelerating about three times faster than the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic, which killed over 11,000. The report emphasizes the extreme containment challenges in harsh conditions and ongoing rapid spread. The article does not specify laboratory confirmation details or infection sources, and it does not mention imported or exported cases.

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola outbreak reaches 5,000 cases as it outpaces response efforts at unprecedented speed
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Congo's remote Bunia region has reached 5,021 cases and 2,378 deaths, according to the Congo Ministry of Health as of Aug. 16, 2026. Responders warn transmission is accelerating at an unprecedented pace, outstripping containment efforts in one of the country's most challenging settings shaped by insecurity, displacement, and intense population movement. The outbreak is spreading about three times faster than the 2014–2016 West Africa Ebola epidemic, which killed more than 11,000 people. The article emphasizes the severity of conditions hindering response but does not detail laboratory confirmation methods or the precise infection source. The figures indicate ongoing, explosive transmission in a hard-to-reach region, underscoring the need for intensified public health measures and security considerations to curb the outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱、感染者5,000人に達し、前例のない速さで対応能力を上回る
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱が5,021例・死亡2,378例に達し、2014-16年西アフリカ流行の3倍の速度で拡大しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: 記事はコンゴ・ブニア地域での爆発的なエボラ流行を報告。治安不安・人口移動により対応が困難化しており、致死率約47%と極めて高い。アンゴラは発生地域リストに含まれているが記事本文では言及されておらず、対象国リストにも含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Association between lumpy skin disease outbreaks in cattle and climatological variables, Thailand
article.articleSummary: Lumpy skin disease (LSD) outbreaks in Thailand from 2021–2024 affected 69 of 77 provinces, with 290 beef cattle farms and 15 dairy farms affected. Beef mortality peaked in the northeastern region (0.13%), followed by central (0.02%), northern (0.017%), western (0.012%), eastern (0.007%), and southern (0.003%). In dairy cattle, mortality was highest in the northern region (0.03%), then western (0.008%), central (0.004%), and northeast (0.0036%). Rainy seasons saw higher mortalities for beef, and higher morbidity, attack rate, and mortality for dairy than summer/winter. Climate data show 2024 max temperature 33.70±2.73°C, rising since 2021; THI increased from 79.06 to 80.43, with regional THI >78 indicating heat stress. Beef morbidity correlated with humidity (r=-0.31), T-min (r=0.38) and T-max (r=0.35); dairy morbidity correlated strongly with T-max (r=0.60). These associations inform LSD prevention and control strategies in Thailand.

triage.headline_ja: タイにおける牛のランピースキン病発生と気候変動要因との関連性
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は2021〜2024年のタイでの牛ランピースキン病(LSD)発生に関する気候要因との相関を分析した学術研究であり、新規発生や人への感染リスクを示すものではない。LSDは牛の疾患でヒトへの感染性はなく、公衆衛生上の緊急性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: DRK: liczba przypadków wirusa ebola przekroczyła pięć tysięcy
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRK: the number of Ebola virus cases has exceeded five thousand.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-19, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths, recorded over the past three months, making it the deadliest epidemic in the country’s history. Kinshasa notes all fatalities occurred within three months, while 2018–2020 saw 2,299 deaths among 3,381 infections. AFP reports the outbreak has spread to six provinces, primarily in the north and east, where weak healthcare infrastructure and armed-group activity hinder response. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the outbreak is far from stabilization. Ebola causes severe fever and hemorrhagic symptoms. Since its discovery in 1976, Ebola has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa. The figures reflect data from the DR Congo Public Health Institute, with coverage by Reuters and AFP.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo: What's going on and why is the outbreak so alarming?
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo strain Ebola outbreak in eastern DRC (Ituri, Bunia) has 5,021 cases and 2,378 deaths as of Aug. 16, CFR 47.4%. Formally declared in May, the outbreak centers near the South Sudan/Uganda border; Uganda reported cases but declared Ebola-free in July. The first suspected case was a health worker in Bunia (April 24). This is the DRC’s 17th outbreak; the Bundibugyo strain currently has no vaccine or treatment, though two vaccine trials have begun. The outbreak is spreading faster than any prior Ebola outbreak. Response challenges include armed conflict, mass displacement, cross-border movement, and distrust, with many patients avoiding care. Testing, contact tracing, safe funerals, and isolation are essential. WHO is scaling up with 100 additional epidemiologists and 400 beds; calls for more international support, notably from Canada.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC : au-delà des 5 000 cas, une riposte encore désordonnée
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC: beyond 5,000 cases, a still disorganized response.
article.articleSummary: DRC reports 5,021 confirmed Ebola cases and 2,378 deaths as of Aug 18, 2026, with six provinces affected and Ituri as the epicenter. The outbreak extends to Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Tshopo and Bas-Uélé, driven by insecurity, population mobility, and cross-border/mining activity. Uganda’s Bundibugyo outbreak ended July 28 after 42 days of surveillance, with 20 cases (15 imported), 18 recoveries, 2 deaths, and no community transmission. Bundibugyo, a rarer species, lacks an approved vaccine; Ervebo (Zaïre Ebola vaccine) was initially not recommended but later authorized for use, alongside remdesivir. Two Bundibugyo-specific vaccines entered Phase I (Oxford/Serum Institute; Moderna mRNA candidate), with trials starting July 24 (UK) and the PARTNERS trial ongoing in Ituri. Operational gaps include 75% contact tracing (vs 95% target) and 139% bed occupancy at Nord-Kivu treatment centers; unpaid health workers contribute to response disruptions.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ:5,000例を超え、対応は依然として混乱

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RD Congo : l'OMS met en garde contre un risque élevé de propagation internationale
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in DR Congo: WHO warns of a high risk of international spread.
article.articleSummary: On 19 August 2026, the World Health Organization warns that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) poses a high risk of international spread. Declared on 15 May as the 17th Ebola outbreak, it affects six provinces and 55 health zones in North and East DRC, with nearly 5,000 infections and over 2,300 deaths reported. It is described as the second-largest Ebola outbreak ever, progressing faster than the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic, fueled by insecurity, population movement, and routes along roads, rivers, and mining sites. Ebola transmission occurs via contact with bodily fluids; early symptoms include fever and headaches, delaying diagnosis. No licensed vaccine or treatment exists; clinical trials are underway, with discussions to trial Ervebo. Response challenges include slow coordination and community distrust; some patients die before being listed in contact tracing. The EU has allocated €2.5 million for testing, while the OMS intensifies decentralized response, notably involving community-based transport networks; Ituri is a focal area.

article.articleHeadline: Epidemia di ébola ta "leu for di bou kòntròl" - èxtra
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola Epidemic Is "Out of Control" - Extra
article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is described as 'out of control' by WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, with a high risk of international spread. The outbreak, attributed to Bundibugyo ebolavirus, is centered in the northern and eastern regions, with more than 5,000 laboratory-confirmed cases and over 2,300 deaths. Congo declared the outbreak on May 15 after several weeks of delay, as health systems grapple with weak governance and severely limited health infrastructure. The WHO Emergency Committee has met twice since May 17 to declare a Public Health Emergency of International Concern and to signal elevated international alerts. There is currently no licensed vaccine or specific treatment for Bundibugyo ebolavirus, though multiple development efforts aim to halt transmission, highlighting ongoing global concern about potential spread to other countries.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola-Ausbruch noch lange nicht unter Kontrolle
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak still far from under control.
article.articleSummary: In the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Ebola outbreak has surpassed 5,000 cases and about 2,500 deaths in roughly 100 days since it was announced in mid-May 2026. WHO Chief Tedros warns the epidemic is far from under control and could become Africa’s largest Ebola outbreak; Africa CDC and WHO fear it may exceed the continent’s previous worst (2014–2015 West Africa, >11,000 deaths). Maximilian Gertler of Charité/MSF reports over 2,000 deaths since the outbreak began; many cases are not registered as contacts, signaling substantial undercount. Transmission remains via contact with body fluids; early symptoms are non-specific (fever, malaise, headaches, body pains). Initially confined to Ituri, the outbreak now affects six provinces (Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, Tshopo, among others). MSF operates seven treatment centers with ~430 beds and >1,400 staff. Access is hampered by armed conflict and border/flight restrictions; the upcoming rainy season risks spikes in malaria, cholera, measles, and respiratory infections.

article.articleHeadline: School closed for 15 days after jaundice outbreak in Khordha
article.articleSummary: Jaundice outbreak at Mugamanda Ashram School in Bolagada, Khordha district, Odisha, affects more than 600 students (350 living in hostels). The school closed for 15 days as a precaution. Blood tests were conducted on several ill students, who were sent home. Preliminary investigations point to contaminated water as the likely source. Bolagarh health committee and education authorities visited the campus to assess the situation, while locals expressed dissatisfaction over the handling of water supply and facilities review. No details on confirmed cases, deaths, or laboratory confirmation are provided. The incident highlights water-safety concerns for school facilities in the Bolagada area of Khordha.

triage.notes: 確定症例数・死亡例・検査結果の詳細は不明。原因は汚染水と推定されているが確定診断（A型肝炎等）は記事内で明示されていない。地域住民の不満が報じられており社会的関心は一定程度存在するが、国際的拡大や渡航制限の懸念はない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola-Ausbruch noch lange nicht unter Kontrolle
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak still far from under control.
article.articleSummary: As of 19 August 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ebola outbreak—the country’s 17th—remains far from under control. Officially announced in mid-May in Ituri, experts believe transmission likely began earlier in the year, with nonspecific early symptoms delaying detection in areas lacking rapid lab testing. The outbreak has spread to six provinces; urban centers like Bunia have expanded treatment and labs, while remote, insecure regions face limited access. Médecins Sans Frontières reports about 430 beds and more than 1,400 staff across Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, and Tshopo, with a new center under construction in Tshopo. Challenges include ongoing armed conflict, border/air restrictions delaying supplies, and population fear of isolation. The upcoming rainy season could elevate malaria, cholera, measles, and other illnesses, complicating Ebola differentiation. Cases have appeared in Kisangani (Tshopo), raising concerns about spread to Kinshasa (~17 million residents); training and preparedness measures are ongoing.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱の流行、依然として制御下になし
triage.triage_reason: IHR4基準中4件、WPRO5基準中5件が該当し、DRCの第17次エボラ流行が6州に拡大、武装勢力による治安悪化・国境/空路制限・大都市キンシャサへの拡大リスクなど国際的関心が高い深刻な事例であるため。
triage.notes: DRCの第17次エボラ流行。イツリ、北キブ、南キブ、ツショポなど6州に拡大し、キサンガニでの感染確認によりキンシャサ（人口約1700万）への拡大が懸念されている。武装勢力による治安不安、国境・空路の制限、雨季によるマラリア・コレラ・麻疹との鑑別困難などの複合的リスクが存在し、MSFなど国際機関が対応中。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola cases top 5,000 as outbreak spreads in DR Congo
article.articleSummary: Kinshasa, DR Congo — As of Aug 19, 2026, Ebola cases have surpassed 5,000, with 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths. The Bundibugyo strain is circulating, and there are no approved treatments or vaccines specifically for this strain. Transmission occurs through direct contact with bodily fluids of an infected person, including those who have died. Reported symptoms include fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and in severe cases, internal and external bleeding. The public health institute provided the latest epidemiological update; Reuters cited the figures. Health authorities continue to monitor the outbreak and implement containment measures to curb transmission.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱の感染拡大、症例数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱が5,000例超・死亡2,378例に達し、承認された治療法・ワクチンがないBundibugyo株が拡大している重大な公衆衛生事象であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: 致死率約47%（2,378/5,021）と高く、Bundibugyo株には承認済み治療薬・ワクチンがないため、国際的な支援と監視が必要とされる。

article.articleHeadline: Najveća epidemija ebole u istoriji Konga: Više od 5.000 potvrđenih slučajeva
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The largest Ebola epidemic in Congo's history: More than 5,000 confirmed cases.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo's 17th Ebola outbreak has surpassed 5,000 confirmed cases, with 2,378 deaths reported in the latest government tally. The outbreak, the largest in the country’s history and the second-worst globally after 2014–2016 West Africa, is caused by the Bundibugyo Ebola strain, for which no licensed vaccines or therapies exist. Transmission has accelerated since it was declared on May 15, amid weak health infrastructure, local resistance to control measures, instability, and protests by health workers involved in containment. The National Institute of Public Health reports 5,021 cases in the current situation update, highlighting ongoing challenges in detection and suppression. The article does not provide details on imported or exported cases.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴにおける史上最大のエボラ流行：確認症例数5,000人超
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大規模のエボラ流行（5,000例超、死者2,378人）が発生し、承認済みワクチン・治療法が存在しないバンディブギョ株が原因であり、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と異常性からIHR基準を2つ以上満たす。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれているが、記事サマリーではDRC国内の流行のみが言及されており、Angolaへの拡大については記載がないため除外した。国際的拡大リスクや渡航・貿易制限については記事に情報がなく不明とした。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola im Kongo: Ebola-Ausbruch noch lange nicht unter Kontrolle
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the Congo: Ebola outbreak far from being under control.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has spread from Ituri in the northeast to six provinces, with Bunia (Ituri capital) and Kisangani (Tshopo) among affected hubs. Doctors Without Borders operates seven treatment centers and numerous isolation units, totaling about 430 beds and over 1,400 staff across Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, and Tshopo. Rural areas lack rapid diagnostics, delaying case detection and isolation. Armed groups, insecurity, and border/air travel restrictions hinder aid delivery and logistics. The coming rainy season risks surges of malaria, cholera, measles, and respiratory infections, complicating Ebola recognition. Fear of isolation drives families to hide patients or seek traditional healers, while hunger raises competing priorities. Last week Ebola cases appeared in Tshopo; Kinshasa could face spillover via regular Congo River ship routes from Kisangani. Training is underway to prepare for such a scenario.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱：エボラ流行はまだ制御下にない
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ流行が6州に拡大し、キンシャサへの流入リスクや治安不安による対応の困難さが報告されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため、フルリスク評価が必要と判断。
triage.notes: 記事はエボラ流行が主題で、Ituri・North Kivu・South Kivu・Tshopoなど6州に拡大、Kinshasaへの河川経由の流入リスクも指摘。マラリア・コレラ・麻疹は雨季による合併リスクとして言及されているが、主要イベントはエボラである。武装勢力による治安悪化と渡航制限が既に発生しており、国際支援（MSF）が展開中。

article.articleHeadline: Над 5.000 заболени од ебола во Конго
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Over 5,000 people infected with Ebola in Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 5,000 confirmed cases, with the Institute of Public Health reporting 5,021 cases and 2,378 deaths. A World Health Organization representative, Tierno Baldé, said the epidemic could be brought under control within three months if the necessary resources are provided. The update follows earlier WHO projections of containment within 90 days, but signs of deterioration have emerged as transmission has spread into a sixth province. The data underscore the ongoing severity of the outbreak and the need for sustained international support to bolster response efforts and resources. Date of report: 2026-08-19.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ感染者5,000人超
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRCで5,000例以上・死亡2,378例に達し、6県目への拡大や国際支援の必要性が明記されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: 致死率は約47%と高く、感染が6州目に拡大している点、WHOが資源提供による制御見通しを示している点から継続的な監視とフルRRAが必要。

article.articleHeadline: Огнището се разраства: Случаите на ебола в Конго надхвърлиха 5000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The outbreak is spreading: Ebola cases in the Congo surpassed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there are no approved vaccines or specific treatments. Confirmed cases have risen beyond 5,000, with the latest government data cited by Reuters showing 5,021 cases. The weekend death toll reached 2,378, surpassing the previous record from the 2018–2020 outbreak. Declared on May 15, the current outbreak is the 17th in the DRC and, by the end of July, the largest in the country’s history by both case counts and deaths. As of the latest situation report, the outbreak remains among the world’s worst, second only to West Africa’s 2014–2016 epidemic. Contributing factors include weak health infrastructure, community resistance, instability, and protests by workers involved in outbreak response that impede identification and treatment of cases.

triage.headline_ja: 拡大する感染爆発：コンゴのエボラ感染者数が5000人を超えた
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ（ブンディブジョ株）流行が同国史上最大規模となり、承認済みワクチン・治療法が存在しない中で死者数が過去最多を更新しているため、フルリスク評価が必要と判断。
triage.notes: BluedotではAngolaも発生地域として付与されているが、記事サマリー本文ではAngolaへの拡大について言及がないため、verified_locationsから除外した。ブンディブジョ株には承認済みワクチン・特効薬がなく、コミュニティの抵抗や治安不安が対応を妨げている点が特に懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: El ébola se combate con motos en el Congo: así colaboran contra el virus los motoristas
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola is fought with motorcycles in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: this is how motorcyclists are helping against the virus.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo ebolavirus Ebola outbreak in Ituri province, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), declared May 2026. It marks the 17th Ebola outbreak in the DRC since 1976, with the WHO declaring a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. As of August 19, 2026, confirmed cases exceed 5,000 and deaths exceed 2,300 (case fatality around 46%). The WHO is enlisting motorbike taxi drivers as frontline surveillance and response partners to accelerate detection, contact tracing, and patient referrals, leveraging their access to communities and trust. Drivers will report suspected cases, coordinate with surveillance teams, and help transport patients to care, while receiving infection prevention training (hand hygiene, disinfection). Risks to drivers exist but preventive measures are in place. The response also adds about 100 epidemiologists, 500 local staff, and 400 additional hospital beds. Motorcycles have historically aided surveillance in hard‑to‑reach areas.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラと戦うバイクタクシー：ウイルスに対抗するモトタクシー運転手たちの協力
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEICを宣言した大規模エボラ流行（症例5000超、死亡2300超、致死率約46%）であり、IHR基準の複数に該当し社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: WHOがPHEICを宣言済みの大規模エボラ流行であり、既にフルRRA相当の事案。本記事は対応策（バイクタクシー活用）に関する続報。

article.articleHeadline: El brote de ébola en Congo supera los 5.000 casos y se propaga a un ritmo alarmante
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 cases and is spreading at an alarming rate.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease has reached 5,021 cases and 2,378 deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, according to the Ministry of Health, with figures as of last Sunday. The outbreak centers on Bunia, in one of the country’s most remote regions, where response teams warn that transmission is accelerating at an unprecedented pace amid insecurity, displacement, and heavy population movement. Health authorities characterize this outbreak as more lethal and contagious than any prior in history, with a pace of spread roughly three times faster than the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic, which claimed over 11,000 lives. The current trajectory poses a severe challenge for containment and underscores ongoing risk in the affected areas.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行、5,000例を超え驚異的な速さで拡大
triage.triage_reason: DRCで5,000例超・死者2,378人規模のエボラ流行が、過去最悪の致死率・伝播速度で拡大しており、IHR基準の複数(深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際拡大リスク)に該当するためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれるが記事本文はDRC(ブニア中心)のみが主題であり、Angolaでの発生は記載されていないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Epidémie d'Ebola : un mort toutes les 30 secondes
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak: one death every 30 seconds.
article.articleSummary: DRC's Ebola outbreak is the deadliest in the country's history, with 2,325 deaths among 4,945 confirmed cases over three months as of 17 August 2026. The epidemic has spread to 55 health zones across six provinces in the north and east, driven by the Bundibugyo variant, for which no licensed vaccine or specific treatment exists. The UN and WHO call it the fastest, most lethal outbreak yet, with about one death every 30 minutes and rapid case increases in hard-hit areas. On the ground, 730 patients are in isolation or hospitalized, 1,040 have recovered (about 30 in the last 24 hours), and contact tracing is at 85%. Vaccines in trials include two Bundibugyo-targeted candidates in Phase 1; Zaïre vaccine shows potential cross-protection in animals, and WHO has urged including it in Phase 3 trials, though human efficacy remains unproven. Response emphasizes surveillance, care, and community engagement.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱流行：30秒に1人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最悪規模のエボラ流行（致死率約47%、6州55保健区に拡大）が発生し、ワクチン未承認のBundibugyo株が原因であり、IHR基準の複数（重大な公衆衛生影響・異常性・国際拡大リスク）に該当するため、フルRRAへ進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: WHO・国連が史上最も致死的かつ急速な流行と評価。ライセンス済みワクチン・特効薬が存在せず、Bundibugyo株に対する臨床試験も未確立で、国際的な支援・介入が急務。

article.articleHeadline: बदलते मौसम में फ्लू को हल्के में न ले, बीमारी में गलती से भी ना करे ये काम | Don't take the flu lightly during the changing weather; avoid making these mistakes while ill.
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Don't take the flu lightly during the changing weather; don't do these things even by mistake when you're ill.
article.articleSummary: Influenza (flu) is a viral infection of the nose, throat, and lungs. In New Delhi, as weather changes, flu symptoms rise. Typical signs include sudden fever, cough, sore throat, headache, body aches, and fatigue, with reduced appetite. Most recover with rest, fluids, and proper nutrition, but see a doctor if fever is very high, breathing trouble, chest pain, severe weakness, or condition worsens. Dehydration is common, so sip water, soups, and other fluids; avoid relying on tea or coffee. Rest and adequate sleep support recovery; limit activity and maintain distance to reduce spread; cover mouth/nose when coughing or sneezing and practice hand hygiene. Diet should include protein (lentils, eggs, dairy), fruits, vegetables, and light meals like khichdi or porridge. Antibiotics are not routinely needed for flu; do not self-prescribe. Special care for children, the elderly, pregnant women, and those with comorbidities.

triage.headline_ja: 季節の変わり目にインフルエンザを軽視しないで、病気の際にこれらのことをしないよう注意
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザに関する一般的な健康啓発記事であり、異常な流行や公衆衛生上の重大な懸念を示す情報は含まれていない。
triage.notes: 季節変化に伴う一般的なインフルエンザ予防・対処に関する啓発記事であり、特定の発生や集団感染についての報告ではない。

article.articleHeadline: El ébola ha vuelto...y el fondo de ayuda del FMI está vacío
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola has returned... and the IMF's aid fund is empty.
article.articleSummary: Ebola has returned in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with more than 2,000 deaths confirmed as of 2026-08-19, prompting renewed concern about health-finance strain. The UNDP estimates the outbreak could push nearly a million people into poverty. The IMF's Catastrophe Debt Relief Fund (FFADC), expanded into the Catastrophe Relief and Containment Trust (FFACC) after Ebola in 2014, is now nearly exhausted due to COVID-19, holding only about $120 million for debt relief. DRC owes the IMF over $3 billion and faces rising needs amid higher oil prices and slower growth. A proposed remedy: sell roughly 10% of the IMF's gold reserves—about 9.05 million ounces—at current prices to seed a permanent endowment of $35.8 billion. A 3% return would yield over $1 billion annually, funding FFACC and all concessional lending facilities indefinitely and reducing reliance on donor replenishments.

triage.headline_ja: エボラが再来...そしてIMFの支援基金は空っぽ
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラによる2,000人以上の死亡が確認されており、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と国際的な財政・支援ニーズが示されているためフルRRAへの移行が適切。
triage.notes: 記事は主にIMFの財政支援スキームに関する論評記事であり、エボラの疫学的詳細（発生地域内の分布、症例数、ヒト-ヒト感染状況等）は限定的。死亡者数2,000人以上という記述の信頼性・出典が不明確なため、フルRRAでの確認が必要。COVID-19は文脈上の言及のみで主要疾病ではない。

article.articleHeadline: தென்காசி அருகே டெங்கு காய்ச்சலுக்கு மேலும் ஒரு பெண் பலியானதால் அதிர்ச்சி
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Shocking: another woman dies of dengue fever near Tenkasi.
article.articleSummary: Near Tenkasi district, in a Sri Lankan Tamil refugee camp at Kadayanallur taluk, Poganalur, more than 150 families have lived there for 35 years. Over the past month dengue fever cases have surged in the area. In that period, more than 50 people contracted a fever described as mysterious and were hospitalized. The article's title notes the death of another woman from dengue fever nearby. No laboratory confirmation details, infection source, or information on imported/exported cases are provided. The report underscores a potential dengue outbreak in this refugee camp setting and signals an urgent need for public health response, clinical management, and vector-control measures.

triage.headline_ja: テンカーシ近郊でデング熱により別の女性が死亡し衝撃
triage.triage_reason: スリランカ系タミル難民キャンプでデング熱による死亡例と50人超の発熱患者が報告されているが、検査確認や規模の詳細が不明であり、地域限定の風土病的流行との見方もあるため続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 難民キャンプという特殊な居住環境での集団発生であり、検査確認情報がないため症例の実態（デング熱か他の熱性疾患か）が不明確。地域の公衆衛生対応能力に関する情報も不足している。

article.articleHeadline: Έμπολα: Τα κρούσματα στη Λαϊκή Δημοκρατία του Κονγκό ξεπέρασαν τα 5.000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: The cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpassed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo's 17th Ebola outbreak, the largest in the country by case count, now exceeds 5,000 confirmed cases. As of August 19, 2026, authorities report 5,021 cases and 2,378 deaths. The outbreak is caused by Ebola virus of Bundibugyo strain, for which there are no licensed vaccines or therapies. Declared on May 15, the outbreak has intensified, with control efforts hampered by weak health infrastructure, community resistance, insecurity, and strikes by workers responding to the outbreak, hindering case detection and management. The current outbreak ranks as the second-worst globally, behind the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic in both cases and deaths, per the public health institute. The report notes ongoing challenges in containment in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ:コンゴ民主共和国での症例数が5,000人を超えた
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大規模(5,021例、死亡2,378例)のエボラ流行が続いており、ワクチン・治療薬未承認の株で、対策が治安悪化・スト等で難航しているため深刻な公衆衛生上の脅威であり国際的拡大リスクもある。
