article.articleHeadline: DRK: Liczba przypadków wirusa ebola przekroczyła 5 tysięcy
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRK: The number of Ebola virus cases has surpassed five thousand.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has surpassed 5,000 confirmed cases. The DRC Public Health Institute reported 5,021 cases and 2,378 deaths in the ongoing epidemic. Kinshasa's government stressed that all fatalities occurred within three months, making this the deadliest outbreak in the country's history. By comparison, the 2018-2020 epidemic in the DRC involved 3,381 infections and 2,299 deaths. Reuters reported the latest tallies as part of ongoing coverage. The article does not detail transmission chains, laboratory confirmation, or infection sources. No information is provided about imported or exported cases, vaccination status, or public health interventions. The situation remains unresolved as of the published date (2026-08-19), underscoring a severe, rapidly evolving Ebola outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: DRC:エボラウイルスの症例数が5000人を超えた
triage.triage_reason: DRCにおけるエボラ大規模流行(5,021例、死亡2,378人)は同国史上最悪規模であり、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクが認められるためフルRRAへ進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: 記事は感染経路、検査確定方法、輸出入例、ワクチン接種状況、対応策について詳細を欠くため、これらの点は不明と評価した。史上最悪規模の流行である点から緊急のフルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: L'épidémie constitue une urgence sanitaire mondiale avec plus de 5.000 cas confirmés
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The epidemic constitutes a global public health emergency with more than 5,000 confirmed cases.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo’s Ebola outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, has 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths (as of Aug 16), with 1,061 recoveries across 55 health zones in six provinces (case fatality rate 47.4%). Ituri remains the epicenter (84.8% of cases) but transmission is spreading to neighboring regions. The WHO declared the outbreak a global public health emergency three months after onset, describing it as the second-largest Ebola outbreak and potentially the deadliest worldwide if unchecked. The initial 95 days show a seven-day moving average above 90 cases, with high mortality and many deaths outside treatment facilities, indicating gaps in surveillance and response. No vaccine or approved therapy exists for Bundibugyo yet; two strain-specific vaccines are in early human trials. The PARTNERS trial tests remdesivir plus MBP134, with results expected in 3–4 weeks. ERVEBO for Zaire Ebola is being considered for frontline workers to assess cross-protection, though efficacy against Bundibugyo remains unproven.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱の流行は5,000人以上の確定感染者を伴い、世界的な公衆衛生上の緊急事態を構成する
triage.triage_reason: WHOがコンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱流行（Bundibugyo株）を国際的な公衆衛生上の緊急事態（PHEIC）として宣言し、5,000人超の感染者・致死率47.4%という重大な公衆衛生上の影響と国際的拡大の懸念が確認されるため、フルリスク評価に進むべき事案。
triage.notes: IturiはDRC国内のADM1地域であり、国としてはDRCのみを対象国とした。WHOによるPHEIC宣言、ワクチン未承認、致死率47.4%という重大性から即座にフルリスク評価（RRA）への移行が推奨される。

article.articleHeadline: L'OMS renforce sa riposte face à un risque de propagation " très
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO strengthens its response in the face of a risk of spread " very."
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) as of August 2026. WHO convened its Emergency Committee on August 18, with six provinces affected and national/international spread risk rated as very high. In the past three months, the outbreak has produced more than 5,000 confirmed cases and about 2,370 deaths, across five provinces. Mobility via rivers and roads, plus mining-area movement and ongoing insecurity, hamper surveillance and patient management. An attack on a response team in Kandoy, Ituri, injured an ambulance driver and damaged three vehicles; UN Ebola coordinator Julien Harneis condemned the attack and called for protection of civilians, health workers, and aid staff under international humanitarian law. To reinforce response, WHO is deploying 100 additional epidemiologists and mobilizing over 500 community health workers for contact tracing, active case finding, and community engagement, while urging local authorities and residents of Ituri to cooperate and reject violence.

triage.headline_ja: WHOが「非常に高い」拡大リスクに対する対応を強化
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱の大規模流行（5000例超、死者約2370人）が発生し、WHOが緊急委員会を開催、国際的拡大リスクを「非常に高い」と評価しているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: WHO緊急委員会が招集され、100名の疫学者と500名以上の地域保健員を追加投入する対応強化が行われている。治安不安・河川/道路移動・鉱山地域での人流がサーベイランスと患者管理を妨げており、対応チームへの攻撃も発生している。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in DRC crosses 5 000 cases, outpacing containment efforts
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of Congo's Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak has surpassed 5,000 confirmed cases, reaching 5,021 with 2,378 deaths, making it the largest Ebola outbreak by case count in DRC history and the second-worst globally after 2014–2016 West Africa. The Bundibugyo species currently has no approved vaccines or treatments. Declared May 15, the outbreak has intensified amid weak health infrastructure, community resistance, instability, and protests by response workers. Resource gaps persist, with WHO reporting about 60% of the $115 million funding appeal secured. Officials estimate 70–80% of new cases have no known link to a prior patient, indicating sustained community transmission. The WHO says the outbreak could be brought under control within roughly three months if impediments are overcome.

triage.headline_ja: DRCのエボラ出血熱、5000例を超え封じ込め対応を上回る拡大
triage.triage_reason: DRC史上最大規模のエボラ(Bundibugyo種)アウトブレイクで5000例超・死者2378人、コミュニティ感染が持続しワクチン・治療薬もない状況であり、IHR基準複数該当かつ社会的関心も高いためフルRRAへ進めるべき。
triage.notes: 発生地域にUganda・Angolaが含まれているが、記事サマリー上はDRC国内での拡大のみが主題であり、これら周辺国での実発生は言及されていないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC : Le Gouvernement évalue la riposte 3 mois après et mise sur les vaccins
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC: The government evaluates the response three months later and bets on vaccines.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) driven by the Bundibugyo strain. Three months after the outbreak declaration, a technical session on August 17, 2026, sought to reassess and recalibrate the response. The country has surpassed 5,000 confirmed cases and over 2,300 deaths across six provinces: Ituri (epicenter), Tshopo, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, Haut-Uélé, and Bas-Uélé. Kinshasa remains under heightened surveillance with no confirmed cases to prevent importation. Authorities are advancing two candidate vaccines targeting Bundibugyo and discussed antivirals to improve outcomes with timely treatment. The strategy prioritizes strengthened medical care, support for field teams, and intensified risk communication to counter rumors and reinforce barrier measures, while ensuring remuneration for frontline workers. A dual approach is emphasized: enhanced clinical treatment followed by reinforced community prevention, including transit controls toward Kinshasa and major urban centers.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱：政府が3か月後の対応を評価し、ワクチンに注力
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で大規模なエボラ（ブンディブジョ株）流行が継続中で、5000例超・死者2300人超と重篤な公衆衛生影響があり、複数州への拡大と首都への流入リスクも存在するためフルRRA相当と判断。
triage.notes: 6州に拡大し5000例超・死者2300人超の大規模流行。ワクチン・抗ウイルス薬の導入、キンシャサへの流入防止策が進行中。既知の継続流行だが規模と死亡者数から重要シグナルとして継続監視・評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Le nombre de cas d'Ebola en RDC dépasse les 5.000 en RDC
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of Ebola cases in the DRC exceeds 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 cumulative confirmed cases, reaching 5,021 infections and 2,378 deaths, according to the Institut National de la Santé Publique (INSP) via Reuters. Reported from Kinshasa on 2026-08-19, the outbreak remains ongoing. Transmission occurs through direct contact with blood, organs, or other bodily fluids of infected animals, with hunting, and the preparation or consumption of bushmeat identified as high-risk activities. The figures indicate the outbreak is still active in the DRC, underscoring ongoing public health challenges and the need for continued surveillance and infection control in affected regions.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ感染者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の累積感染者が5,000人超、死亡者2,378人と非常に高い致死率を示し、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクが認められるためフルRRAへ進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: 致死率は約47%と非常に高く、感染規模も拡大が続いている。国際的な支援・監視の継続が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Los mineros de oro itinerantes en el este de Congo complican la contención del ébola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Itinerant gold miners in eastern Congo complicate Ebola containment.
article.articleSummary: Artisanal gold miners in Ituri Province, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, are hindering Ebola containment as the Bundibugyo ebolavirus (Bundibugyo virus) strain drives a rapidly expanding outbreak that has killed more than 2,300 people and sickened at least 5,000. At one large site in Iga-Barrière, miners work under ground with basic tools, many are children, and mining camps are often illegal and insecure, undermining infection control practices such as handwashing and distancing. The virus is spreading faster than any prior outbreak; mobility of itinerant miners—who travel between villages to seek ore—complicates surveillance and contact tracing because there is no reliable system to register workers or track their movements. Two identified contacts disappeared after moving to another site. The Bundibugyo strain has no specific treatments or vaccines, and conflict-driven displacement in Ituri fuels labor in artisanal mining.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ東部の移動式金採掘労働者がエボラ対応を複雑化させている
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国東部でBundibugyo株エボラが急速に拡大し死者2300人超・感染者5000人超という重大な公衆衛生上の影響があり、渡り金採掘労働者の移動により接触者追跡が困難で国際的拡大リスクも懸念されるため、IHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo株には特異的な治療薬・ワクチンが存在せず、紛争による住民避難と非正規の採掘活動が感染拡大とサーベイランス困難を助長している点が特に懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: डीआरसी में लगातार बढ़ रहा इबोला प्रकोप, पीड़ितों की संख्या 5,000 के पार
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak continues to rise in the DRC, with the number of victims surpassing 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) continues to rise, driven by Bundibugyo ebolavirus. As of Sunday, 5,021 laboratory-confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths have been reported across six provinces and 55 health zones (case fatality rate 47.4%). Ituri province accounts for about 84.8% of cases, with the infection spreading rapidly to neighboring provinces. WHO notes this is the second-largest outbreak and is spreading faster than previous epidemics, keeping the event a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Africa CDC warns of ongoing high mortality (roughly one death every 30 minutes) and an elevated risk of cross-border importation to Uganda, South Sudan, and the Central African Republic. No specific vaccine or treatment exists for Bundibugyo, but experimental therapies are being trialed, including remdesivir and MBP134 monoclonal antibodies (and combinations); post-exposure prophylaxis with the oral antiviral Obeldesivir is under study. Ervebo cross-protection potential is being evaluated, with results expected in 3–4 weeks.

triage.headline_ja: DRCでエボラ流行が拡大継続、感染者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEIC（国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態）を宣言している大規模エボラ流行で、致死率47.4%、周辺国への越境拡大リスクも指摘されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: ウガンダ、南スーダン、中央アフリカ共和国への越境拡大リスクが指摘されているが、これらは確定発生国ではなくリスク国として言及されているため、対象国リストにも該当しないDRCのみをverified_locationsに含めた。

article.articleHeadline: Ébola: Epidemia na RDCongo ultrapassa 5.000 casos com propagação sem precedentes
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Epidemic in the DR Congo surpasses 5,000 cases with unprecedented spread.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 cases, with 5,021 infections and 2,378 deaths reported. Authorities warn the transmission is accelerating at an unprecedented pace, driven by insecurity, forced displacement, and large population movements. The outbreak’s spread is three times faster than the West Africa epidemic (2014–2016), which had over 11,000 fatalities. The World Health Organization stresses the situation is far from under control and poses a high risk of international spread. The outbreak is linked to the Bundibugyo Ebola virus, which carries a 30–50% case fatality rate and for which there is no approved vaccine or specific treatment. Transmission occurs via direct contact with bodily fluids of infected humans or animals; symptoms include fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and internal bleeding. The virus began circulating in eastern DRC in February (possibly January per Science), affecting Ituri and other regions, with Uganda reporting 20 cases (15 imported) and two deaths; Uganda declared itself Ebola-free on 28 July.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：コンゴ民主共和国の流行、前例のない拡大で5,000人を超える感染者数に
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ患者5,000人超・死者2,378人に達し、WHOが国際的拡大リスクを高いと明言している重大な公衆衛生危機であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当する。
triage.notes: ウガンダ（対象国外）でも輸入例が報告されているが7月28日にエボラ終息を宣言済み。アンゴラは記事内で感染発生の主題として言及されていないため除外。ブンディブギョ型エボラウイルスで承認済みワクチン・治療法がない点も重大なリスク要因。

article.articleHeadline: डीआरसी में लगातार बढ़ रहा इबोला प्रकोप, पीड़ितों की संख्या 5,000 के पार | Ituri: Health workers respond to Ebola outbreak
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak on the rise in the DRC; number of victims has surpassed 5,000 | Ituri: Health workers respond to Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: WHO lists the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo as a continuing public health emergency of international concern, with Bundibugyo virus cases surpassing 5,000 and spreading to new areas. By Sunday, 5,021 confirmed cases were reported across six provinces in 55 health zones, with 2,378 deaths (case fatality 47.4%). Ituri remains the epicenter, accounting for about 84.8% of cases, though transmission is rising in neighboring provinces. The outbreak is the second-largest and is accelerating, with a 95-day period showing a seven-day moving average over 90. Early symptoms are not distinctive, delaying care. There is no specific vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo yet; experimental and existing therapies are being used. Two vaccines are in human trials; remdesivir, MBP134 monoclonal antibody, and their combinations are under evaluation; obeldesivir is studied for post-exposure prophylaxis. Ervebo may offer cross-protection, but confirmation is pending. Import risk to Uganda, South Sudan, and Central African Republic remains very high.

triage.headline_ja: DRCでエボラ流行が拡大続く、感染者数5,000人を超える | イトゥリ：医療従事者がエボラ流行に対応
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEIC（国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態）として継続認定しているコンゴ民主共和国のエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）流行で、感染者5,000人超・致死率47.4%と深刻化・拡大しており、IHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: ウガンダ・南スーダン・中央アフリカ共和国は輸入感染リスクが高いとされているが、記事サマリー上では実際の発生は確認されておらず、対象国リストにも南スーダンは含まれないため verified_locations には含めない。イトゥリ州はDRC国内の行政区分のため国レベルではDRCに統合。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : l'OMS maintient l'urgence internationale en RDC
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: WHO maintains the international public health emergency in the DRC.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-08-19, the WHO maintains the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC), status established on May 17 and renewed after an emergency committee meeting. The outbreak totals 4,945 confirmed cases and 2,325 deaths, the largest in the DRC and second globally after the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak. Risk is rated very high in the DRC (six provinces) and high in Uganda and several neighboring countries, with low risk elsewhere. The epidemic is advancing rapidly amid insecurity and population movements; response efforts are challenged by security incidents, including an ambulance driver attack and vehicle vandalism in Kandoy, Ituri. WHO has deployed 100 additional epidemiologists, over 500 community health workers, and added about 400 beds; safe burials are improving in Lita and Nizi. About 60% of the $115 million needed has been mobilized. Survivors, such as Esther (19) in Kigonze, are aiding community trust and prompt care-seeking.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：WHOがコンゴ民主共和国における国際的な公衆衛生上の緊急事態を維持
triage.triage_reason: WHOがDRCのエボラ出血熱をPHEIC（国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態）として継続認定しており、感染者数・死者数ともに歴史的規模で、IHR基準の複数項目に該当するためフルRRAへ移行すべき。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCにおけるエボラ出血熱の大規模流行とWHOによるPHEIC継続を報じている。ウガンダなど近隣国でもリスクが高いとされるが、対象国リストに含まれるのはDRCのみ。ルーマニア・クルージュ等の地理情報はBluedotの位置付与誤りと判断し除外した。

article.articleHeadline: डीआरसी में लगातार बढ़ रहा इबोला प्रकोप, पीड़ितों की संख्या 5,000 के पार - Punjab Kesari
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the DRC continues to rise, the number of victims has crossed 5,000 - Punjab Kesari
article.articleSummary: Six provinces in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo report 5,021 confirmed Ebola cases and 2,378 deaths (case fatality 47.4%) as of 19 August 2026, with Ituri province the epicenter (84.8% of cases) and spread to neighboring areas. WHO declares the Bundibugyo strain outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern and notes it is the second-largest and fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak to date, with about one death every 30 minutes at current pace. Response includes experimental and existing measures: two Bundibugyo-specific vaccines are in human trials; the Partners Treatment Trial assesses remdesivir, the MBP134 monoclonal antibody, and their combination; oral antiviral Obeldesivir is studied for post-exposure prophylaxis. Researchers also explore whether the licensed ERVEBO vaccine offers cross-protection against Bundibugyo virus. Imported-case risk is high for Uganda, South Sudan, and the Central African Republic due to proximity and cross-border movement.

triage.headline_ja: DRCでエボラ流行が拡大続く、感染者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEIC（国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態）を宣言した史上2番目に大規模かつ最速拡大のエボラ流行であり、致死率47.4%、周辺国への輸出リスクも高いためフルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダ、南スーダン、中央アフリカ共和国は輸入例のリスク国として言及されているが、対象国リストに含まれず、かつ確定例の報告はないため verified_locations には含めていない。

article.articleHeadline: DRC Ebola outbreak "far from under control", warns WHO
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) remains far from under control. Almost 5,000 people infected and more than 2,300 deaths across six provinces and 55 health zones. May 15 marked the declaration of the DRC's 17th Ebola outbreak; the WHO followed with a public health emergency of international concern on May 17. The outbreak is the second-largest on record and spreading faster than previous ones, driven by insecurity, population displacement, and movement along roads and to mining sites. Uganda has 20 confirmed cases and two deaths; mid-July reports indicated no ongoing infections there. There is no approved vaccine or specific treatment for Bundibugyo, though clinical trials are ongoing. The EU has provided €2.5 million in screening tests. WHO is decentralising response and engaging communities, including motorbike taxi drivers, to improve surveillance.

triage.headline_ja: DRCのエボラ出血熱流行「制御には遠い」とWHOが警告
triage.triage_reason: DRCで第17次エボラ（ブンディブギョウイルス病）流行が発生し、WHOがPHEICを宣言済み。5,000人近い感染者、2,300人以上の死亡、ウガンダへの越境拡大も確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため直ちにフルリスク評価に進むべき事案。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCでの流行が主題であり、ウガンダは越境例（20例確定、2死亡、7月中旬時点で新規感染なし）として言及されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めなかった。渡航・貿易制限に関する具体的記述はなく「不明」とした。

article.articleHeadline: West African countries pledge stronger response to epidemics
article.articleSummary: Abidjan – West African experts from ECOWAS reaffirm commitment to stronger epidemic response, during a four-day workshop in Abidjan to technically validate the third Regional Strategic Plan for Epidemic Preparedness and Response and other Public Health Emergencies of the RCSDC for 2027–2031. The gathering notes continued threats from yellow fever, meningitis, cholera, measles and viral hemorrhagic fevers, exacerbated by climate change and zoonotic risks. In June, ECOWAS said it is strengthening preparedness to reduce imported Ebola virus disease risk into West Africa. ECOWAS member states have activated contingency plans and ramped up surveillance at airports, border posts and other entry points following the Ebola outbreak currently reported in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda. The 2014–2016 Ebola outbreak—West Africa's deadliest—mainly hit Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone, killing more than 11,000 and stretching health systems.

triage.headline_ja: 西アフリカ諸国、感染症流行への対応強化を約束
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はECOWAS主催の疫病対応強化ワークショップに関する内容であり、新規の感染症アウトブレイク発生を報じるものではない。DRC・ウガンダのエボラ流行は既存事象として背景的に言及されているのみ。
triage.notes: 記事の主題は西アフリカ諸国（コートジボワール、シエラレオネ、リベリア、ギニア）の地域的な感染症予防対応計画に関するものであり、対象国リストに含まれる国は主題として登場しない。DRC・ウガンダのエボラ流行は既存事象の背景説明として言及されているのみで、新規発生情報は含まれていないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Preparan curso escolar a distancia en zonas con ébola en RDC
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Distance-learning school year being prepared in Ebola-affected areas of the DRC.
article.articleSummary: As of 19 August 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 confirmed cases and more than 2,300 deaths, with six provinces reporting cases since 15 May. Kinshasa remains free of Ebola to date, while authorities bolster border and river-area controls along the Congo to prevent spread to the capital. In education, authorities are preparing a distance-learning school year in Ebola-affected areas to maintain learning while reducing transmission in schools. Educational materials will be printed and circulated every four weeks and broadcast via local and community radio stations. The Education and Health ministries are coordinating, with emphasis on sensitizing teachers, school administrators, and communities. Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka announced a salary-support framework for frontline healthcare workers as part of the response.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ流行地域で遠隔学習の新学期準備
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ流行は5000例超・2300人以上の死亡、6州に拡大し首都キンシャサへの波及防止措置が取られており、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクが認められるためフルRRAへ進める。
triage.notes: 既に大規模流行が進行中の既知のエボラアウトブレイクであり、首都キンシャサへの拡大防止策や教育・保健当局の連携、医療従事者への給与支援など、政府の本格対応が報じられている。

article.articleHeadline: Ignoring mild fever during monsoon can be risky: It could be dengue, malaria or chikungunya, says doctor
article.articleSummary: During India's monsoon, a mild fever may signal dengue, malaria, chikungunya, or typhoid and should not be ignored. Provisional NCVBDC data show 6,927 dengue cases and 10 deaths till February 2026, far below 2025’s 121,824 cases and 131 deaths, underscoring ongoing risk during rainfall. Stagnant water fosters mosquitoes; contaminated food/water raises typhoid risk. Early symptoms often overlap: dengue with fever, headache, body aches and fatigue; malaria with fever and chills; chikungunya with fever and joint pain; typhoid with fever, weakness, and headache. Tests should be timed and targeted: CBC for baseline; dengue NS1 antigen in early phase; rapid malaria tests; blood cultures for typhoid; molecular tests for relevant pathogens. Avoid self-medication and unnecessary antibiotics. In suspected dengue, avoid aspirin/ibuprofen due to bleeding risk. Persistent fever with severe headache, vomiting, rash, or exposure history warrants medical assessment to guide treatment and monitoring.

triage.headline_ja: モンスーン期の軽い発熱を無視すると危険：デング熱、マラリア、チクングニア熱の可能性があると医師が指摘
triage.triage_reason: 季節性のデング熱・マラリア等に関する一般的な健康啓発記事であり、新規の異常発生や特異なイベントを報じるものではない。2026年のデング熱データは2025年より大幅に減少していることが示されている。
triage.notes: 記事はインドのモンスーン期における発熱性疾患（デング熱、マラリア、チクングニア熱、腸チフス）の鑑別診断に関する医療啓発記事。2026年のデング熱症例数（6,927件、死亡10件）は2025年（121,824件、死亡131件）より大幅に減少しており、異常事態を示すものではないため、季節性の毎年恒例の内容としてDISMISSと判定した。

article.articleHeadline: Над 5000 са потвърдените случаи на ебола в Конго
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 5,000 confirmed Ebola cases in Congo.
article.articleSummary: More than 5,000 confirmed Ebola cases have been reported in the Democratic Republic of Congo, marking the 17th outbreak and the largest in the country’s history by late July. The death toll reached 2,378 over the weekend, surpassing the prior record from 2018–2020. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there are no approved vaccines or specific treatments. Declared on May 15, the outbreak’s spread continues, with health authorities warning that containment efforts are not delivering the necessary results. Ongoing challenges include weak health infrastructure, resistance in some communities, instability, and protests by staff involved in the response, all of which hinder timely identification, isolation, and treatment of infected individuals.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ確認例が5000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大規模のエボラ流行(5000人超の確定例、死者2378人)が発生し、承認されたワクチン・治療法がなく、封じ込めも機能していないため、公衆衛生上深刻かつ国際的拡大リスクがある。
triage.notes: 史上最大規模のエボラ流行（Bundibugyo株）で、承認ワクチン・治療法なし。医療インフラの脆弱性、地域社会の抵抗、不安定な情勢、対応スタッフの抗議行動が封じ込めを阻害しており、国際的な支援介入が必要な状況。

article.articleHeadline: डीआरसी में इबोला का बढ़ा प्रकोप, 5,000 लोग महामारी की चपेट में आए
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak has intensified in the DRC; 5,000 people have been affected by the epidemic.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease outbreak intensifies in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), with 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths (case fatality 47.4%) across six provinces and 55 health zones as of Sunday. The World Health Organization (WHO) warns the outbreak remains a Public Health Emergency of International Concern and is the second-largest and fastest-spreading Ebola epidemic yet. New areas are affected, prompting use of experimental vaccines and treatments. Africa CDC reports roughly one death every 30 minutes, risking the outbreak becoming the world’s deadliest if not contained. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus emphasizes the outbreak is far from under control. In about 95 days since reporting, the seven-day moving average has exceeded 90 cases per day, higher than West Africa’s 2014-2016 epidemic and DRC’s 2018-2020 outbreak at comparable stages.

triage.headline_ja: DRCでエボラ出血熱の流行が拡大、5,000人が感染
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEICと明言し、致死率47.4%・5,000人超の感染者を伴う大規模流行であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCでのエボラ流行が主題。Angolaは発生地域に含まれるが記事本文で拡大の言及なく除外。WHOがPHEICと表明しており既にフルRRA相当の重大事案。

article.articleHeadline: कांगो में इबोला वायरस संक्रमण के मामलों की संख्या पांच हजार से अधिक हुई
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of Ebola virus infections in Congo has surpassed five thousand.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus infections in Bunia, Democratic Republic of the Congo, have surpassed 5,000, with 5,021 cases and 2,378 deaths reported as of Sunday, according to official tallies. Health authorities warn that transmission is accelerating in remote areas, challenging containment efforts. The outbreak’s rapid spread is described as faster than any previous global outbreak. By comparison, the 2014–2016 Ebola outbreak killed more than 11,000 people. The report highlights ongoing transmission due to gaps in control measures in hard-to-reach regions, underscoring the need for strengthened public health response and monitoring. The article does not provide laboratory confirmation details or a defined infection source, but emphasizes the elevated public health risk posed by Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラウイルス感染例が5000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRCで5000例を超え死亡率も高く、遠隔地での感染拡大が加速しており公衆衛生上の深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクが認められるため。
triage.notes: 記事は感染者数・死者数の増加と遠隔地での制御困難を強調しているが、検査確認や感染源の詳細は不明。

article.articleHeadline: China Detects First Human H1N2v Swine Flu Case: Could The Rare Virus Spread To India?
article.articleSummary: China reports its first laboratory-confirmed human infection with influenza A(H1N2)v, a swine-origin variant, in a 2-year-10-month-old boy from Yunnan. The child developed recurrent fever and paroxysmal cough, progressed to bronchopneumonia, and was hospitalized; he recovered and was discharged. Initial RT-PCR was negative; full viral genome was obtained by sequencing, showing a reassortant lineage from swine H1N1, H1N2, and H3N2 circulating in China. Close contacts (30) remained negative, with no influenza-like illness, and there is no evidence of sustained human-to-human transmission. The likely source was exposure in a rural compound with pigs, chickens, and pigeons; a deceased pig tested positive for influenza, though the exact transmission route was not established. WHO and China CDC emphasise sporadic zoonotic infections with low public health risk; India should maintain surveillance and One Health coordination, focusing on early detection and genomic monitoring.

triage.headline_ja: 中国で初のH1N2v型豚インフルエンザ人体感染例を確認：インドへの拡大の可能性は？
triage.triage_reason: 中国雲南省で新規リアソータント型H1N2v豚インフルエンザの人への初感染例が確認されたが、単発症例で持続的なヒト-ヒト感染の証拠はなく、WHO・中国CDCともに公衆衛生リスクは低いと評価している。新規変異株であるため継続的な監視が必要。
triage.notes: インドは記事中で「拡大の可能性」として言及されているのみで、実際の感染発生国ではないため verified_locations には含めない。豚・鶏・鳩と接触する農村環境での動物由来感染で、豚H1N1・H1N2・H3N2由来のリアソータント株。濃厚接触者30名は陰性でヒト-ヒト感染の証拠なし。新規変異株のため今後の続報（追加症例の有無、遺伝子解析結果等）を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: H1N1 Scare At Bengaluru School: 500+ Students Fall Sick -- Expert Explains What Parents Must Know
article.articleSummary: Date 2026-08-19: In Bengaluru, more than 500 students at Clarence High School (Richards Town) fell ill with flu-like symptoms, prompting suspension of offline classes at the 2,500-student school. While two staff members tested positive for H1N1, Karnataka health authorities later said no student had tested positive for H1N1. The episode underscores influenza vigilance in children. H1N1 influenza (swine flu) is an Influenza A virus; most children have mild to moderate illness, but it can progress to pneumonia, bronchiolitis, or ARDS in vulnerable kids. Typical onset includes sudden high fever, dry cough, sore throat, rhinitis, body aches, fatigue; emergency signs include respiratory distress, extreme lethargy, dehydration, or returning fever. High-risk children include those under 2, asthma, chronic neurological or immunocompromised conditions. Prevention: annual vaccine, good hand hygiene, and avoiding aspirin. Parents should distinguish home-managed symptoms from urgent care needs; seek ER for respiratory distress or severe symptoms.

triage.headline_ja: ベンガルールの学校でH1N1騒動：500人以上の生徒が発病――専門家が保護者に伝えるべきこと
triage.triage_reason: 学校で500人以上がインフルエンザ様症状を発症し休校となったが、実際にH1N1陽性が確認されたのは職員2名のみで生徒は陰性。地域内での学校閉鎖という社会的関心の高まりとヒト-ヒト感染の可能性からWPRO基準を満たすためPICKUPとする。
triage.notes: 生徒の症状はインフルエンザ様であり、H1N1陽性は職員2名のみで生徒の検査結果は陰性とされている。学校の一時休校と大規模な発症数から地域的関心は高いが、重症例や死亡例の報告はなく、現時点では局地的な学校内アウトブレイクの範囲に留まる可能性が高い。続報でH1N1確定例の拡大有無を確認する必要がある。

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Don't delay—Swine flu cases are rising in Delhi; here are the precautions and the vaccine.
article.articleSummary: Delhi is experiencing a surge in H1N1 swine flu and H3N2 influenza, with rising cases across multiple Indian states. In the capital, around 10–15 new cases are reported daily; patients present with high fever (102–103°F), runny nose, cough, shortness of breath, frequent sneezing, body aches, and headaches. Transmission is through close contact with infected individuals and by touching contaminated surfaces, underscoring the need for masks and distancing from the sick. Vaccines for swine flu and influenza are available in the market, priced about INR 2,000–2,500, offering roughly one year of protection when taken on a doctor’s advice. If symptoms appear, seek medical consultation rather than self-prescribing, and maintain general immunity through precautions.

triage.headline_ja: 急いで対処を―デリーでスワインフル（豚インフルエンザ）の症例が増加中、予防法とワクチンについて
triage.triage_reason: インドの季節性インフルエンザ（H1N1/H3N2）の毎年見られる増加であり、重症例や死亡の報告もなく、異常性や国際的拡大のリスクも認められないため。
triage.notes: 記事は健康啓発・予防情報を主とするローカル記事であり、季節性インフルエンザの通常の増加を報じている。重症例・死亡・入院増加などの記載はなく、社会的・政治的関心の高まりも確認できない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola cases in Congo exceed 5,000, government data shows
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-19, the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ebola outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo species, has reached 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths, making it the largest such outbreak in DRC’s history and the second-worst globally after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic. Declared on May 15, this is the 17th Ebola epidemic in the country and it has gained momentum despite response efforts. The public health institute notes that weak health infrastructure, community resistance, instability, and protests by response workers hinder efforts to identify and respond to cases. There are no approved vaccines or treatments for Bundibugyo Ebola. The situation report underscores ongoing transmission with record-case counts, highlighting a challenging, protracted response.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ感染者数が5,000人を超える、政府データで判明
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大規模のエボラ流行が発生し、死者2,378人・症例5,021人と拡大継続中であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準を複数満たすためフルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれているが、記事サマリーではDRC国内の状況のみが記述されており、Angolaでの発生は言及されていないため除外した。ワクチン・治療薬未承認のBundibugyo種による流行で、致死率約47%と非常に高い。

article.articleHeadline: الكونغو الديمقراطية: حصيلة الإصابات بفيروس إيبولا تتجاوز 5 آلاف حالة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Ebola virus infections exceed 5,000 cases.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo reports Ebola virus infections exceeding 5,000, with 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths as of late July. The 17th outbreak wave is the largest on record by case count, surpassing the 2018–2020 epidemic. The surge is linked to the Bundibugyo strain, for which there are no licensed vaccines or approved treatments. The figures come from the Public Health Institute of the DRC, cited by France 24 in its English-language bulletin. Ebola is a human disease; symptoms typically appear 2–3 weeks after infection and begin with fever, sore throat, and muscle and joint pains, followed by vomiting, diarrhea, rash, and liver and kidney dysfunction. The report emphasizes the severity of the current outbreak and the absence of strain-specific preventive or therapeutic options.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国:エボラウイルス感染者数が5000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCで確認例5,021人、死亡2,378人と過去最大規模のエボラ流行が継続しており、当該株（Bundibugyo）にはワクチン・治療法が存在しないため、深刻な公衆衛生上のリスクと国際的拡大の懸念がある。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Congo cases surpass 5,000 as record-setting pace of spread continues
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in Congo has reached 5,021 cases and 2,378 deaths as of Sunday, August 16, 2026, per the Ministry of Health. The epidemic, centered in Ituri province with Bunia and Aru affected, is Congo’s 17th Ebola outbreak and has spread about three times faster than the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic, continuing since it was declared on May 15. WHO Director-General Tedros warned the epidemic remains far from under control and the risk of national and international spread remains high. Response is hampered by insecurity, displacement and attacks on health workers; in Aru, residents attacked a health team after a suspected case, with an ambulance set on fire and two vehicles damaged. Data indicate rapid escalation despite containment efforts under challenging regional conditions.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ患者数が5,000人を超え、過去最速の感染拡大が続く
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラが記録的速度で拡大し、死者2,378人・症例5,021人に達し、WHOも国際的拡大リスクを警告しているため、IHR基準の複数該当かつ社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: WHO事務局長が国内外への拡大リスクが高いと警告。治安不安、住民による医療従事者への攻撃など対応が困難な状況で、2014-2016年の西アフリカ流行の3倍の速度で拡大中。

article.articleHeadline: कांगो में बेकाबू हुआ इबोला: अब तक 2300 से ज्यादा मौतें, WHO ने दी दुनिया भर में फैलने की चेतावनी
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola out of control in the Congo: More than 2,300 deaths so far, WHO warns of global spread
article.articleSummary: EBOLA outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has surged, with about 5,000 suspected/confirmed cases and over 2,300 deaths reported to date. Declared on May 15, this is the 17th Ebola outbreak in the country, driven by the Bundibugyo strain; no vaccine or specific treatment is yet proven, though clinical trials are underway. The WHO declared an international public health emergency after a May 17 emergency committee meeting. Risk levels assign a 'Very High' threat inside the DRC, 'High' for Uganda and other border areas, and 'Low' for the rest of Africa and the world. Six provinces are affected, including near the South Sudan border; Uganda has reported cases. High transmission is linked to insecurity, under-resourced health facilities, and home deaths. Relief efforts are being decentralized and surveillance expanded to reach communities and transport networks.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラが制御不能に：これまでに2,300人以上が死亡、WHOが世界的拡大を警告
triage.triage_reason: DRCでの大規模エボラ流行（死者2,300人超、症例約5,000人）に対しWHOがPHEICを宣言し、国際的拡大への警告も出されているため、フルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCでの流行を主題としており、ウガンダや南スーダンは国境地域での症例確認に留まるため、対象国リストに含まれるDRCのみをverified_locationsとした。

article.articleHeadline: Congo Ebola outbreak hits 5,000 cases as it outpaces response efforts
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Congo (DRC) has reached 5,021 cases and 2,378 deaths, per the Ministry of Health, as of Sunday. Responders warn transmission is accelerating at an unprecedented speed, outpacing containment in one of the country’s most remote regions amid insecurity, displacement, and heavy population movements. The outbreak is the fastest Ebola spread on record, about three times faster than the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak, which started from its first detected case and killed more than 11,000. The data underscore ongoing, uncontrolled transmission in challenging conditions, underscoring the difficulty of response efforts in settings marked by insecurity and high population movement.

article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), centered in the Congo-Kinshasa region, is spreading faster than any prior outbreak. More than 5,000 people have been infected, with 2,378 confirmed deaths recorded by the country's health ministry as of Sunday. Although the West Africa Ebola crisis of 2014–2016 caused more fatalities overall, the current outbreak is propagating roughly three times faster than that wave. World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus cautioned that the epidemic is far from under control. The outbreak has been active since May. The article notes rapid transmission but does not detail laboratory confirmation or specific transmission sources. The situation underscores ongoing regional risk and the need for intensified surveillance and public health measures to control spread.

article.articleHeadline: Scrub Typhus Outbreak: पूर्वांचल में तेजी से पांव पसार रहा स्क्रब टाइफस; बीएचयू अस्पताल में एक हफ्ते में मिले 12 नए मरीज
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Scrub Typhus Outbreak: Scrub Typhus Is Rapidly Spreading in Purvanchal; 12 New Patients in a Week at BHU Hospital
article.articleSummary: Scrub Typhus is rapidly spreading in Purvanchal, Eastern Uttar Pradesh, including Varanasi and surrounding districts, during the monsoon season. The illness is caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi and transmitted by chigger mites; farmers and rural residents working in fields are most at risk. At BHU’s Sir Sundarlal Hospital, 12 Scrub Typhus patients were admitted in the past week, with one discharged; a comprehensive health advisory from the General Medicine department is in the works. In 2025, BHU tested 2,790 samples, 493 positive (about 19%). After the August 17 death of a girl, a three-member team (Dr. Ajay Kumar Singh, Dr. Shishir Kumar, Sharat Chandra Pandey) was formed to review the case; private pathology confirmed Scrub Typhus. In 2026 (Jan–Aug) the district has recorded 23 cases, with heightened surveillance in rural blocks. Symptoms: high fever, headache, myalgia, body pain, rash or eschar; seek prompt testing and wear full clothing when in tall grasses or bushes.

triage.headline_ja: スクラブチフス発生：東部ウッタル・プラデーシュ（プールヴァーンチャル）で急速に拡大、BHU病院で1週間に12人の新規患者
triage.triage_reason: 季節性の媒介動物媒介感染症だが、死亡例と入院例の増加が確認され、地元衛生当局が調査チームを編成し注意喚起を準備している点で行政の関心が高い。
triage.notes: スクラブチフスはOrientia tsutsugamushiによるダニ媒介感染症で、モンスーン期にウッタル・プラデーシュ州東部で季節的に流行する既知の疾患。ヒト-ヒト感染はなく、国際的拡大リスクは低いが、死亡例発生と地域衛生当局の対応強化が見られるため経過観察・詳細情報収集が望ましい。

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceed 5,000
article.articleSummary: As of August 19, 2026, Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceed 5,000, driven by Bundibugyo ebolavirus. The outbreak has rapidly spread to six provinces and 55 health zones since mid-May, with insecurity, population displacement, mining areas, and busy transport routes hindering containment. There is currently no licensed vaccine or specific therapy; clinical trials are ongoing, but health officials fear existing measures are insufficient to stop transmission. The DRC Ministry of Health notes that early symptoms resemble ordinary fever, and community transmission often occurs before diagnosis; resistance to control measures has also led to ambulance destruction and injuries to health workers, complicating the response. The WHO Director-General warns the outbreak remains far from controlled with high international spread risk; WHO and partners are urged to accelerate funding, resources, and community engagement to curb further spread.

article.articleHeadline: "상어보다 무서운 살인 생물 1위가 모기...?" 질병청의 무서운 경고
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: "Is the mosquito the No. 1 deadly creature more terrifying than a shark...?" KDCA's alarming warning.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-08-19, Korea's KDCA issued a nationwide Japanese encephalitis (JE) alert after JE virus was detected in Ulsan and vector mosquitoes confirmed in Suwon, raising risk. JE can progress from fever and headache to paralysis and seizures, with a case fatality rate of 20-30%. A 119-person study links why some people are bitten more to skin microbiota and skin chemicals. The piece contrasts mosquito lethality with sharks, noting malaria kills about 610,000 annually versus roughly 10 shark deaths, and recalls malaria experiments on soldiers during the Sino-Japanese War. It discusses ecological considerations of mosquito extinction, the role of mosquitoes in ecosystems, and a 'mosquito factory' approach: Wolbachia bacteria and a $2 trap that reduced dengue by about 70% in Brazil. Summer prevention tips: wear long sleeves, use repellents, and notes on future biosecurity prospects.

triage.notes: 記事は韓国（対象国外）の日本脳炎注意喚起および蚊全般に関する啓発記事。ブラジルのデング熱対策（Wolbachia・トラップ）は事例紹介であり、ブラジルでの新規発生報告ではないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola outbreak reaches 5,000 cases as it outpaces response efforts at unprecedented speed
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 5,021 cases and 2,378 deaths as of Aug 16, 2026, with transmission accelerating in the insecure Ituri region. The epidemic is spreading at an unprecedented speed, outpacing response efforts amid displacement and high population movement. Health workers face safety threats, including an Aug 17 attack in Aru where a mob set fire to an ambulance and damaged vehicles. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned on Aug 18 that the outbreak remains far from under control and carries a high risk of national and international spread. Since the first detected case, it has spread roughly three times faster than the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak and is now the second-most lethal Ebola episode on record.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行、前例のない速さで対応を上回り5000例に達する

article.articleHeadline: Aproape 5.000 de cazuri și peste 2.300 de morți în Congo: cel mai rapid focar de Ebola din istorie scapă de sub control
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Almost 5,000 cases and over 2,300 deaths in Congo: the fastest Ebola outbreak in history is getting out of control.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, is the fastest-spreading in the country’s history. As of August 17, 4,945 confirmed cases and 2,325 deaths have been recorded, with nearly half of the infected succumbing. The epidemic has spread across multiple eastern provinces amid poverty, armed conflict, and limited access to care. Medecins Sans Frontieres warns that transmission is outpacing on‑the‑ground response, with about two‑thirds of deaths occurring in communities before patients reach hospitals or treatment centers, hampering isolation, contact tracing, and safe burials. Ebola transmits via direct contact with blood or other body fluids and can remain contagious after death. Fragile local health systems, ongoing conflict, and hard-to-reach communities complicate control efforts. International agencies urge rapid, intensified intervention as the window to prevent wider spread narrows, noting the outbreak’s scale and mortality exceed recent past outbreaks in speed and impact.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴで約5,000例、2,300人超の死者:史上最速のエボラ流行が制御不能に
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で史上最速規模のエボラ流行が拡大し、死亡率が高く医療体制崩壊のリスクがあるため、IHR基準・WPRO基準いずれも複数該当し社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: 国際機関（国境なき医師団など）が介入強化を要請しており、致死率が高く、地域の武力衝突や医療アクセス制限が拡大要因となっている。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC: la barre des 5.000 cas franchie, l'épidémie est "loin d'être maîtrisée", selon l'OMS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC: the 5,000-case threshold crossed, the outbreak is "far from being under control," according to the WHO.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) driven by the new Bundibugyo strain has reached 5,021 confirmed cases across six provinces as of August 18, 2026, with 2,378 deaths and 1,061 recoveries, yielding a case fatality rate of 47.4%. Three months after the outbreak was officially declared, the response has been rapid but the outbreak is far from under control. The World Health Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned of a high risk of national and international spread during an emergency committee meeting. Ongoing transmission and a substantial mortality burden characterize the situation, underscoring continued vigilance and containment efforts in the affected regions of the DRC; no details on infection source or exported/imported cases are provided.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ:感染者5,000人の壁を突破、WHOによれば流行は「制御されているとは言い難い」状況
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱が6州で5,000人超・致死率47.4%に達し、WHOが国内外への拡大リスクを警告しており、IHR基準複数該当かつ社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: 新規Bundibugyo株による流行で致死率が非常に高く、WHOが緊急委員会で国際的拡大リスクを警告している。フルRRAへの移行を推奨。

article.articleHeadline: El brote de ébola en Congo llega a 5.000 casos y supera la respuesta de salud a velocidad inédita
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in Congo reaches 5,000 cases and outpaces the health response at unprecedented speed.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo reaches 5,021 cases and 2,378 deaths as of Sunday, according to the Ministry of Health. The response is overwhelmed by insecurity, displacement, and intense population movements, with Ituri province bearing the brunt. The outbreak is spreading at an unprecedented pace, infecting and killing more people faster than any prior Ebola crisis; authorities say it is about three times faster than the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak, which caused more than 11,000 deaths. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned that national and international spread remains a high risk and that the epidemic is far from under control. Security concerns have hampered teams, with attacks on health workers in Aru territory, including an ambulance set on fire and vehicles damaged. The situation remains volatile in remote northern regions of the country.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行、5000例に達し前例のない速さで保健対応を上回る
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がコンゴで5000例・2378人死亡に達し、WHOが国際的拡大リスクを警告するなど深刻な公衆衛生上の脅威であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準を複数満たすためフルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: 治安不安定化と人口移動により対応が困難化しており、WHO事務局長が国際的拡大の高リスクを警告している。フルリスク評価が必要な重大シグナル。

article.articleHeadline: Virus Zapadnog Nila preti Balkanu: Bolest odnela četvrtu žrtvu u Severnoj Makedoniji
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: West Nile virus threatens the Balkans: the disease has claimed a fourth victim in North Macedonia.
article.articleSummary: West Nile fever remains a public health concern in the Balkans. As of August 19, 2026, North Macedonia reports its fourth death since May, with at least 35 confirmed infections and 24 hospitalizations, several on ventilators. In Serbia, six infections have been recorded (since June 1) across Belgrade, South Banat District, and Central Banat District, with an average patient age of 64; four men and two women affected. People over 80 and those over 50 with weaker immune systems are at higher risk, though younger individuals can be infected. The virus is mosquito-borne; the primary vector is Culex pipiens, with birds as the main reservoir and humans as incidental hosts. Most infections are asymptomatic; about 20% resemble flu, and fewer than 1% develop severe disease (headache, neck stiffness, confusion, seizures, paralysis). Prevention centers on avoiding bites; no vaccine, though vaccine development and trials have occurred since the early 2000s.

triage.headline_ja: 西ナイルウイルスがバルカン半島を脅かす：北マケドニアで4人目の死者
triage.triage_reason: 北マケドニア・セルビアでの西ナイル熱流行に関する記事であり、対象国リストに含まれる国（インド等）は記事本文で言及されておらず主題ではないため見送り。
triage.notes: 発生地域リストにインド（Uttar Pradesh等）が含まれているが、記事サマリーは北マケドニア・セルビアでの西ナイルウイルス流行のみを扱っており、インドについての言及はない。Bluedotの地域付与誤りと判断し、対象国は該当なしとした。

article.articleHeadline: Thailand tightens border surveillance over Yangon cholera outbreak
article.articleSummary: Yangon, Myanmar reports a cholera outbreak with about 500 severe diarrhoea admissions since August 9; 149 screened positive for cholera and 9 laboratory-confirmed Vibrio cholerae infections, per DDC Director-General Dr Montien Kanasawat. No serogroup/serotype details released. One elderly patient with pre-existing heart and lung disease died; authorities have not confirmed cholera as the direct cause. Central Yangon hosts most cases near restaurants and street-food stalls. Public health actions include food and water inspections, increased chlorination, disinfecting homes, and temporary suspension of high-risk street food. Latest information indicates new admissions are declining, but surveillance remains. Thailand assesses public risk as low, but travel to outbreak areas carries higher risk; continued Thailand–Myanmar travel means imported cases could enter Thailand, and travellers with severe watery diarrhoea or vomiting should seek medical care and report travel history.

triage.headline_ja: タイ、ヤンゴンのコレラ流行を受け国境監視を強化
triage.triage_reason: ミャンマー・ヤンゴンで重症下痢500件超、コレラ確定9件・死亡1名を伴う流行が発生し、タイが国境監視を強化するなど国際的な対応が生じているため、フルリスク評価に進むべきシグナルと判断した。
triage.notes: 発生地域にThailandが含まれているが、記事の主題はミャンマー・ヤンゴンでのコレラ流行であり、タイは国境監視強化という対応措置の主体に過ぎないためThailandはverified_locationsから除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Outbreak Still Far From Under Control
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains far from control, with more than 5,000 cases and nearly 2,500 deaths in just under 100 days. Officially announced in mid-May, the outbreak is spreading faster than any prior Ebola event in Africa and could become the continent’s largest. Transmission is via physical contact and bodily fluids; symptoms include fever, diarrhea, and bleeding. Experts warn many cases and deaths are unreported, hindering a full picture of transmission. Early detection was delayed by nonspecific symptoms and limited diagnostics; it may have been circulating since early in the year. Initially centered in Ituri Province, the fever has spread to six provinces including North Kivu, South Kivu, and Tshopo. Urban hubs like Bunia have expanded treatment and lab capacity; MSF runs seven treatment centers with 430 beds and 1,400 staff. Rural areas face gaps in rapid testing amid armed conflict and border restrictions.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱の流行、依然として制御不能な状況
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で5000例超・死者2500人規模のエボラ流行が拡大中で、過去最大規模になる恐れがあり、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 感染は6州（イトゥリ州、北キブ州、南キブ州、ツショピ州など）に拡大しており、武力衝突や国境規制により対応が困難な状況。MSFなど国際支援団体が既に治療拠点を運営している。

article.articleHeadline: Hà Nội phát động tháng cao điểm phòng chống sốt xuất huyết hiệu quả năm 2026
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Hanoi launches the peak month for effective dengue prevention and control in 2026.
article.articleSummary: Hanoi launches a peak month for dengue prevention and control in 2026, spanning August 15–September 15, with ongoing environmental sanitation and larval control campaigns through November. Free health checks for all students begin August 18. The city aims to prevent dengue outbreaks and ensure timely patient care; the Health Department leads clinical triage, cross‑facility treatment protocols, and guarantees medicines, IV fluids, and blood products. Local authorities will implement the ‘4 at chỗ’ approach, identify and contain transmission zones, and address high‑risk areas, including construction sites and worker camps. The Education Department orders weekly school cleanups and removal of standing water; Construction monitors worker camps and water‑ponds; Public Security supports access for spraying and environmental work. Communications and mass organizations heighten awareness and encourage prompt medical attention. Hanoi maintains a 24/7 drainage system with about 200 suction vehicles and 129+ specialized cars/excavators for flood response.

triage.headline_ja: ハノイ、2026年デング熱対策のピーク月間を発動
triage.triage_reason: ハノイ市が例年の季節的なデング熱対策キャンペーンを実施しているという行政広報であり、異常な流行拡大や重症例増加の報告はないが、デング熱はベトナムで毎年流行する感染症のため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 本記事は具体的な感染者数や死亡者数を含まない行政の予防キャンペーン発表であり、季節性のデング熱対策の一環。異常な発生報告ではないためPICKUPには至らない。

article.articleHeadline: वर्षा ऋतु में संचारी बीमारियों की रोकथाम हेतु फागिंग अभियान जारी,लाल बहादुर शास्त्री एवं इंदिरा गांधी वार्ड में चला वृहद फागिंग अभियान
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Fogging campaign continues to prevent communicable diseases during the monsoon season; a large-scale fogging campaign was carried out in the Lal Bahadur Shastri and Indira Gandhi wards.
article.articleSummary: As of 19 August 2026, Katni municipal authorities are sustaining a large-scale fogging campaign to prevent vector-borne diseases during the monsoon. Rain-induced waterlogging and humidity raise mosquito breeding, elevating risks of dengue, malaria and other mosquito-borne illnesses. Health teams have conducted extensive fogging in Lal Bahadur Shastri ward and Indira Gandhi ward, targeting residential areas, lanes, and other moisture-prone locations. Alongside fogging, officials are monitoring waterlogged spots and carrying out cleaning to reduce breeding habitats. The aim is proactive, preventive measures to safeguard public health during rainfall and to maintain regular fogging and rapid action on complaints. Residents are urged to avoid standing water around homes by cleaning coolers, pots, tanks, and other water containers. Collective participation is essential to effectively control vector-borne diseases in the monsoon.

article.articleHeadline: Kongo Demokratik Cumhuriyeti'nde Ebola Vakaları 5 Bini Aştı

The Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain is circulating, and there is no approved specific treatment or vaccine for this strain. Transmission occurs through direct contact with body fluids of an infected person or the deceased. Common symptoms include fever, vomiting, and diarrhea, with severe cases leading to internal and external bleeding. Health authorities continue outbreak surveillance and implement necessary control measures to curb spread in the DRC.

article.articleHeadline: Dugaan Keracunan MBG di Kulon Progo, Dinkes Temukan 6 Jenis Bakteri pada Muntahan Siswa
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Suspected MBG poisoning in Kulon Progo, the Health Office found six types of bacteria in students' vomit.
article.articleSummary: Kulon Progo Health Office in DI Yogyakarta reports suspected MBG poisoning after four student vomit samples tested positive for Staphylococcus aureus and other bacteria—Enterobacter, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Streptococcus, and Serratia. One student’s stool sample yielded Escherichia coli. Food samples were insufficient for testing, preventing direct links between bacteria and MBG meals, though epidemiological analysis was conducted to identify likely menu associations. Multivariate analysis identified barbecue chicken as the most strongly linked item, with an adjusted odds ratio of 10.47 (p<0.001). Officials caution that this does not prove barbecue chicken as the source due to the lack of adequate food samples for comparison. Reported symptoms include abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, and vomiting mirroring the affected students’ presentation. Investigation concerns the Free Nutritious Meals (MBG) program in Kulon Progo, DI Yogyakarta, as of 19 August 2026.

triage.headline_ja: クロンプロゴでのMBG食中毒疑い、保健局が学生の嘔吐物から6種類の細菌を検出

triage.notes: 国家的な学校給食プログラム(MBG)に関連する食中毒事案であり、地元保健当局が調査中。国際的な公衆衛生上の脅威とは考えにくいが、プログラムの信頼性に関する国内政治的関心はある可能性がある。

article.articleHeadline: الكونغو.. 5000 حالة إيبولا وجهود الاستجابة عاجزة عن كبحه

article.articleHeadline: تفشى إيبولا فى الكونغو يتجاوز 5 آلاف حالة.. وتحذيرات من انتشار سريع |
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Congo has surpassed 5,000 cases, with warnings of rapid spread.
article.articleSummary: As of 19 August 2026, Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 5,000 cases with 2,378 deaths (5,021 cases, 2,378 fatalities) per the health ministry, cited by Associated Press. The outbreak’s eastern provinces face compounded control problems due to ongoing conflict and damaged infrastructure, reflecting a long history of Ebola in the DRC, including a major 2018 outbreak that lasted about two years.

article.articleHeadline: अफ्रीकी देश कांगो में नहीं थम रहा इबोला प्रकोप, 5000 पार हुई पीड़ितों की संख्या
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the African country Congo continues unabated, with the number of victims crossing 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola caused by Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) remains a public health emergency of international concern, with 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths (case fatality rate 47.4%) as of Sunday. The outbreak is the second-largest and fastest-spreading on record, across six provinces and 55 health zones, centered in Ituri Province which accounts for about 84.8% of cases. Despite intense response, high mortality, deaths outside treatment centers, and surveillance gaps signal ongoing transmission. No Bundibugyo-specific vaccine or treatment exists yet; two vaccines are in human trials under WHO collaboration, and remdesivir plus an experimental monoclonal antibody MBP134, and their combinations, are being evaluated. An oral antiviral, obeldesivir, is studied for post-exposure prophylaxis. Officials are assessing whether the licensed Ervebo vaccine for Zaire ebolavirus provides cross-protection. Imported-case risk to Uganda, South Sudan, and the Central African Republic remains very high.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカ・コンゴのエボラ流行が収まらず、被害者数が5000人を超える

article.articleHeadline: WHO chief says the DR Congo's Ebola outbreak remains a global emergency
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak remains a global health emergency, WHO chief Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on 2026-08-19, with the epidemic spreading faster than any prior flare and continuing to pose a high risk of regional spread. Almost 5,000 people have been infected and more than 2,300 have died since mid-May, making it the deadliest outbreak in the country's history. The Bundibugyo strain behind this surge causes a haemorrhagic fever; there is no specific vaccine or treatment, though clinical trials are underway. The outbreak has reached six provinces in the north and east, including the epicentre Ituri, where state presence is weak and fighting with armed groups limits access. Increased cases and deaths are attributed to unsafe areas and misinformation fueling community resistance. Transmission occurs via contact with bodily fluids; deaths at home and in communities, outside treatment centres and outside known contact lists remain a major concern. The WHO emergency committee met again, with new recommendations to come and international support urged.

triage.headline_ja: WHO事務局長、コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱流行は依然として世界的緊急事態であると発言
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目中3項目が該当し、WHOがグローバル・ヘルス・エマージェンシーとして継続的に警告している重大なエボラ出血熱流行であり、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo株によるエボラ出血熱流行で、2026年5月中旬以降約5000人感染、2300人超死亡と同国史上最悪の流行。武装勢力との衝突によりアクセスが制限され、コミュニティの抵抗も感染拡大要因となっている。WHO緊急委員会が再招集され、新たな勧告と国際支援が求められている。

article.articleHeadline: Количество заболевших Эболой в Демократической Республике Конго резко увеличилось
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of people infected with Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has risen sharply.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surged, with more than 5,000 people infected and 2,378 deaths (case fatality rate ~47.3%). The current outbreak began in May in both DRC and Uganda and now spans six DRC provinces, with Ituri as the epicenter; Uganda’s outbreak was officially declared over in late July. The virus is from the rare Bundibugyo ebolavirus species, for which a vaccine is in clinical trials. The World Health Organization has declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. The 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak remains the deadliest, claiming over 11,000 lives. The first Ebola case in DRC occurred in 1976, and this marks the 17th outbreak. Emergency Coordinator Tierno Balde called for additional resources to strengthen response. Symptoms include fever, headache, and muscle pains; authorities advise seeking care promptly and strict use of personal protective equipment and hygiene measures, especially in the outbreak zone.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ感染者数が急増
triage.triage_reason: 5000人超の感染、致死率約47%、WHOがPHEICを宣言しているなど、公衆衛生上深刻かつ国際的拡大リスクが高い事例であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: ウガンダでの流行は7月末に終息宣言済みのため、verified_locationsにはDRCのみを含めた。WHOはPHEICを宣言済みであり、フルリスク評価が必要な事例。

article.articleHeadline: Reuters сообщило о более 5 тыс. случаях заболевания Эболой в ДР Конго
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Reuters reported more than 5,000 cases of Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: As of Aug 19, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reports its 17th Ebola outbreak, now the largest in the country by case count and the second-largest globally. Government data indicate 5,021 Ebola virus disease cases and 2,378 deaths, recorded over the latest weekend. The outbreak surpasses the 2018–2020 Congo outbreaks and remains behind the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak in total infections and fatalities. There are no approved vaccines or therapeutics for this outbreak. Initial transmission is linked to a spillover from animals to humans, but authorities have not identified the animal reservoir.

triage.headline_ja: ロイター、コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱の感染者が5000人を超えたと報道
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で過去最大規模（5,021例、死者2,378人）のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクが発生しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが付与されているが、記事サマリーではDRCのみが主題であり、Angolaへの拡大は明記されていないため除外した。ワクチン・治療薬未承認、動物リザーバー未特定であり、今後の続報を要する。

article.articleHeadline: Smrtonosna epidemija širi se neviđenom brzinom: Umrlo više od 2320 ljudi, a lijeka i cjepiva još nema
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A deadly epidemic is spreading at an unprecedented speed: More than 2,320 people have died, and there is still no cure or vaccine.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo is battling a deadly Ebola epidemic with over 5,000 confirmed cases and more than 2,320 deaths. The WHO has declared the outbreak a global health emergency. This is the 17th Ebola epidemic in DRC and the deadliest, with the toll past 2,299; multiple sites suggest undiscovered transmission chains. The Bundibugyo Ebola virus strain currently has no approved vaccine or treatment. Genetic analysis shows the virus began spreading in February, three months before the official May 17 declaration. Response is hampered by armed conflict, misinformation, mistrust of health workers, and local cultural practices. Vaccines are advancing: a volunteer received an experimental vaccine in the UK last month, and India has produced hundreds of thousands of doses developed with Oxford University, which could be deployed if trials succeed.

triage.headline_ja: 未曽有の速さで拡大する致死的な感染症流行：死者2,320人超、治療薬・ワクチンはまだない
triage.triage_reason: DRCで確認例5,000超・死者2,320人超のエボラ流行にWHOがグローバル・ヘルス・エマージェンシーを宣言しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し社会的関心も高いため。
triage.notes: インドと英国はワクチン開発・臨床試験に関する記述のみで、実際の流行発生地はDRCのみ。既にWHOが緊急事態宣言済みの既知の大規模流行であり、続報の推移確認が重要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola sprids tre gånger snabbare än tidigare
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola spreads three times faster than before.
article.articleSummary: As of 19 August 2026, Ebola virus disease caused by the Bundibugyo variant has infected 5,021 people and caused 2,378 deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, a case-fatality rate of about 47%. The outbreak is spreading about three times faster than the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic. Early cases went undetected due to Bundibugyo presenting with malaria-like symptoms, later progressing to hemorrhagic fever. There is currently no vaccine or specific treatment for Bundibugyo; two new vaccines are in human trials. Ongoing conflict in eastern DR Congo and mass displacement hinder the response, with distrust of authorities and widespread misinformation. Global funding shortfalls, including reduced aid from major donors, have left the WHO with less than half of what is needed to tackle the outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ、これまでより3倍速く拡大
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ（ブンディブジョ株）流行が5,021人感染・2,378人死亡（致死率約47%）に達し、過去の西アフリカ流行の3倍の速さで拡大しており、ワクチン・治療法未確立、資金不足、紛争による対応困難という複数の深刻な要因が確認されるため。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれるが、記事サマリーではDRCのみが主題であり、Angolaでの発生は言及されていないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC : plus de 5 000 cas et 2 378 morts, l'épidémie s'aggrave - La Presse de Tunisie
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC: more than 5,000 cases and 2,378 deaths, the outbreak is worsening.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is escalating, with 5,021 laboratory-confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths as of August 16, 2026, making it the largest Ebola outbreak in the DRC and the second-largest worldwide (behind 2014–2016 West Africa). Declared in May 2026, the 17th Ebola outbreak in the DRC has spread across six provinces, 55 health zones, amid fragile health infrastructure, population movements, insecurity, and response challenges. The outbreak is driven by the Ebola Bundibugyo virus, a strain for which no vaccine or approved specific treatment exists yet. While several vaccine and therapeutic candidates are being evaluated, none are licensed for Bundibugyo. Global and local health authorities warn that transmission remains high and containment is far from assured, requiring intensified surveillance, vaccination trials where appropriate, and strengthened public health measures.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱：5,000人以上の感染例、2,378人の死者、流行は悪化
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ(ブンディブギョ株)がDRCで6州55保健区に拡大し、5,000例超・2,378死亡と過去最大規模で、ワクチン・治療薬未承認のため国際的拡大・公衆衛生上の重大リスクがある。
triage.notes: ブンディブギョ株にはワクチン・特異的治療薬が未承認であり、致死率・拡大リスクが高い。DRC史上最大規模のエボラ流行として既にフルRRA相当の重大性を持つ。

article.articleHeadline: Sốt xuất huyết diễn biến phức tạp, một xã ghi nhận 21 ca mắc
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue fever with complex developments; a commune records 21 cases.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever outbreak escalates in Ky Hoa commune, Ha Tinh Province, Vietnam, with 21 total cases reported as of 19 August 2026. A new cluster along the boundary of Văn Miếu and Trung Thượng villages accounts for 8 cases, raising the commune’s tally to 21; previously, 5 cases in Tân Đức village formed a cluster now totaling 9. Four additional scattered cases contribute to the rise. The Ha Tĩnh CDC links the surge to high population density and poor environmental sanitation, noting unaddressed waste and water-holding containers that create Aedes mosquito breeding sites. Public health actions include intensified health education, environmental cleanup, removal of larval habitats, and targeted chemical fogging to contain transmission. The agency has supplied 19 liters of insecticide and deployed staff to guide operations. Authorities warn of potential further cases and urge residents to maintain hygiene and eliminate water-holding containers to prevent spread.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱の感染状況が複雑化、ある村で21例を記録
triage.triage_reason: ベトナム・ハティン省の一村落におけるデング熱小規模流行で、地元当局が既に対応中。国際的拡大や重篤性の情報はなく、風土病的発生の範囲内と見られるため、続報を注視する。
triage.notes: デング熱はベトナムの季節性・地域的流行病であり、本記事はハティン省Ky Hoa村における小規模クラスター（計21例）についての地方レベルの報告。死亡例や重症例の言及はなく、地元CDCが殺虫剤配布・防疫作業を実施済み。国際的な影響や渡航制限の要素は見られない。

article.articleHeadline: पता चल गया कैसे हुई बालाघाट के बैगा अंचल में 19 बच्चों की मौत; ICMR की जांच में निकला ये वायरस, 20 अगस्त से टीकाकरण का विशेष अभियान
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: It has come to light how 19 children died in Balaghat's Baiga Belt; the virus identified in ICMR's investigation, a special vaccination campaign from August 20.
article.articleSummary: In Balaghat district’s Baiga belt (including Bondari, Kundeksa, Matla, Machharda, Korka villages), investigation by ICMR and partners confirms measles as the principal cause of a deadly outbreak that claimed 19 children over about two months after many had missed routine immunisation. Earlier, malaria, cold/flu, viral illness, skin rashes, and anemia were reported. NiV Pune testing for Chandipura virus, West Nile virus, and Japanese Encephalitis virus came back negative. From June to August, a health survey across 11 villages in 3 gram panchayats screened 2,780 people, finding 236 malaria, 116 diarrhea, 160 skin diseases, and 101 fever with rash. About 152 children were admitted to the district hospital; roughly 250 treated at Birsa CSC Center; most have recovered and been discharged, with others under monitoring. A Measles-Rubella catch-up campaign will run Aug 20–25 for 9 months–10 years old in Bahar, Birsa, and Parswada blocks, adding an MR vaccine dose. A state-level team is monitoring from Bhopal.

triage.headline_ja: バラガット県バイガ地域で19人の子供が死亡した経緯が判明；ICMRの調査でウイルスが特定、8月20日から特別ワクチン接種キャンペーン実施
triage.triage_reason: 麻疹による児童19人の死亡が確認され、ICMRによる調査と大規模ワクチン接種対応が行われている。深刻な公衆衛生影響と予防接種率不足による流行しやすさが認められる。
triage.notes: 当初はマラリア、チャンディプラウイルス、西ナイルウイルス、日本脳炎ウイルスも疑われたが検査で否定され、最終的に麻疹が主因と確認された。予防接種率の低さが背景にあり、8月20日から9カ月～10歳を対象としたMR（麻疹風疹）ワクチンの追加接種キャンペーンが実施される。

article.articleHeadline: Việt Nam ghi nhận ca thứ 44 mắc giun rồng
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Vietnam records its 44th case of Guinea worm disease.
article.articleSummary: Vietnam reports its 44th Guinea worm disease (dracunculiasis) case. N.V.T., born 1977 in Mậu A commune, Lao Cai Province, presented Aug 19 at Dang Van Ngữ Hospital (Institute of Malaria, Parasite, and Zoonotic Diseases) with two left-forearm lesions and a worm longer than 20 cm previously extracted but torn by family. He is afebrile and nonsymptomatic aside from swelling; ultrasound showed subcutaneous thickening in the left forearm. No diagnostic test can detect infection before worm emergence; treatment requires complete worm removal, with care to avoid breaking the worm to prevent inflammation and infection—no specific drug exists. Vietnam has 43 prior cases since 2020; Lao Cai (26), Phú Thọ (14), Thanh Hóa (3) account for most cases, with males predominating. Preventive guidance includes keeping wounds dry, boiling drinking water, avoiding raw foods, good hand hygiene, and minimizing water exposure; authorities emphasize community surveillance and prompt medical consultation for suspicious lesions.

triage.headline_ja: ベトナムでギニアワーム病の44例目を確認
triage.triage_reason: ベトナムでの持続的なギニアワーム症例報告は疾患としては異例だが、個別軽症例であり公衆衛生上の深刻な影響や国際的拡大リスクは低い。継続的な発生状況の監視が必要。
triage.notes: ギニアワーム病はWHO撲滅プログラム対象疾患で、通常アフリカ(特にチャド・南スーダン等)で報告される。ベトナムでの2020年以降の継続的な症例発生（累計44例）は疫学的に注目すべき異常事例だが、本記事は個別症例報告であり重症度・拡大リスクは低い。過去の発生地域（Lao Cai, Phú Thọ, Thanh Hóa）の動向を継続的に注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Грозница Западног Нила у Банату: сви пацијенти имају тежи облик болести
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: West Nile fever in Banat: all patients have a more severe form of the disease.
article.articleSummary: West Nile fever is a seasonal illness transmitted by bites of infected mosquitoes. In the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina, Serbia, four confirmed cases were reported as of August 16, 2026—two in Central Banat and two in Southern Banat. The four patients (three men, one woman; average age 52) developed the neuroinvasive form (encephalitis/meningitis) requiring hospitalization. Although about 80% of infections are asymptomatic and around 20% cause a mild flu-like illness, fewer than 1% progress to severe neuroinvasive disease. Neurological symptoms include severe headache, neck stiffness, drowsiness, confusion, coma, tremor, seizures, weakness, and paralysis, more common in older individuals and those with immunosuppression or chronic diseases (diabetes, cancer, cardiovascular). Diagnosis is by infectious disease specialists using clinical evaluation and laboratory testing. The illness circulates June–November; surveillance continues.

triage.headline_ja: バナトの西ナイル熱：全患者が重症型を発症
triage.triage_reason: セルビア・ヴォイヴォディナ州で西ナイル熱の神経侵襲型症例が4例確認され重症度は高いが、対象国（India等）での発生は確認できず、社会的関心や国際的拡大の情報も不足しているため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 発生地域リストにIndia（Uttar Pradesh, Banat）が含まれるが、これはBanat（インドの地名）との地名混同によるBluedotの誤タグ付けと判断。記事本文はセルビア・ヴォイヴォディナ州（Banat地区）での発生を報じており、対象国リストに該当する国はないためverified_locationsは空とした。

article.articleHeadline: RDC : ''l'épidémie d'Ebola est loin d'être maîtrisée'', a averti l'OMS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: "The Ebola outbreak is far from being under control," the WHO warned.
article.articleSummary: DRC Ebola outbreak far from under control, WHO warns. Three months after its declaration, the outbreak has about 5,000 cases and 2,300 deaths, the deadliest in the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s history. The response is impeded by insecurity, restricted access, persistent infodemics, and community resistance, according to Dieudonné Mwamba, director of the National Institute of Public Health in the DRC. On May 17, the WHO declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. The UN agency assesses national risk as very high in the DRC, high in Uganda and neighboring countries, and low elsewhere. The response spans six provinces, with the Ituri province as the epicenter; authorities urge accelerated containment at the origin to prevent spillover. There is no vaccine or specific treatment for the Bundibugyo strain driving this surge.

triage.headline_ja: DRC:「エボラの流行は制御下にはほど遠い」とWHOが警告
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEICを宣言し、5000例・2300死亡という史上最悪規模のエボラ流行で、国際的拡大リスクや対応困難な状況が報告されているためフルRRAに進むべき事案。
triage.notes: ウガンダはリスク評価で「高」とされているが、記事の主題はDRCでの流行であり、ウガンダでの発症事例は明記されていないため、verified_locationsには含めていない。ワクチン・特異的治療法がないBundibugyo株による流行である点も重要。

article.articleHeadline: Mobile gold miners in eastern Congo complicate health workers' efforts to contain Ebola
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-19, Ebola is spreading in eastern Congo's Ituri province, where a fast-moving outbreak is concentrated. The article notes that mobile artisanal gold miners complicate containment by health workers, with hundreds of people, many of them children, at mining sites. A cited example is Isaac Batisa, an 11-year-old, illustrating how livelihoods pull people into high-risk settings amid transmission. The piece underscores challenges in surveillance and case finding as mobile populations move between sites, potentially sustaining transmission. It highlights the intersection of artisanal mining and infectious disease control in Ituri, Congo, with ongoing transmission and frontline containment efforts facing significant obstacles.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ東部の移動する金採掘者たちが、エボラ対策を行う医療従事者の努力を複雑化させている
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱はIHR基準上重大な公衆衛生上の懸念があり、移動性の高い採掘者集団により国際的拡大や制御困難のリスクが高いため、フルRRAへの移行が適切。
triage.notes: 記事はコンゴ民主共和国イツリ州でのエボラ流行に特化しており、移動性の高い金採掘者が感染制御を困難にしている点を強調している。

article.articleHeadline: Կոնգոյում էբոլայով հիվանդացածների թիվը գերազանցել է 5000-ը
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Congo, the number of people ill with Ebola has surpassed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has infected 5,021 people and caused 2,378 deaths (case-fatality 47.3%). The current outbreak began May 15 in DRC and Uganda, spreading across six provinces with Ituri as the epicenter. Uganda declared the outbreak over on July 28. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain is involved, with a vaccine still in early clinical trials. The World Health Organization has declared a public health emergency of international concern for the outbreak. This is the second-deadliest Ebola outbreak in Africa’s history; the largest occurred in 2014–2016 in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone, with fatalities exceeding 11,000. Ebola transmits from wildlife to humans; the first human case in the DRC was recorded in 1976, and this is the 17th Ebola outbreak in the country.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ感染者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 致死率47.3%の大規模エボラ流行がWHOによりPHEIC宣言されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: 記事はDRC（イトゥリ州を中心）での流行を主題としており、ウガンダは既に終息宣言済み。シエラレオネ・リベリア・ギニアは2014-2016年の過去流行の比較として言及されているのみで現行事例ではないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: L'épidémie d'Ebola en RDC dépasse 5000 cas et progresse à un rythme sans précédent | L'actualité
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in the DRC surpasses 5,000 cases and progresses at an unprecedented pace.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 cases, with 5,021 infections and 2,378 deaths reported as of 2026-08-19, making it the fastest-spreading and most deadly Ebola outbreak in history. The epidemic has spread about three times faster than the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak, which caused more than 11,000 deaths. The World Health Organization warned that the risk of cross-border and international spread remains high and that the outbreak is far from controlled. Security challenges hinder the response, with health workers frequently targeted, especially in Ituri, the province hardest hit. On Monday, a health team in Aru territory was attacked after a suspected case was reported; a crowd burned an ambulance and damaged two other vehicles, according to Michael Wani, president of the Union of Cultural Associations for the Development of Ituri.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ流行、5000例を超え前例のない速度で拡大
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRCで5,000例超・死者2,378人と過去最速のペースで拡大し、WHOも国境を越えた国際的拡大リスクを警告しているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: Angolaは発生地域に含まれるが記事本文では言及がなく、越境拡大リスクとしてWHOが警告しているのみで実際の発生確認ではないため verified_locations には含めていない。治安悪化により対応チームが襲撃される等、対応の困難さも報告されている。
