article.articleHeadline: H1N1 cases up in Aug, highest monthly count this year
article.articleSummary: Gurgaon city, Haryana, India, recorded seven H1N1 (swine flu) cases in August 2026 so far, lifting Jan–Aug totals to 21. August is the year’s highest monthly count; monthly pattern: 3 (Jan), 2 (Feb), 3 (Mar), 0 (Apr–May), 3 (Jun), 3 (Jul), 7 (Aug). Officials caution that numbers are too small to confirm a sustained rise; September figures will indicate trend. Patients show flu-like symptoms: fever up to 103°F, chills, sore throat, cough, runny or blocked nose, with some nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea; headaches and fatigue also common. Laboratory confirmation is important to distinguish H1N1 from other influenza. Most healthy individuals have self-limiting illness; antivirals for severe cases; antibiotics only if bacterial infection suspected. Preventive measures: masks in crowded or poorly ventilated spaces, hand hygiene, avoid touching eyes/nose/mouth, ventilation, staying home when symptomatic and seeking care for persistent fever, breathing difficulties, or low oxygen.

triage.headline_ja: 8月にH1N1症例数が増加、今年最多の月間件数
triage.triage_reason: 季節性H1N1インフルエンザの通常範囲内の増加であり、当局も「傾向確認には数が少なすぎる」としている。異常性・重症度・国際的拡大リスクいずれも認められず、既知の病原体で対応も国内で可能。
triage.notes: 季節性H1N1インフルエンザの月次症例報告であり、既知の疾患パターン内の変動。当局自身も統計的に有意な増加傾向とは断定していない。

article.articleHeadline: Brote de ébola en Congo supera los 5,000 contagios
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in Congo surpasses 5,000 infections
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, caused by the rare Bundibugyo variant, has exceeded 5,000 confirmed infections and 2,378 deaths, making it the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country's history. As of Sunday, the Congolese Ministry of Health had recorded 5,021 cases and 2,378 fatalities, with nearly half of those infected dying. The surge occurs amid ongoing difficulties in tracing exposed individuals and containing transmission, emphasizing the strained public health response in the affected region. The Bundibugyo variant is a rare Ebola strain, complicating surveillance and containment efforts. The outbreak has heightened regional health alerts and response measures. This update reflects the situation as of 2026-08-19.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱、感染者5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約47%、5000人超の感染と2378人の死亡という大規模かつ深刻な公衆衛生インパクトがあり、IHR基準の複数項目に該当するため。
triage.notes: 希少なブンディブギョ株による過去最悪規模のエボラ流行。接触者追跡と感染制御が困難な状況が継続しており、国際的な支援と警戒レベルの引き上げが必要と考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: Ебола в ДР Конго: Жертвите на ебола са близо 2400 | Новини.бг
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in DR Congo: Ebola victims are near 2,400
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo reaches 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths since mid-May, affecting 55 health zones across Haut-Uele, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Bas-Uele, and Chopo. Ituri remains the epicenter with ongoing transmission. The government calls for intensified, consistent public communication to counter misinformation and ensure adherence to health measures. To curb spread toward Kinshasa, authorities have strengthened surveillance along the Congo River about 65 km (40 miles) from the capital, with a health post monitoring boats from affected areas, according to Health Minister Samuel Roger Kampamba. The World Health Organization states this outbreak remains a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱：死者数約2,400人に
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で5,021人の確定例、2,378人の死亡が報告され、WHOはPHEIC（国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態）を継続中と表明。首都キンシャサへの拡大リスクも監視されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: WHOがPHEICを継続していると明言しており、キンシャサへの拡大防止のためコンゴ川沿いの監視が強化されている。55の保健区に影響が及ぶ大規模なアウトブレイクであり、既にフルRRAの対象となる可能性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: الكونغو... عددٌ إصابات فيروس 'إيبولا' يتجاوز 5 آلاف
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo... the number of Ebola virus infections exceeds 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has exceeded 5,000 infections, according to an Africa CDC health authority, as of August 19, 2026. The current outbreak, the seventeenth in DRC, has caused 2,378 deaths among 5,021 confirmed cases, with officials noting the outbreak began spreading weeks before it was declared on May 15. Previously, the 2018–2020 outbreak in DRC was the deadliest on record, with 2,299 deaths among 3,381 confirmed cases. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned that the risk of continued spread remains high at national and international levels. Ebola is transmitted via contact with body fluids and causes hemorrhagic fever; no approved vaccines or treatments exist for the current Bundibugyo strain, though clinical trials are ongoing. Africa CDC cites testing reluctance by some communities as a surveillance and containment obstacle.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ…エボラウイルス感染者数が5000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCで進行中の第17次エボラ流行が5,000人感染・死亡率約47%に達し、WHO事務局長が国内・国際的な拡大リスクを警告しているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: 2018-2020年流行を超える死者数を記録し、承認されたワクチン・治療法が存在しないBundibugyo株による流行。コミュニティの検査への抵抗感が監視・封じ込めの障害となっている。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC : le bilan grimpe à 5 021 cas et 2 378 décès - LePotentiel
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC: the toll rises to 5,021 cases and 2,378 deaths - LePotentiel
article.articleSummary: Ebola disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) caused by the Bundibugyo strain escalates, with 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths (case fatality 47.4%) as of 19 August 2026. 751 patients are isolated or hospitalized and 1,061 have recovered; contact tracing is at 82.2%. The outbreak began in Ituri Province in May 2026 and has spread to multiple regions, becoming the largest Ebola epidemic in the DRC with dozens of health zones affected, per WHO data through July. Week 30 recorded 567 new cases and 296 deaths, the highest weekly totals to date. There is currently no licensed vaccine or specific treatment for Bundibugyo; management relies on rapid case identification, isolation, supportive care, testing, contact tracing, infection prevention, and safe burials, with strong community engagement. Uganda reported the outbreak’s end on 28 July; cross-border coordination and reinforced surveillance are emphasized, while WHO monitors risk and convenes an Emergency Committee (Aug 18, 2026).

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱：感染者数5,021人、死者数2,378人に増加
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国史上最大規模のエボラ流行（Bundibugyo株）で、致死率47.4%、ウガンダへの越境拡大歴があり、WHO緊急委員会が招集されている。IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ移行すべき。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの越境拡大が記載されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。ウガンダ側は7月28日に流行終息を報告済み。WHO緊急委員会が2026年8月18日に招集された点が重要な社会的関心の指標。

article.articleHeadline: Hortolândia faz ação contra Aedes em duas regiões
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Hortolândia takes action against Aedes aegypti in two regions
article.articleSummary: Hortolândia continues eliminating Aedes aegypti breeding sites in Jardim Nova Hortolândia and Parque Bella Ville this week, led by the Zoonoses Surveillance Unit (UVZ) of the Health Secretariat amid a heat advisory from the state Civil Defense. The two regions recorded high ADL in July. Door-to-door inspections target and remove breeding sites and educate residents on preventing mosquito reproduction. UVZ states about 80% of breeding sites are inside homes, and residents are asked to allow entry for the work; teams wear badges and uniforms. For verification of routes, residents can contact UVZ at (19) 3897-3312 or (19) 3897-5974. Dengue vaccination is available at Basic Health Units (UBS) from 7:30 to 15:30, with seven units offering extended hours: until 17:30 at Amanda II, Dom Bruno Gamberini, Rosolém, Santa Clara; until 18:30 at Amanda I, Figueiras, Parque do Horto.

triage.headline_ja: オルトランジアが2地域でネッタイシマカ対策を実施
triage.triage_reason: 自治体レベルの日常的な蚊媒介対策・予防接種活動に関する記事であり、異常な発生増加や重症例の報告はなく、社会的関心の高まりも確認できない。
triage.notes: 記事は特定都市（Hortolândia, São Paulo州）での日常的なデング熱媒介蚊対策・ワクチン接種案内であり、感染拡大の異常事態を示す内容ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Peptídeos avançam contra Salmonella como alternativa para segurança alimentar
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Peptides advance against Salmonella as an alternative for ensuring food safety.
article.articleSummary: Brazilian HYH Biotechnology unveiled a platform of engineered antimicrobial peptides targeting Salmonella, with laboratory results showing initial control in about two hours and suppression of new colonies for more than four days. The platform was also evaluated against Escherichia coli and Listeria monocytogenes, achieving roughly 95% degradation of biofilms. Built from about four years of bioinformatics, computational modeling, peptide engineering, and validation, the approach uses multiple rationally designed peptides rather than a single molecule. Pending industrial validation, applications could span slaughterhouses, incubators, poultry farms, dairies, and egg-processing facilities in Brazil, aiming to strengthen hygiene, reduce cross-contamination and losses, and meet Brazilian and international market requirements. The technology is patent-protected and may form a base for multiple biosafety products. A cited study notes direct recall costs can reach US$10 million.

triage.headline_ja: ペプチドが食品安全のための代替策としてサルモネラ対策で進展
triage.triage_reason: 実際の感染症発生事例ではなく、ブラジルの企業による抗菌ペプチド技術の開発に関する記事であり、公衆衛生上のシグナルとは無関係。
triage.notes: 本記事は特定の感染症発生事例を報告するものではなく、食品安全技術（抗菌ペプチド）の研究開発ニュースである。

article.articleHeadline: RDC : " Le paludisme demeure jusqu'à ce jour un problème majeur de santé publique " (Chercheur) - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: "Malaria remains to this day a major public health problem" (Researcher) - ACP.
article.articleSummary: As of 19 August 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) still faces malaria as a major public health problem. A thesis by Michel Itabu notes that DRC ranks just behind Nigeria for malaria morbidity and mortality, together accounting for about half of the global burden. Malaria is described as a communication-related disease; despite wide awareness campaigns and interventions, its prevalence and incidence remain high. Dr. Pagès calls malaria a closed disease, with its etiologic agent effectively confined within the human body. Health professionals are advised to suspect malaria in cases of acute fever. A major challenge is the sale of counterfeit antimalarials. Other weaknesses include low health funding, population underestimation of malaria, non-adherence to free distributions of insecticide-treated nets and the distribution of ineffective nets. World Mosquito Day honors Ronald Ross's 1897 discovery and reinforces vector-control efforts to protect vulnerable populations.

triage.headline_ja: DRC:「マラリアは今日まで公衆衛生上の重大な問題である」（研究者）- ACP
triage.triage_reason: 既知の風土病であるマラリアに関する一般的な公衆衛生課題を論じた研究者の見解記事であり、新規性・異常性・国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: ナイジェリアも言及されているが対象国リストに含まれないため除外。記事は既存の風土病の構造的課題（偽薬、資金不足、蚊帳配布の問題等）を論じたもので、突発的なアウトブレイクではない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: médica de Médicos Sem Fronteiras vê cenário mais complexo do que na epidemia de 2014
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: a Doctors Without Borders doctor sees a more complex scenario than during the 2014 outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), declared in May 2026, has infected over 5,000 people and caused 2,378 deaths, the largest in the DRC and advancing faster than prior outbreaks. MSF doctor Rachel Soeiro, speaking at a conference in Brasília on August 18, 2026, says the current scenario is at least as complex as the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic. There are no vaccines or approved treatments for the Bundibugyo strain driving this outbreak, and studies suggest immunizations and therapies developed after 2014 may not be effective against it; vaccine and therapy stocks are largely under U.S. government control. The conflict-affected region has displaced thousands, hindering access to care, and there are no rapid diagnostic tests, delaying diagnosis, isolation, and surveillance. Soeiro calls for pre-positioned stockpiles, ongoing research, strong community engagement, and sustaining other health services (births, vaccines, TB, HIV, malaria) with PPE for health workers.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：国境なき医師団の医師が2014年の流行より複雑な状況と指摘
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で2026年5月に宣言されたエボラ出血熱の流行が5000人超の感染・2378人の死亡に達し、同国史上最大規模で拡大速度も速く、有効なワクチン・治療薬がないため国際的な公衆衛生上の重大リスクと判断される。
triage.notes: ブラジル(ブラジリア)は会議開催地であり、実際の発生地域ではないためverified_locationsから除外。アンゴラも記事本文で発生地として言及されていないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Journée mondiale du moustique : 26 millions de cas de paludisme enregistrés en RDC (Par Héritier Matenga) - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Mosquito Day: 26 million malaria cases recorded in the DRC (By Héritier Matenga) - ACP
article.articleSummary: Malaria in the Democratic Republic of the Congo totaled 26,064,143 cases and 29,938 deaths in 2025, making it the leading cause of illness and mortality nationwide. According to PNLP data and the Severe Malaria Observatory, the DRC accounts for more than half of Central Africa’s malaria burden. The disease disproportionately affects children under five and pregnant women, with humanitarian crises in the east (notably North Kivu) driving crowded camps and heightened transmission. Prevention remains vital: systematic use of insecticide-treated nets, elimination of standing water, and regular environmental sanitation. While new tools, including targeted vaccination campaigns, offer hope, they do not replace traditional measures. World Mosquito Day on 20 August underscores the urgent need for strengthened funding and sustained prevention to save millions of lives in the DRC.

triage.headline_ja: 世界蚊の日：コンゴ民主共和国でマラリア症例2,600万件を記録（エリティエ・マテンガ記者）- ACP
triage.triage_reason: マラリアはDRCで既知の風土病であり、本記事は世界蚊の日に合わせた年間統計の公表に過ぎず新規異常事象ではないが、死亡者数・患者数の規模は大きく、資金や支援強化の必要性が示唆されているため継続的な注視が必要。
triage.notes: 本記事は世界蚊の日（8月20日）に合わせた年次統計・啓発記事であり、新規のアウトブレイクや異常事象を報告するものではない。北キブ州等の人道危機による感染拡大リスクは指摘されているが、具体的な急性の公衆衛生上の異常事態としての記述はない。

article.articleHeadline: عدد مصابي إيبولا في الكونغو الديموقراطية يتجاوز الـ5000... - الوكيل الإخباري
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpasses 5,000.
article.articleSummary: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ebola cases have surpassed 5,000, with 2,378 deaths among 5,021 confirmed infections, according to Africa CDC. The outbreak, the seventeenth in the country, was declared on May 15, though spread likely began weeks earlier, affecting northern and eastern regions where state presence is weak and health infrastructure is almost non-existent amid ongoing conflict. A previous 2018–2020 outbreak was the deadliest, with 2,299 deaths from 3,381 cases, per WHO data. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned that the risk of further spread remains high domestically and internationally. The virus is transmitted via contact with body fluids and causes hemorrhagic fever; the current outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain, for which no licensed vaccines or treatments exist, though clinical trials are ongoing. The government’s response has faced criticism for slowness and disorganization amid public distrust.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ感染者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で発生中のエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）が5,000例・死亡2,378例に達し、WHOが国内外への拡大リスクを警告しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 現行の第17次アウトブレイクは治療薬・承認済みワクチンが存在しないブンディブギョ株によるもので、紛争地域における医療体制の脆弱性が拡大リスクを高めている。

article.articleHeadline: Joaquim Felício reforça ações de prevenção e combate ao Aedes aegypti
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Joaquim Felício reinforces prevention and control measures against Aedes aegypti.
article.articleSummary: Drone-assisted aerial mapping over a 10-hectare area in Joaquim Felício enhances surveillance and prevention against arboviruses. The effort targets Aedes aegypti, the mosquito that transmits dengue, Zika, and chikungunya, by identifying potential water-collection sites and conditions conducive to breeding. The technology broadens observers' capacity to pinpoint areas needing attention and strengthens preventive work against outbreaks. The initiative underscores continuous vigilance in vector control and the importance of community participation; residents are urged to keep yards, plots, and outdoor spaces free of containers that can hold water, reducing breeding opportunities. With drone data complementing field teams, Joaquim Felício reinforces its commitment to population health and to reducing transmission risk as of 2026-08-19.

triage.headline_ja: ジョアキン・フェリシオ市、ネッタイシマカ対策の予防・防除活動を強化
triage.triage_reason: デング熱等の媒介蚊対策としての予防的な行政活動の紹介であり、発生や症例増加の報告ではないため、シグナルとしての重要性は低い。
triage.notes: 記事は地方自治体によるドローンを用いた蚊の発生源調査という予防活動の紹介であり、具体的な症例数や流行状況の報告は含まれていない。

article.articleHeadline: الكونغو الديمقراطية تسجل أكثر من 5 آلاف إصابة بـ"إيبولا" و2378 وفاة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Democratic Republic of the Congo records more than 5,000 Ebola cases and 2,378 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 cases with 2,378 deaths, according to Africa CDC data through 2026-08-19, representing the largest outbreak in the country’s history. A total of 5,021 confirmed infections and 2,378 fatalities have been recorded since the outbreak was declared in May, the 17th Ebola flare-up in the DRC. Northern and eastern regions are most affected, where weak health infrastructure and ongoing armed conflict hinder response efforts. The World Health Organization warns that the risk of further spread remains high both domestically and internationally, with containment hampered by community resistance to testing. By comparison, the 2018–2020 outbreak caused 3,381 cases and 2,299 deaths, underscoring the persistent severity of Ebola in the region.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、エボラ感染5,000人超・死者2,378人を記録
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRC史上最大規模の流行となり、致死率も高く国際的拡大リスクがWHOにより指摘されているため、IHR基準の複数項目に該当する。
triage.notes: 史上最大規模のエボラ流行であり、武力衝突や検査への地域住民の抵抗が対応を妨げているとWHOが警告。国際的な支援と監視の継続が必要。

article.articleHeadline: DSÖ: KDC'de Ebola salgını, uluslararası öneme sahip "halk sağlığı acil durumu" olmaya devam ediyor
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO: Ebola outbreak in the DRC remains a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.
article.articleSummary: The World Health Organization states that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Ituri Province, near the Ebola River) remains a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) per the Emergency Committee’s latest advice. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus announced via X that, despite ongoing containment efforts, the international community should intensify support and resource mobilization to protect communities in the coming months. The outbreak was declared on May 15 after 246 suspected cases and 65 deaths were reported in eastern DRC. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus variant causing the outbreak has no approved treatment or vaccine. Updated guidance for the DRC and other at-risk countries is expected in the coming days as authorities coordinate responses.

triage.headline_ja: WHO：コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ流行、国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態(PHEIC)が継続
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEICを継続表明しており、致死率の高いエボラ出血熱の流行拡大リスクと国際支援の必要性が明確であるため、フルRRAへ進めるべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: WHOがPHEICを継続宣言していることから既にIHR通知相当のイベントであり、ワクチン・治療薬未承認のBundibugyo型エボラウイルスによる流行が続いている点にも留意。

article.articleHeadline: Febre maculosa faz interior do Rio ficar em alerta | | O Dia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rocky Mountain spotted fever puts Rio de Janeiro's interior on alert
article.articleSummary: Rocky Mountain spotted fever outbreaks in Rio de Janeiro state, Brazil, mainly in the Norte and Noroeste Fluminense regions, with four deaths this year and 14 statewide. In São Fidélis, the latest fatality occurred in early August following two prior deaths there; other fatalities occurred in Itaperuna (two) and Campos dos Goytacazes (one). Laboratory confirmation by Lacen and Fiocruz linked the death of veterinarian Gabriel Serra, 30, to Rickettsia rickettsii. The state mobilized a regional public health response, including environmental vector control focused on the star tick around Bonsucesso on the RJ-158 corridor, plus surveillance, education, and guidance to residents. Fiocruz estimates a 28% case fatality for the current outbreak. From 2024-2025, 46 infections/19 deaths and 33 infections/14 deaths; 2026 so far: 14 cases, 4 deaths. Symptoms: high fever, severe headache, myalgias, nausea, abdominal pain; rash on palms/soles later. Antibiotics should start at first suspicion.

triage.headline_ja: リオデジャネイロ内陸部でロッキー山紅斑熱が警戒レベルに
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル・リオデジャネイロ州で紅斑熱（ロッキー山紅斑熱）による複数死亡例と28%の致死率が報告され、州当局が緊急のベクター対策・監視体制を強化しているため、深刻度と社会的関心の観点からピックアップと判断。
triage.notes: ロッキー山紅斑熱（紅斑熱、Rickettsia rickettsii感染）はダニ媒介性疾患であり、ヒト-ヒト感染はない。リオデジャネイロ州北部・北西部地域で例年発生している地域流行病だが、今年の致死率(28%)が高く、州レベルでの緊急対応が行われている点が注目される。

article.articleHeadline: Escola estadual em João Pessoa suspende aulas após casos de catapora
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: State school in João Pessoa suspends classes after cases of chickenpox.
article.articleSummary: Nine students from various grades at Escola Estadual de Ensino Fundamental e Médio Desembargador Boto de Menezes in the 13 de Maio neighborhood of João Pessoa, Paraíba, Brazil, have been diagnosed with varicella (chickenpox). Classes were temporarily suspended as a preventive measure to curb spread among students and staff. The health status of the students was not disclosed. On Aug 19, the school and the Gerência Executiva das Escolas Integrais met to devise a contingency plan and outline measures to control the situation. This reflects a proactive public health response by the state Department of Education to identified chickenpox cases in the school setting.

triage.headline_ja: ジョアン・ペソアの州立学校、水痘（水疱瘡）の発生により休校
triage.triage_reason: 水痘は一般的な感染症であり、学校単位の限定的な発生で重症化や国際的拡大のリスクは低い。社会的関心も限定的。
triage.notes: 水痘は小児に多い一般的な感染症で、学校内での限定的な集団発生。学校側は予防的措置として休校を実施しているが、重篤な健康被害の報告はない。

article.articleHeadline: Cruzeiro do Sul tem queda de 84% nos casos de dengue
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Cruzeiro do Sul records an 84% drop in dengue cases.
article.articleSummary: Cruzeiro do Sul, Acre, Brazil, posted an 84% drop in probable dengue cases in 2026 compared with the same period in 2025, based on epidemiological weeks 1–32 and updated through Tuesday, Aug 18. A total of 2,547 notifications were recorded, with 2,161 discarded, 215 confirmed, and 171 under investigation; overall, 386 probable cases versus 2,450 in the prior year. The reduction is attributed to sustained vector-control work and community cooperation. The health surveillance coordinator notes 53 active neighborhoods and about 1,025 blocks visited daily by endemic agents. Persistent breeding sites include ground-level water tanks and small containers that accumulate water; these should be kept sealed and eliminated whenever feasible. Despite the decline, residents with fever, headache, body pains, or red spots are urged to seek care at a health facility.

triage.headline_ja: クルゼイロ・ド・スルでデング熱症例が84%減少
triage.triage_reason: デング熱症例数が前年比84%減少という改善傾向を示す内容であり、公衆衛生上の懸念や異常事態を示すものではない。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はブラジル・アクレ州クルゼイロ・ド・スルにおけるデング熱症例の大幅な減少であり、対象国リストにブラジルは含まれるが、内容は改善報告であり、シグナルとして拾う必要性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: "إيبولا" يفتك بالكونغو.. 5000 وفاة في التفشي الأسوأ تاريخياً
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola ravages Congo... 5,000 deaths in the worst outbreak in history.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has reached 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths as of 2026-08-19, the largest outbreak in Kinshasa’s history. The outbreak is linked to Bundibugyo ebolavirus, with the May 15 declaration marking the 17th Ebola outbreak in the DRC, though spread likely began weeks earlier. Transmission occurs via contact with bodily fluids, causing hemorrhagic fever with fever and other symptoms typical of Ebola. The North and East regions are hardest hit, where state presence is weak and health infrastructure is nearly non-existent amid decades of armed conflict. No licensed vaccines or treatments exist for Bundibugyo; clinical trials are ongoing. Authorities face challenges including community resistance to testing, complicating surveillance and control, while WHO warns the national and international risk remains high.

triage.headline_ja: 「エボラ」がコンゴを破壊…史上最悪のアウトブレイクで5000人死亡
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大規模のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク（5,021例、2,378死亡）が発生し、WHOが国内外のリスクを高いと警告しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: Bundibugyoエボラウイルスによる史上最大のキンシャサでのアウトブレイクとされ、ワクチン・治療法未承認、コミュニティの検査拒否等サーベイランス上の課題あり。WHOが国内外リスクを高いと評価。

article.articleHeadline: У Конго від Еболи померли понад 2400 людей, кількість випадків перевищила 5000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Congo, Ebola has killed more than 2,400 people, with the number of cases exceeding 5,000.
article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo continues to expand, with 5,105 confirmed cases and 2,420 deaths since it began on 15 May. The case fatality rate is 47.4%. As of 17 August, 782 patients are in isolation or receiving treatment, and 1,091 have recovered. The outbreak has spread across six provinces: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, Tshopo, and Lower Uele. On 15 August, it surpassed the 2018–2020 regional epidemic in deaths and pace, reaching 5,000 cases less than two weeks after 4,000. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned it could approach the death toll of the 2014–2016 Western African outbreak (about 11,000). The WHO maintains the Public Health Emergency of International Concern status. The strain is Bundibugyo, for which there is no approved vaccine or specific treatment; lethality is 30–50%.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ出血熱により2,400人以上が死亡、感染者数は5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCにおけるエボラ流行が5,000例超・死亡2,400人超と拡大を続け、WHOがPHEIC状態を維持していることから、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: WHOはPHEIC状態を維持し、2014-2016年西アフリカ流行(約11,000人死亡)に近づく可能性がテドロス事務局長より警告されている。Bundibugyo株には承認済みワクチン・特異的治療法が存在しない点も重大なリスク要因。

article.articleHeadline: Presidente Juscelino recebe visita técnica para acompanhar ações de combate à doença de Chagas
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: President Juscelino receives a technical visit to monitor actions in the fight against Chagas disease.
article.articleSummary: Chagas disease surveillance and prevention actions intensified in Presidente Juscelino, Brazil, with a technical visit by professionals from the Sete Lagoas Regional Health Superintendent (SRS-SL) and Paula Caroline Vital Mattos Paula (UFRJ Public Health resident). The visit reviewed actions under the Chagas Disease Control Program and reinforced integration among municipal authorities, SRS-SL, Fiocruz Minas (Instituto René Rachou), UFRJ, and the municipal administration. Strategies include enhancing field operations, acquiring a suitable vehicle and motorcycle, organizing workflows, and training. Technical support from SRS-SL aims to qualify teams and sharpen response. Emphasis on knowledge exchange between public sector, health institutions, universities, and research centers, plus community participation in prevention and risk identification. The initiative underscores ongoing investment in structure, capacity building, and inter-institutional collaboration to strengthen public health policies and protect local health.

triage.headline_ja: プレジデンテ・ジュセリーノ市がシャーガス病対策の取り組みを監視するための技術訪問を受ける
triage.triage_reason: 通常のシャーガス病監視・予防プログラムの技術視察に関する記事であり、異常発生や公衆衛生上の緊急性を示す情報はない。
triage.notes: 記事はブラジル・プレジデンテ・ジュセリーノ市における既存のシャーガス病対策プログラムの技術視察・体制強化に関する内容で、新規の感染事例や流行の報告は含まれていない。

article.articleHeadline: Município reforça vigilância contra arboviroses diante da previsão de aumento das temperaturas com chegada do El Niño
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Municipality steps up surveillance for arboviral diseases in light of the forecast of rising temperatures with the arrival of El Niño.
article.articleSummary: El Niño forecasts may intensify circulation of arboviruses—dengue, Zika, and chikungunya—in the municipality. In response, the Health Ministry urged states and municipalities to boost surveillance, preventive actions, and household visits. The Municipal Health Secretariat’s Endemics Coordination maintains continuous monitoring focused on high-risk areas, with real-time ovitraps guiding resource allocation. A central monitoring unit aggregates systems to track infestation indices and direct field teams to priority zones. On August 19, agents visited the Patagônia neighborhood, identified among areas with high notification rates. Coordinator Saulo Ferreira said the municipality moved from bi-monthly to weekly monitoring, enabling rapid deployment of arbovirus control. Three main strategies are employed: focal treatment (larviciding standing water), perifocal treatment (adult-control near breeding sites), and insecticide spraying by backpack sprayers and truck-mounted fogging in critical areas.

triage.triage_reason: 既存の予防的サーベイランス強化を伝える内容であり、異常な流行や重症例の報告はなく、社会的関心の高まりも確認できない。

article.articleHeadline: مخاوف من عودته.. اعرف أعراض إنفلونزا الخنازير
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Fears of its return... Know the symptoms of swine flu.
article.articleSummary: Swine flu (influenza A H1N1) remains a global health concern after China reported a child infected, triggering fears of its return. The article notes that H1N1 symptoms mirror other influenza viruses and can appear rapidly. In this case, China confirmed a pediatric infection, though no case counts or fatalities are provided. Common symptoms described include fever (not always present), muscle pains, chills and sweating, cough, sore throat, runny or blocked nose, red eyes with tearing, eye pain, body aches, headaches, fatigue, and diarrhea. Abdominal pain and vomiting are more common in children than adults, with influenza symptoms typically developing 1 to 4 days after exposure. The piece emphasizes vigilance about potential resurgence but does not detail laboratory confirmation methods, infection source, or imported/exported case information.

triage.notes: 記事は単一小児例の報告を基にした一般的な症状解説記事であり、アウトブレイクの規模や公的機関の対応に関する情報は含まれていない。H1N1は季節性インフルエンザ株として既に定着しているため、新規性・異常性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: الكونغو تواجه أسوأ تفشٍ لإيبولا في تاريخها.. الإصابات تتجاوز 5 آلاف حالة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is facing its worst Ebola outbreak in its history; infections have surpassed 5,000 cases.
article.articleSummary: As of August 19, 2026, Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths, per Africa CDC. This is the current outbreak—the DRC's largest—declared May 15 and now the seventeenth Ebola outbreak in the country. It is driven by the Bundibugyo virus, a rare strain with no vaccines or approved treatments; clinical trials are ongoing to test preventive and therapeutic options. The infection concentrates in the northern and eastern regions where healthcare systems are weak and armed conflict persists. Public trust is eroded; many residents refuse testing, complicating contact tracing. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warns that the risk of continued spread inside the DRC and to neighboring countries remains high. Transmission occurs via contact with bodily fluids, causing fever and severe hemorrhagic fever. The current outbreak surpasses the 2018-2020 wave (3,381 cases, 2,299 deaths).

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、史上最悪のエボラ出血熱の流行に直面…感染者数5000人を超える

triage.notes: ワクチン・承認済み治療法がないBundibugyoウイルス株による流行で、武力紛争地域での対応が困難。WHOが近隣国への拡大リスクを警告している。

article.articleHeadline: Haut-Uélé : le trafic suspendu à Salisa pour limiter la propagation d'Ebola vers l'Ituri - LePotentiel
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Upper Uele: Traffic suspended at Salisa to limit the spread of Ebola to Ituri - LePotentiel
article.articleSummary: Traffic at the Salisa border post on RN26 between Haut-Uélé and Ituri has been suspended until further notice to curb movement amid a renewed Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreak in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. Interim Wamba territory administrator Christophe Taratibu Nassor ordered border controls, with enforcement by the PNC, ANR, DGM, and FARDC. The outbreak, declared on 15 May 2026, has reached more than 4,600 laboratory-confirmed cases and over 2,100 deaths. The Bundibugyo strain is implicated. Ituri and Haut-Uele are among the most affected; cases have also been detected in North Kivu, South Kivu, Tshopo, and Bas-Uele. The measure aims to strengthen epidemiological surveillance, patient management, and research into prevention and treatment. No reopening date is announced; crossing the Salisa post, crucial for people and goods along the Isiro-Wamba axis, could be disrupted pending updates.

article.articleHeadline: بلا لقاحٍ معتمد.. منظمة الصحة العالمية: تفشّي إيبولا في
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Without an approved vaccine... WHO: Ebola outbreak in
article.articleSummary: Outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) per WHO, as confirmed by Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus. Governments and partners are urged to intensify efforts and resources to protect communities in the coming months, with updated recommendations due soon. The Ebola outbreak was declared on May 15 in eastern Ituri Province; health authorities report 246 suspected cases and 65 deaths. The Bundibugyo strain currently has no approved treatment or vaccine. Ebola is a viral hemorrhagic fever first identified in 1976 near the Ebola River. The 2014–2017 West Africa outbreak infected roughly 30,000 people and caused more than 11,000 deaths.

article.articleHeadline: Brote de ébola en el Congo: lo que debes saber
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Congo: What you need to know.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths, making it the largest Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak and the deadliest in Congo’s history. The virus is a rare Ebola species with no approved vaccine or antiviral; patient care is primarily supportive. WHO warns the outbreak could eventually exceed the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic. Most cases are in Ituri province, centered on Bunia (the provincial capital) and Mongbwalu nearby; the first patient developed symptoms in late April and died in Bunia, with the outbreak declared on May 15. Transmission occurs through contact with blood or body fluids; it is not airborne. The outbreak has spread beyond Ituri into other provinces, crossed the border into Uganda (transmission halted) and produced a confirmed imported case in France in June. Case fatality is about 47.4% overall, higher (around 70%) in North Kivu. Six provinces are affected.

article.articleHeadline: Município reforça vigilância contra arboviroses
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Municipality Strengthens Arboviral Surveillance.
article.articleSummary: El Niño forecast this year could intensify arboviruses such as dengue, Zika, and chikungunya in the municipality. The Health Ministry issued an alert to reinforce surveillance and preventive actions, including intensified house-to-house visits. The Municipal Health Secretariat’s Endemias Coordination maintains continuous monitoring with a real-time ovitrap system, shifting from biweekly to weekly infestation indices to target high-risk areas. Heat maps guide interventions as temperatures rise. Three strategies—focal larviciding in standing water, perifocal adult mosquito control near breeding sites, and insecticide spraying by backpacks and vehicle fogging in critical zones—are in place. In the 31st Epidemiological Week (2–8 Aug), 15 suspected dengue and 1 suspected chikungunya were reported; no Zika cases. Alto da Boa Vista and adjacent neighborhoods including Brasil, Espírito Santo, Felícia, Jardim Guanabara have dengue cases under investigation. Community participation is urged to remove standing water and seek care for fever and related symptoms.

article.articleHeadline: Meningite meningocócica: entenda a doença e saiba como prevenir
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Meningococcal meningitis: understand the disease and learn how to prevent it.
article.articleSummary: Meningococcal meningitis, caused by Neisseria meningitidis, is a severe, rapidly evolving infection in Brazil and globally. Early symptoms within eight hours: headache, fever, sore throat, runny nose, irritability, nausea, vomiting, and drowsiness; by 9–15 hours: skin rashes, cold extremities, photophobia, neck stiffness; 16–24 hours: seizures, confusion, possible death. Mortality in Brazil is 20–30%, higher in children under five and the elderly; survivors may have permanent impairments. Six serogroups exist: A, B, C, W, X, Y; vaccines for A, C, W, Y exist. Brazil’s National Immunization Program provides meningococcal C at 3 and 5 months, with ACWY boosters at 12 months and 11–14 years. Since 2010, MenC vaccination reduced cases by >80% (to about 3,000/year). In 2025, serogroup B caused 69% of notifications in children under 1; MenB is available only in the private sector, while doctors urge broader MenB and ACWY vaccination.

article.articleHeadline: Marataízes emite alerta após aumento de casos de catapora
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Marataízes issues an alert after an increase in chickenpox cases.
article.articleSummary: Varicella (chickenpox) outbreak alert in Marataízes, Espírito Santo, Brazil, as of 19 August 2026. The municipality reports 55 confirmed varicella cases from 1 July to 15 August, affecting students across 13 basic education units. Epidemiological Surveillance is monitoring; authorities urge vaccination up to date, avoiding contact with suspected or confirmed cases, and seeking medical care for symptoms. Varicella-zoster virus causes fever, fatigue, loss of appetite, and red skin lesions that progress to itchy blisters before crusting. Transmission occurs via respiratory droplets (coughs/sneezes) and direct contact with blister fluid. The situation is continuously followed, with emphasis on community vaccination and isolation when symptomatic.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Outbreak, DRC and Region, Situation Report #12 (August 19, 2026)
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) continues, caused by the Bundibugyo strain. As of August 18, the DRC reports 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths; Uganda has 20 confirmed cases and 2 deaths, with the last confirmed Ugandan case discharged on July 16. The outbreak centers in Ituri province, with spread to Bas-Uele, Haut-Uele, North Kivu, South Kivu and Tshopo. No confirmed cases in South Sudan, but risk remains high due to porous borders. International Medical Corps coordinates a regional response with a hub-and-spoke model: 162 facilities conducting screening and treatment; 376,857 screenings; 1,374 patients treated, including 377 confirmed cases. Training includes 2,820 personnel in EVD management. The response operates three Ebola Treatment Centers (one the country’s largest) and seven transit centers, plus IPC, WASH, MHPSS, RCCE, surveillance, and MoH coordination; Uganda preparedness through Ntoroko and Bundibugyo districts.

article.articleHeadline: ஈரோட்டில் 3 பேருக்கு டெங்கு காய்ச்சல் பாதிப்பு
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Three people in Erode affected by dengue fever.
article.articleSummary: Three people in the Erode Municipal Corporation area are affected by dengue fever as of 19 August 2026. Health authorities are taking preventive measures, with public health workers going door-to-door to raise awareness. Residents are urged to keep water storage containers clean and to discard unused items to prevent mosquito breeding and to avoid stagnation of rainwater. The story highlights community outreach and sanitation as key strategies to curb dengue transmission in Erode, focusing on elimination of mosquito habitats rather than clinical treatment details or laboratory-confirmed case information. No additional case counts or fatalities are stated. Public health measures aim to disrupt dengue transmission through community action and environmental management.

article.articleHeadline: Pesquisa da USP desenvolve 'vacina inteligente' contra a chikungunya; entenda
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: USP research develops 'smart vaccine' against Chikungunya; understand.
article.articleSummary: Chikungunya vaccine research at the University of São Paulo (USP), in collaboration with German partners, developed a genetically engineered 'smart vaccine' against chikungunya. In mice, the single-dose formulation achieved protective responses, highlighting potential safety improvements over existing vaccines. Brazil’s licensed chikungunya vaccine is an attenuated preparation indicated for ages 18–59 without comorbidities; the team aimed to merge benefits of attenuated and inactivated approaches. The strategy modifies the chikungunya virus so that, after entry into a cell and initial protein production, the maturation/ replication process is halted, leaving only viral proteins to stimulate the immune system. This engineered virus remains non-infectious while eliciting antibodies against chikungunya. Researchers suggest the same maturation-blocking approach could be applied to other viruses with similar life cycles, including Zika, dengue, yellow fever, and SARS-CoV, enabling broader vaccine development.

article.articleHeadline: Día Mundial del Mosquito 2026: el insecto que causa más de un millón de muertes al año
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Mosquito Day 2026: The Insect That Causes More Than a Million Deaths Per Year
article.articleSummary: World Mosquito Day 2026 highlights mosquitoes as the planet's deadliest animal, responsible for more than one million deaths annually from malaria and other vector-borne diseases such as dengue, Zika, yellow fever, and chikungunya. Sir Ronald Ross’s India-based work established that female mosquitoes transmit malaria, revolutionizing epidemiology and control. The article notes that climate warming accelerates mosquito development; when temperatures exceed 30°C, the life cycle can complete in six days, enabling rapid expansion, including the European spread of Aedes albopictus. Preventive measures emphasized include eliminating standing water, using mosquito nets, applying repellents, installing screens, and keeping patios clean. In tropical zones, surveillance and vector-control programs are essential. The piece also underscores ongoing research into genetic and biological control methods and the urgency of climate actions to curb global transmission.

This preventive activity highlights local health authorities’ proactive dengue surveillance in the village, with the team comprising the district health official and two other officials coordinating the examination of residents for dengue-related symptoms.

article.articleHeadline: Ébola en Congo supera los 5 mil casos; es el brote más letal de su historia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpasses 5,000 cases; it is the deadliest outbreak in its history.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (eastern regions) has reached 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths as of August 19, 2026, per Africa CDC. Declared May 15, 2026, it is the deadliest outbreak in the DRC’s history, surpassing the 2018–2020 eastern outbreak (2,299 deaths, 3,381 cases). The Bundibugyo strain drives the epidemic, for which no licensed vaccine or approved treatment exists; clinical trials are underway. Transmission occurs mainly through contact with bodily fluids, underscoring the need for rapid case finding and isolation. Response is hampered by limited healthcare infrastructure, weak state presence in some areas, community distrust, insecurity, and protests by responders. International support is increasing; the European Union has allocated €2.5 million for diagnostic tests to strengthen diagnostics. Authorities warn the virus could spread beyond current zones; the article provides no details on imported/exported cases.

article.articleHeadline: Carapebus marcha contra a tuberculose e pela prevenção | Carapebus | O Dia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Carapebus marches against tuberculosis and for prevention | Carapebus | O Dia
article.articleSummary: Tuberculosis awareness and prevention efforts were launched in Carapebus, Rio de Janeiro State, Brazil, by the Municipal Health Secretariat (Semsa). To mark the State Day Against Tuberculosis, residents, health professionals, Senior Program groups and a Rehabilitation Center participated in a march and received updates on diagnosis and clinical management across the municipal network. The campaign highlights that tuberculosis is an infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, mainly affecting the lungs (pulmonary form) but potentially involving other organs (extrapulmonary), with extrapulmonary TB more common among people living with HIV/AIDS. Diagnosis and complete treatment are provided free through the Unified Health System (SUS), including Directly Observed Therapy (DOT) and nutrition support to aid adherence. A cough lasting three weeks or more should prompt medical evaluation. Mayor Bernard Tavares and Health Secretary Marcelo Queiroz emphasized community solidarity and proactive care to interrupt transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Wabah Mematikan Tembus 5.000 Kasus: Tak Terkendali-Belum Ada Obatnya
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Deadly outbreak surpasses 5,000 cases: Out of control—no cure yet.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 confirmed cases, with 2,378 deaths, as of August 19, 2026. Government data show 5,021 total infections, making this the largest Ebola outbreak in the country since late July and the second-worst globally after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic. The crisis is driven by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, and, per the report, there is no approved vaccine or treatment to curtail it. The outbreak began with declarations on May 15 and has since intensified, hampered by weak health infrastructure, community resistance, regional instability, and protests by healthcare workers. Health authorities warn that current response efforts have failed to contain the disease, signaling an ongoing and severe public health emergency in the DRC.

article.articleHeadline: Em um mês, Maringá registra apenas duas confirmações de dengue
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In one month, Maringá records only two confirmed dengue cases.
article.articleSummary: As of 19 August 2026, dengue in Maringá, Brazil, has fallen sharply. In the last three months, 31 cases; since January, 175 occurrences. This represents an 81.6% decrease from the same period in the previous year (4,134) and a 99.2% drop versus 2024 (22,531). The decline follows prevention efforts launched in 2025, notably 2,383 intelligent Larvicidal Dissemination Stations (EDLs) and about 1,200 ovitraps citywide, plus Indoor Residual Spraying (IRS) in high-traffic sites (health units, schools, cemeteries). Biweekly inspections, drone monitoring, school health campaigns, and training for Community Health Agents and Endemic Combat Agents accompany ongoing surveillance. Health Secretary Antônio Carlos Nardi credits these investments in traps and spraying, plus resident efforts to remove standing water, with reducing transmission and calls for continued community participation to sustain gains.

article.articleHeadline: Каким странам угрожают малярийные комары?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Which countries are threatened by malaria-carrying mosquitoes?
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-19, Anopheles stephensi, a malaria-carrying mosquito native to South Asia, has expanded into Africa, first arriving via Eritrea and rapidly spreading to Ethiopia, Sudan, Somalia and Nigeria, with detections now in Ghana and Kenya. The spread threatens malaria control, placing more than 126 million people at risk. Unlike many local species, A. stephensi tolerates urban environments and breeds in artificial water containers, water tanks, construction debris, and discarded tires, allowing efficient transmission in crowded cities. It also shows high levels of resistance to many insecticides, complicating control efforts. WHO recommends a comprehensive, integrated vector management approach, including insecticide-treated nets and repellents for people, and elimination of standing water and other breeding sites. The situation highlights the urgent need for surveillance, vector control adaptation, and international cooperation to curb urban malaria expansion.

article.articleHeadline: Prevenção da dengue em Itajaí avança com Método Wolbachia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue prevention in Itajaí advances with the Wolbachia Method.
article.articleSummary: 9,100 pots received to prepare the Wolbachia Method in Itajaí, Brazil, with releases of Wolbachia-carrying Aedes aegypti (wolbitos) expected by year-end 2026 to curb dengue, Zika, and chikungunya transmission. The program targets Cidade Nova, São Vicente, Cordeiros, and São João, encompassing about 130,000 residents. Wolbachia-infected mosquitoes disrupt virus development, reducing arboviruses as they spread through local populations. The initiative aligns with the schedule set by the Ministry of Health and aims for a self-sustaining Wolbachia-infected mosquito population to decrease disease circulation. A municipal health team will visit Joinville’s Wolbachia Reproduction Core to study production and maintenance processes to establish a local nucleus in Itajaí, covering infrastructure, workflows, and materials, informing the local setup.

article.articleHeadline: Redefining the end of Uganda's Ebola virus crisis
article.articleSummary: On July 28, 2026, the Bundibugyo virus outbreak in Uganda was declared ended, defined by WHO as 42 consecutive days after the last patient’s second negative PCR or safe burial. The article cautions that official end points are epidemiological and may mask true epidemic resolution, especially in resource-poor settings with underdiagnosis and weak surveillance. It notes Bunia in eastern DRC as the outbreak epicenter linked to transmission into Uganda, where discharged patients virologically cured can suffer post-acute complications, including acute kidney injury requiring dialysis, and some die after discharge. Virological clearance does not equal recovery; post-Ebola syndrome includes ocular, neurological, renal, musculoskeletal, and psychological sequelae, with viral persistence in immune-privileged sites raising delayed sexual transmission risk. The authors propose a four-stage recovery: epidemiological end, clinical end, health-system end, footprint end, and urge distinguishing transmission end from epidemic recovery.

article.articleHeadline: Brote de ébola en el Congo es el segundo peor de la historia: van más de 5 mil contagios
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in Congo is the second-worst in history: more than 5,000 cases.
article.articleSummary: DR Congo reports 5,105 confirmed Ebola cases and 2,420 deaths, making this outbreak the second-worst globally and the deadliest in the country, with a case fatality rate of 47.4%. As of the latest update, 782 patients remain in isolation or hospitalized and 1,091 have recovered; contact tracing is at 84.1%. The outbreak is the fastest-growing since its declaration. The World Health Organization leader warned it could reach the scale of the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak, which caused about 11,000 deaths and 28,000 infections. Transmission affects six provinces: Ituri (epicenter), North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, Tshopo, and Bas-Uele. Uganda declared the end of its Ebola outbreak on July 28, after 20 cases and 2 deaths.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola surpasses 5,000 cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and the World Health Organization keeps the outbreak as an international emergency.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 confirmed cases, with 5,021 cases and 2,378 deaths reported by the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, marking the largest outbreak in the country’s history. The World Health Organization maintains the event as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC), warning of ongoing local and international risk and urging intensified response and resource mobilization. The outbreak, first declared in May, affects northern and eastern areas where weak health infrastructure hinders containment. Access to some regions remains difficult, and some residents resist undergoing tests. Authorities and partners are urged to accelerate case finding, testing, and infection-control activities to curb transmission and prevent cross-border spread.

article.articleHeadline: मच्छर से होने वाली बीमारियों के खिलाफ गुजरात का असरदार काम, मलेरिया में 45 तो डेंगू में 39 प्रतिशत की कमी
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Gujarat's effective efforts against mosquito-borne diseases: 45% reduction in malaria and 39% in dengue.
article.articleSummary: Gujarat, India reports dramatic reductions in mosquito-borne diseases as of week 33, 2026, under an expanded public-health program. Malaria cases fell 45.0% (1,407→774); dengue 39.1% (1,293→788); chikungunya 48.1% (154→80). No malaria or dengue deaths in this period. Testing rose: week-33 2026 saw 111 lakh blood samples tested, with dengue and chikungunya serology across 42 diagnostic centers totaling about 96,000 samples (83,000 dengue; 12,000 chikungunya). Phase 1 home-surveillance (Apr 27–May 6) achieved 89% coverage; Phase 2 (Jul 1–10) mobilized 19,558 teams to cover over 65 million people, collecting 257,000 blood samples and detecting 28 malaria cases. Approximately 2.96 million breeding sites removed and 321,000 houses fogged. In 24 districts, 116 malaria-prone villages received first-round insecticide spray; second round starts Aug 1. Monsoon operations involved 497 vector-control teams, 5,024 larvivorous-fish releases, and steady stockpiling and monitoring of drugs and equipment.

triage.headline_ja: 蚊媒介性疾患に対するグジャラート州の効果的な取り組み：マラリアが45%、デング熱が39%減少
triage.triage_reason: 感染症の減少・公衆衛生対策の成功を報じる内容であり、異常な公衆衛生イベントや国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 記事はグジャラート州における蚊媒介性疾患（マラリア・デング熱・チクングニア熱）の減少と対策の成功を報告する内容で、リスク増大を示す情報はない。

article.articleHeadline: Vì sao đợt bùng phát Ebola tại Congo lan nhanh, gây tử vong cao?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Why is the Ebola outbreak in Congo spreading rapidly and causing high mortality?
article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is the deadliest there and the second deadliest worldwide, with 2,325 deaths and a spread five times faster than prior Congo outbreaks. It is driven by a rare Bundibugroyo (Bundibugyo) strain; early cases were missed or misdiagnosed, and some experimental vaccines and therapies are under evaluation. The outbreak likely began in January but was not announced until May, and WHO notes about 80% of new cases occur outside identified transmission chains, signaling late detection. Mortality rose from about 20% by end-June to 47%. Funding shortages hamper response: July salaries unpaid, USAID surveillance suspended since 2025, WHO funding under half of needs by mid-July. Conflict in eastern Congo hinders access, contact tracing, and supply lines; distrust and misinformation are barriers; displacement to camps has Ebola deaths. There is no licensed vaccine or proven therapy for Bundibugyo; most vaccines target Zaire.

triage.headline_ja: なぜコンゴのエボラ流行は急速に拡大し、高い死亡率をもたらしているのか？
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最悪規模（死亡者2,325人、致死率47%）のエボラ流行が急速拡大しており、資金不足・治安悪化により対応が困難な状況で、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 希少なブンディブギョ株による流行で、既存ワクチン（主にザイール株対象）や治療法が未確立。USAIDの監視支援停止やWHO資金不足、東部コンゴでの武力衝突が対応を著しく阻害している。80%の新規感染が既知の感染経路外で発生しており、検知の遅れも深刻。

article.articleHeadline: Delhi govt on alert over lumpy skin disease among livestock - The Tribune
article.articleSummary: Delhi government is on alert over lumpy skin disease (LSD) among livestock in the capital. So far this year, only sporadic symptomatic cases have been reported. Development Minister Kapil Mishra, after reviewing the situation with the Development Commissioner and Director of Animal Husbandry, stated that the Animal Husbandry Unit is closely monitoring LSD across Delhi and coordinating preventive and control measures per guidelines issued by the Union Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying. A vaccination campaign is underway, with adequate stocks of LSD vaccine available at veterinary hospitals and dispensaries to ensure timely immunization of livestock. Owners are urged to vaccinate their animals, monitor for symptoms, and contact the nearest government veterinary hospital or dispensary if infection is suspected. Suspected cases should be isolated from others, and owners should consult a qualified veterinary professional promptly. The government will continue surveillance and take all necessary measures to prevent spread.

triage.headline_ja: デリー政府、家畜のランピースキン病流行に警戒
triage.triage_reason: 家畜のランピースキン病（LSD）は人獣共通感染症ではなく、デリーでは散発的な症例のみで、既にワクチン接種と監視体制により管理下にあるため、公衆衛生上の懸念は低い。
triage.notes: LSDは牛などの家畜に感染するウイルス性疾患であり、ヒトには感染しない。記事は行政の予防的モニタリングとワクチン接種キャンペーンの実施を報じる内容で、散発的症例に対する通常の管理対応であり、危機的状況ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Cases In Congo Exceed 5,000, Government Data Shows
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has reached unprecedented levels in its 17th outbreak. As of Aug 20, 2026, government data show confirmed Ebola cases exceeding 5,000, with the death toll at 2,378, making it the largest outbreak in the country’s history by case count and surpassing the 2018-2020 crisis. Health officials warn that response efforts are failing to contain the disease. The report, from Kinshasa, highlights ongoing challenges in a protracted epidemic. The article provides no details on symptoms, laboratory confirmation, infection source, or imported/exported cases. The trajectory to-date indicates a continuing escalation beyond the 5,000-case threshold, emphasizing the severity and persistence of the outbreak in the DRC.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ感染者数、5,000人を超える―政府データが示す
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大規模のエボラ流行（5,000例超、死亡2,378人）が継続的に拡大しており、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクが認められるためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: 記事は症状・感染源・検査確定・輸出入例に関する詳細を提供していないが、史上最大規模の流行として公表されており、既存の対応努力が抑制に失敗していると報告されている。

article.articleHeadline: "أيبولا" يتعدى حدود الكونغو.. وتحذير أممي يدق ناقوس الخطر
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola crosses Congo's borders... UN warning sounds the alarm.
article.articleSummary: By 19 August 2026, Ebola outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of Congo have surpassed 5,000 confirmed infections, with health authorities warning containment efforts have not yet succeeded. WHO officials warn the virus is spreading in the DRC faster than any previous outbreak, signaling a heightened risk of cross-border transmission to neighboring countries. In an emergency meeting, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus stated the epidemic is far from under control. The WHO Emergency Committee declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, reflecting international concern. The report notes cross-border risk but provides no details on specific imported or exported cases. The coverage underscores the urgent need for intensified, coordinated international response to curb the outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: 「エボラ」がコンゴの国境を越える…国連の警告が危険を告げる
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ感染者が5000人を超え、WHOがPHEIC（国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態）を宣言しており、IHR基準の複数該当が確認されるため。
triage.notes: 記事は越境リスクに言及しているが、具体的な輸入・輸出感染例の詳細はない。WHOはPHEICを宣言し、過去最速の拡大速度と警告している。

article.articleHeadline: Detectan en Hiroshima un caso de cólera en viajero procedente de Bangladesh
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Cholera case detected in Hiroshima in a traveler from Bangladesh.
article.articleSummary: Cholera case detected in Fukuyama, Hiroshima Prefecture, Japan, in a foreign man in his twenties who recently arrived from Bangladesh. He entered Japan on August 7, developed diarrhea and abdominal pain, and sought care on August 12; laboratory tests confirmed cholera. Authorities believe the infection was acquired in Bangladesh before arrival. The patient is hospitalized and progressing well. The case underscores ongoing vigilance for imported infections in Japan, with Fukuyama previously reporting three cholera cases in travelers from Myanmar last year, maintaining surveillance for travel-associated cases. Cholera is an acute infectious disease transmitted mainly via contaminated water or food and can cause dehydration, but early diagnosis and proper treatment commonly yield favorable outcomes.

triage.headline_ja: 広島でバングラデシュからの渡航者にコレラ症例を検出
triage.triage_reason: 日本国内で確認された輸入例1件であり、対象国（バングラデシュ・日本とも対象国リスト外）における流行事象ではなく、患者も回復傾向にあるため見送りと判断。
triage.notes: 感染地はバングラデシュとされるが同国は対象国リストに含まれず、検出国の日本も対象国リスト外。ミャンマーは前年の別事例として言及されているのみで、本件の発生地ではないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Ação contra a dengue identifica 35 criadouros na região do Ouro Verde em Limeira - Portal Veloz
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Action Against Dengue Identifies 35 Breeding Sites in the Ouro Verde Region of Limeira - Portal Veloz
article.articleSummary: Dengue control mutirão in Limeira, Brazil identified 35 Aedes aegypti breeding sites in the Ouro Verde region, covering Jardim Ouro Verde, Jardim Nova Europa, and Jardim Residencial Alto da Graminha. On Saturday the 15th, 94 agents inspected 1,427 properties; 1,040 were closed at the time. Of the breeding sites, 31 contained water and one had larvae, signaling active mosquito habitats requiring intervention. The operation aims to eliminate potential vector breeding and educate residents on preventing dengue transmission. Authorities urge households to keep yards and outdoor areas free of containers that collect water. This effort supports ongoing arbovirus prevention and control in the municipality and aligns with SDG 3 on health and well-being.

triage.headline_ja: リメイラのオウロ・ヴェルデ地区でデング熱対策活動により35カ所の蚊発生源を特定 - Portal Veloz
triage.triage_reason: デング熱の日常的な媒介蚊駆除活動の報告であり、症例数や異常な流行拡大の情報はなく、通常の公衆衛生対策の一環と判断される。
triage.notes: 記事はブラジル・リメイラ市における通常のデング熱媒介蚊(Aedes aegypti)発生源調査・駆除活動を報じたものであり、症例数増加や異常な流行状況についての記載はない。ブラジルは対象国リストに含まれるが、内容が定例的な防疫活動であるためDISMISSと判断。

article.articleHeadline: Aulas são suspensas após casos de catapora em escola de João Pessoa
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Classes are suspended after cases of chickenpox at a school in João Pessoa.
article.articleSummary: Nine suspected cases of chickenpox (varicella) were identified among students at Escola Estadual Desembargador Boto de Menezes in the 13 de Maio neighborhood of João Pessoa, Paraíba, prompting temporary class suspension as a preventive measure. A coordination meeting between the school and the Executive Management of Integrated Schools on 19 August 2026 defined initial control actions to curb transmission. Varicella is highly contagious and commonly causes fever and skin lesions. Vaccination is the principal prevention, with immunization available through Brazil’s Unified Health System (SUS) according to the National Immunization Program (PNI) criteria. The report does not detail laboratory confirmation, specific exposure sources, or imported/exported cases.

triage.headline_ja: パラ​イーバ州ジョアン・ペソアの学校で水痘症例発生のため休校
triage.triage_reason: 水痘は一般的で重症度が低い疾患であり、学校内での集団発生に留まるが、ヒト-ヒト感染の可能性があるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 水痘（varicella）は感染力が強いが一般的に軽症であり、学校内の集団発生として地域保健当局が対応中。国際的拡大や重大な公衆衛生上の脅威は認められない。

article.articleHeadline: Mosquito Cases Increase | राज्यात डासांचा डंख 'डेंजरस'; ४ वर्षांत रुग्ण ६५ टक्क्यांनी वाढले!
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mosquito Cases Are Increasing | In the state, the mosquito sting is 'Dangerous'; patients have risen by 65 percent in four years!
article.articleSummary: Kolhapur, Maharashtra—A mosquito-borne disease surge is described as dangerous, with dengue, malaria, and chikungunya cases rising 65% over four years and total cases nearing 150,000. The monsoon season has heightened mosquito activity across the state. Combined case counts were 25,116 in 2022, rising to 41,433 by 2025. Patients typically present with fever and headache, often incurring substantial hospital bills. The report highlights the growing burden of these three vector-borne diseases and the financial impact on families during the rainy season. While the data emphasize Maharashtra’s increasing exposure to dengue, malaria, and chikungunya, Kolhapur is singled out as part of the state’s broader seasonal transmission risk.

triage.headline_ja: 蚊媒介性疾患が増加中 | 州内で蚊の刺咬が「危険」に；4年間で患者数が65%増加！
triage.triage_reason: マハーラーシュトラ州における季節性の蚊媒介性疾患（デング熱・マラリア・チクングニア）の増加を報じているが、モンスーン期の通常の季節的増加傾向であり、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは低い。継続的な曝露リスクはあるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 季節性（モンスーン期）の蚊媒介性疾患増加に関する地域報道。4年間で65%増加という統計は懸念材料だが、重症度・死亡例の詳細な記載はなく、国際的な公衆衛生上の緊急性を示す情報はない。

article.articleHeadline: Cần Thơ: Khởi tố hàng loạt đối tượng mua bán thịt lợn nhiễm dịch tả lợn Châu Phi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Can Tho: Prosecution of a number of suspects in the sale of pork infected with African swine fever.
article.articleSummary: Can Tho City, Vietnam reports prosecutions over selling pork infected with African swine fever (ASF). Suspects Trương Văn Công (1984) and Hứa Hoàng Khởi (1984) are indicted for food safety violations and prohibited from leaving their residence; they allegedly conspired with Thị Hồng Cam (1995) to buy diseased or dead pigs, have them slaughtered, and sell the meat. At the Đặng Phú Tỷ slaughterhouse in Vĩnh Viễn Commune, 9 Oct 2025 inspection found 40 live pigs and one slaughtered pig with ASF-positive meat. Two pork lots totaling 840.7 kg from Vĩnh Viễn market yielded 10 of 12 samples ASF-positive. On 10 Nov 2025, three employees from Trạm Chăn nuôi-Thú y khu vực XIII—Phan Ngọc Toại (1977), Lê Quốc Nhiên (1979), Phạm Hồng Phúc (1980)—were charged with abusing public duties. On 12 Feb 2026, Lưu Văn Nam (1981) and Thị Hồng Cam were additionally charged with food safety violations; investigation ongoing.

triage.headline_ja: カントー市:アフリカ豚熱感染豚肉の売買を行った複数の被疑者を起訴
triage.triage_reason: アフリカ豚熱（ASF）は豚のみに感染するウイルス性疾患でヒトへの感染性がなく、本記事は食品安全法違反に関する司法手続き（起訴）を報じるものであり、新規の公衆衛生上の脅威やアウトブレイクを示すものではない。
triage.notes: ASFはヒトに感染しない動物疾病であり、本件は食品安全・法執行に関する報道。公衆衛生上のリスク評価対象としての優先度は低い。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola-epidemie in Congo wordt de dodelijkste ooit en nepnieuws maakt het nog erger
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola epidemic in the Congo is the deadliest ever, and misinformation makes it worse.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), centered on the Bundibugyo variant, has persisted since May. There is no vaccine for Bundibugyo and no effective antiviral; care is supportive, addressing fever, headache, muscle pains, vomiting, diarrhea and bleeding. The World Health Organization warns it could become the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak to date, surpassing the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic of about 11,323 deaths. Misinformation and fear, including claims that white people created Ebola or that vaccines contain coronavirus, hinder response. The Balobaki fact-check collective works with local radio to inform community leaders in the hardest-hit areas. Transmission is via direct contact with bodily fluids, not airborne; many infections occur during funerals due to traditional washing and touching of the deceased. Attacks on ambulances in Bunia illustrate hostility toward responders. AI-generated misinformation on TikTok, X and Facebook worsens the problem.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行は史上最悪となりつつあり、偽情報がさらに悪化させている
triage.triage_reason: WHOが史上最大・最悪のエボラ流行になり得ると警告しており、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と管理の困難さ（偽情報による対応妨害）から、フルリスク評価に進むべきシグナルと判断される。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれているが、記事本文ではDRC（特にBunia周辺）のみが発生地として言及されており、Angolaへの拡大は記載されていないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: 小心感染性腹泻的"头号"病原菌！它是这样"入侵"人体的→
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Beware the #1 pathogen causing infectious diarrhea! This is how it invades the human body.
article.articleSummary: Salmonella infection (salmonellosis) is the leading bacterial cause of infectious diarrhea worldwide. Global burden: about 115 million illnesses and 370,000 deaths annually, with roughly 95 million gastroenteritis cases and over 50,000 deaths. In China, about 90 million people are infected each year, with incidence near 1,300 per 100,000 in several provinces; among children under five, Salmonella is the third leading cause of death from diarrheal diseases. Transmission occurs through contaminated foods (poultry, pork, beef, dairy, eggs), contaminated water, contact with animals, and cross-contamination during food handling; transmission is year-round with peaks in summer and autumn. Symptoms typically appear 6–72 hours after exposure and last 4–7 days, including diarrhea, abdominal cramps, nausea/vomiting, and fever around 38–39°C. Prevention emphasizes thorough cooking, avoiding raw/undercooked foods, handwashing, preventing cross-contamination, and proper refrigeration.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola cases in DR Congo top 5,000 - Africa health agency
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-20, DR Congo's 17th Ebola outbreak declared May 15 has surpassed 5,000 cases, with 5,021 confirmed and 2,378 deaths, according to Africa CDC data. The Bundibugyo virus drives the surge; there is no approved vaccine or specific treatment, though clinical trials are underway. The hardest-hit areas are in the north and east, where weak state presence, poor health infrastructure, and armed groups hinder response. WHO Director-General Tedros warned the epidemic is far from under control and the risk of further national and international spread remains high. Criticism has focused on slow, disorganized responses and mistrust, including refusals of testing. In response, WHO efforts to scale up activities and reach communities are under way, and the European Union is sending testing kits worth 2.5 million euros to aid containment.

triage.headline_ja: DRコンゴのエボラ感染者数が5,000人を超える－アフリカ保健機関
triage.triage_reason: DRコンゴで大規模なエボラ流行（5,000人超、致死率約47%）が継続し、WHOも国際的拡大リスクを警告しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき事案。
triage.notes: 承認済みワクチン・特効薬がなく、治安不安地域での対応が困難な状況。WHOおよびEUが支援拡大中で、国際的な関心・支援ニーズが高い。

article.articleHeadline: Hà Nội tăng cường công tác phòng, chống dịch bệnh sốt xuất huyết
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Hanoi strengthens dengue fever prevention and control efforts.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever prevention and control are being strengthened in Hanoi. The city’s People’s Committee issued Document 4247/UBND-KGVX directing intensified surveillance and rapid response, especially in wards and communes with complex or long-running outbreaks. The Department of Health will monitor the situation, assess risk, and guide measures to prevent transmission; hospitals will triage, admit, treat, and transfer patients promptly to minimize complications and deaths, and ensure adequate supplies, including medicines, intravenous fluids, blood and blood products. Training on surveillance, diagnosis, and standardized treatment will be expanded, with strengthened inter-hospital consultations for severe cases. Inspections will target outbreak areas to resolve obstacles and eradicate transmission. The Culture, Sports and Tourism Department, with media, will disseminate timely, accurate information and promote vector control and environmental sanitation campaigns. The Education sector will supervise weekly campus cleanups and mosquito control; ward/commune chairs carry responsibility under a 4-at-site principle and a citywide dengue prevention month.

triage.headline_ja: ハノイ、デング熱の予防・対策を強化
triage.triage_reason: ベトナム・ハノイで例年発生する季節性のデング熱に対する行政の予防強化通知であり、異常な増加や重症化を示す具体的データはなく、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクも認められない。
triage.notes: デング熱はベトナムで毎年流行する既知の媒介動物感染症であり、本記事は行政による通常の予防・監視強化策の発表に留まる。具体的な患者数や重症例の急増データが示されていないため、シグナルとしての優先度は低い。

article.articleHeadline: Ituri : 4,6 millions de dollars pour le paludisme, débloqués pour accélérer le tri des cas suspects d'Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ituri: $4.6 million for malaria, released to speed up triage of suspected Ebola cases.
article.articleSummary: In Ituri province, DRC, on Aug 14 the National Public Health Institute launched mass antimalarial drug distribution across Bunia, Nyankunde, Mongbwalu, and Rwampara, covering over one million people in four days to support Ebola triage. The Global Fund approved $4.6 million in emergency funding for two phases: initial mass drug administration, followed by a second phase with more than 500,000 bed nets and about 400,000 spatial repellents to reduce malaria fever and aid differentiation of suspected Ebola cases. SANRU maintains 903 community malaria sites across 36 health zones. WHO notes that distinguishing Bundibugyo ebolavirus disease from malaria requires laboratory confirmation. UNICEF DHIS2 data (Apr–Jun 2026) show essential health services down 42% in four outbreak foci and 12.6% province-wide; measles vaccination in Mongbwalu down 69%; and 239 malaria cases per 1,000 people in 2023, with 33 malaria deaths per 100,000.

triage.headline_ja: イツリ州:エボラ疑い例のトリアージ加速のためマラリア対策に460万ドルを投入
triage.triage_reason: DRCイツリ州でエボラ（ブンディブギョ・エボラウイルス病）疑い例のトリアージを支援するための大規模マラリア対策が実施され、国際基金からの緊急資金投入とWHO・UNICEFの関与が確認されており、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響と国際的関心が認められる。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCイツリ州でのエボラ疑い例トリアージ支援のためのマラリア対策強化を主題としている。ルワンダ（Kigali Province）は発生地域として付与されているが、記事本文ではDRC国内の対応のみが述べられており、対象国リストにも含まれないため除外。国際的拡大リスクや渡航制限に関する情報は記事内に明記されていないため不明とした。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : 21 rings de décontamination ouverts sur 171 attendus en Ituri, 74 cas suspects non investigués sur les provinces rapportantes
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: 21 decontamination rings opened out of 171 expected in Ituri, 74 suspected cases not investigated in the reporting provinces
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo remains severe as of 15 August: 4,945 confirmed cases and 2,325 deaths (case fatality 47.0%), across six provinces and 55 health zones. Ituri bears the majority with 4,194 confirmed cases (84.8% of total) and 1,838 deaths, 1,040 recoveries, and 730 in isolation. In Ituri, 171 decontamination rings were expected; 21 opened due to staffing gaps in Bambu-mine and Mangala, supply shortages in Mandima, resistance from families in Kilo, untraceable addresses, and decontaminator strikes. Surveillance logged 1,730 alerts, with 1,575 verified; 380 suspected; 306 investigated; 263 transferred to treatment centers. Tshopo did not report. Contact tracing reached 85.3% (20,791/24,383). Burial operations show 39 death alerts, 37 swabs and burials, with community resistance in Beni and Kalunguta. Entry-screening refusals: 2,187 (2.78%). Ambulance capacity strained; multiple treatment centers saturated in Ituri and Nord-Kivu. Infodemic and fear drive self-medication among displaced communities.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：イトゥリ州で予定171カ所中21カ所の消毒リングのみ開設、報告州で74件の疑い例が未調査
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国におけるエボラ出血熱の大規模流行が継続し、致死率47%、対応能力の限界（消毒リング未開設、サーベイランス遅延、治療施設の飽和）が報告されており、国際的拡大・公衆衛生上の深刻な影響が認められるためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAustraliaが含まれているが記事内容はDRCのエボラ流行のみを扱っており、対象国リストにも含まれないため除外した。消毒リング未開設、コンタクトトレーシング不完全、治療施設飽和など対応能力の限界が示されており、既存の大規模流行事案として継続的な監視・支援が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Rougeole : 34 913 cas suspects au Sud-Kivu, 66 prélevés
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Measles: 34,913 suspected cases in South Kivu, 66 samples collected.
article.articleSummary: Measles outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo centers on North Kivu and South Kivu. South Kivu reports 34,913 suspected cases since Jan 1 with 540 deaths; 66 samples collected and 24 IgM confirmations. North Kivu records 19,431 suspected cases and 62 deaths; 366 samples collected with 137 IgM confirmations. Nationally, 114,004 suspected cases have been reported with 1,487 deaths and 1,289 IgM confirmations; among confirmed cases, 81% are under five, with 34% vaccinated, 48% unvaccinated, and 18% unknown. Lab turnaround is slow: 52.1% of samples take over 8 days to reach a lab, and in South Kivu none arrive before 7 days. Measles-Rubella vaccination campaign (Block 3) began Aug 10, targeting 24,791,774 children aged 6 months–14 years across eight provinces, including North and South Kivu; vaccination started Aug 11 at 13 sites, with four postponed to Aug 17 due to kit deployment delays. UNICEF-backed funding totals $3.008 million for the campaign and $1 million for routine vaccination. Context: Ebola has 4,945 confirmed cases and 2,325 deaths as of Aug 15; in Oicha (Nord Kivu), 29,458 of 53,201 targeted were vaccinated.

triage.headline_ja: 麻疹：南キブ州で疑い例34,913件、66件の検体採取
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で麻疹の疑い例が全国114,004件、死亡1,487件に達し、5歳未満が81%を占めるなど公衆衛生上深刻な影響がある。ワクチン接種率も低く感染拡大が続いており、国際支援（UNICEF資金）も既に動いているためフルRRAへ進めるべき。
triage.notes: 記事はエボラ出血熱（確定4,945例、死亡2,325例）にも言及しているが、これは既存の流行状況の背景情報として記載されており、本記事の主題は麻疹アウトブレイクである。麻疹・風疹ワクチン接種キャンペーン（第3ブロック）が進行中で、検体の検査室搬送に時間がかかる（52.1%が8日以上）など対応体制の課題も指摘されている。

article.articleHeadline: Charbon bactéridien à Vitshumbi : une alerte sur le lac Édouard, sans vaccination de routine du bétail depuis plus de dix ans selon l'OMS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Bacterial anthrax at Vitshumbi: an alert on Lake Edward, with no routine livestock vaccination for more than ten years according to the WHO.
article.articleSummary: Anthrax alert on Lake Edward at Vitshumbi, Virunga National Park, DRC. A hippopotamus found dead on Aug 8, 2026 tested positive for Bacillus anthracis; alert issued Aug 17 by the Kibirizi health zone. Authorities are tracing handlers and meat consumers; residents urged to report skin lesions or fever. No human cases reported as of Aug 18. WHO Africa notes no routine livestock vaccination against anthrax for more than a decade, increasing vulnerability. Risk factors include handling animals or products, bushmeat consumption, and illegal fishing in Lake Edward; there is no evidence that fish consumption transmits the disease. The outbreak history shows 2025 wildlife deaths in Virunga and 17 human cases (1 confirmed, 1 death; CFR 5.9%), with 24 suspects by May 2025. Ongoing armed conflict and water shortages hinder response; July 2026 cholera cases reported in Lubero health zone.

triage.headline_ja: ヴィチュンビの炭疽病:エドワード湖に警戒、WHOによれば10年以上家畜への定期ワクチン接種なし
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国ヴィルンガ国立公園エドワード湖周辺でカバの炭疽菌感染が確認され、武力衝突・水不足・家畜ワクチン未接種という悪条件が重なり外部支援の必要性が高い。2025年には人での感染・死亡例もあり、継続的な監視が必要。
triage.notes: 現時点で人での感染例は報告されていないが、2025年には17人の疑い例（1件確定・1件死亡）があり、武力衝突や水不足、家畜への定期ワクチン未接種など脆弱性要因が多い。同記事内でルベロ保健区の2026年7月コレラ症例にも言及されているが、疾患名リストにCholeraも含まれるため注記。
